# Free content, Pro, sponsored cards, and model failover: implementation plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking. Every task is fully specified: files, interfaces, the complete RED test, the command and the expected failure, the implementation, the GREEN gate, and the commit.

**Goal:** Every bank free; one Pro tier (annual or lifetime) that removes sponsored cards and raises the Ask limit; sponsored cards in the app's own style on web and mobile; the web app on Cloudflare Pages with static output and crawlable pages; the server's model calls failing over between Anthropic and OpenAI and surviving model retirements.

**Architecture:** The content schema loses `access` and `productId` and all 36 banks live under `content/`, bundled (Easy) or downloaded on first use with hash verification (Medium, Hard). The server keeps the RevenueCat webhook and the `entitlements` table, adds `expires_at`, and derives one `pro` status from two products. The app replaces the per-bank paywall with a `ProSheet`, reads `pro` from `/v1/me`, and renders a `SponsoredCard` fed by AdMob native assets on mobile and by EthicalAds, a direct sponsor, or the house card on the web. The web export becomes static HTML per route, deployed to Cloudflare Pages by `wrangler-action`. The server's `ModelProvider` gains an OpenAI implementation and a failover wrapper with a circuit breaker, with model ids from the environment.

**Tech Stack:** TypeScript; Expo 57 / React Native 0.86 / react-native-web (Jest, `@testing-library/react-native`, `@testing-library/react`, `jest-axe`); Express 5 on Railway with Postgres on Neon (Vitest, node-pg-migrate); `@syntactical/content-schema` (Vitest); `pipeline/` (Vitest); RevenueCat (`react-native-purchases`, `@revenuecat/purchases-js`); `react-native-google-mobile-ads` 17.x with `expo-dev-client`; the EthicalAds client; `cloudflare/wrangler-action@v4`; `@anthropic-ai/sdk` and `openai` 7.x; Playwright e2e.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-27-free-content-pro-sponsored-design.md`. **Audit:** `docs/audits/2026-10-27-monetization-marketing.md`.

## Global Constraints

- Product ids: `syntactical.pro.annual` (auto-renewing, one year, $19.99 US) and `syntactical.pro.lifetime` (non-consumable, $39.99 US). Both match `PRODUCT_ID_PATTERN` in `constants/appConfig.ts`. No monthly product, ever.
- Google Play reports a subscription as `<subscription id>:<base plan id>`. `normalizeProductId` strips a `:<suffix>` matching `/^[a-z0-9.]+:[a-z0-9-]+$/` on the server (Task 3.1) and in the app (Task 4.4) before any Pro id is matched.
- `hasPro`: a `granted` row for either product with `expires_at IS NULL OR expires_at > now`. `expires_at` is NULL for lifetime and for admin grants, and never NULL for the annual: an annual grant event without `expiration_at_ms` is recorded, grants nothing, and logs a warning.
- Webhook: grant on `INITIAL_PURCHASE`, `RENEWAL`, `UNCANCELLATION`, `NON_RENEWING_PURCHASE`; revoke on `EXPIRATION`, `REFUND`; `CANCELLATION` revokes the lifetime product and only writes `expires_at` on the annual; every other type is answered 200 and not stored. Ordering stays by `event_timestamp_ms`, a revoke wins a tie, idempotency stays on `(provider, provider_event_id)`.
- Admin access entry keeps today's shape `{ grantSource: 'admin' | 'purchase' | null; isGranted: boolean; productId: 'syntactical.pro.lifetime' }`; `grantSource` is `'purchase'` when any store purchase of either Pro product is active.
- Ask: `ASK.DAILY_LIMIT = { FREE: 5, PRO: 20 }`; session required; no entitlement gate; a 200 carries `{ answer, limit, remaining }`; a 429 carries `{ error: { code: 'ASK_DAILY_LIMIT_REACHED', limit, message, requestId } }`.
- Profile: `pro: { isActive, expiresAt, product }` replaces `entitlements`.
- Banks: Easy is bundled. Medium and Hard download on first use (opening a track's difficulty step) with hash verification and the existing cache; the background refresh updates only banks already on the device.
- Schema: `BankEntry` has no `access` and no `productId`; the manifest schema version becomes 3; bank files stay at their current schema version.
- `SponsoredCard`: "Sponsored" eyebrow at least 15 points high at the top; headline, one body line, optional icon, one button; no media; never on the question card, in the drawer, mid-round, or in a review round. Placements: results screen and track list. Cadence: `SPONSOR.MIN_ROUNDS_BEFORE_FIRST = 2`, `SPONSOR.ROUNDS_BETWEEN = 3`; review rounds count toward the counter but never show a card.
- Mobile ads: non-personalised only (`requestNonPersonalizedAdsOnly: true`); no ATT prompt; UMP consent before the first request in the EEA and UK; AdChoices top-right with that corner kept clear. A missing ad id, no fill, or a load error renders the house card. Google's sample ids are allowed only in development and preview builds; a production build without real AdMob ids fails in `app.config.ts`.
- Web ads: EthicalAds text placement with `data-ea-manual="true"`, the `dark flat` classes, `--ea-` custom properties from the app's tokens, no cookies, no consent banner; a direct sponsor from `content/sponsor.json`; the house card otherwise. No AdSense anywhere.
- Analytics events added: `ad_shown`, `ad_clicked` (`placement`, `source`), `pro_purchased` (`product`). No property named `code`, `email`, or `token`.
- Web: `web.output: 'static'`; `generateStaticParams` on every dynamic route from `BUNDLED_MANIFEST`; `ContentProvider` renders the bundled content before storage is read so the static HTML has a body; the deploy is `wrangler pages deploy dist --project-name=syntactical`; the origin stays `https://syntactical.dev`, so `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` and the `SameSite=Lax` cookie are unchanged.
- Models: `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` defaults to `claude-haiku-5-5`; `OPENAI_MODEL` is required with `OPENAI_API_KEY`; `MODEL_PRIMARY` defaults to `anthropic`. A transient or configuration failure moves the call to the next provider; a refusal or truncation is final and never sent to the other vendor. Each attempt gets 11 seconds. No prompt, learner message, answer, or SDK error object reaches a log line or an error message.
- Fixtures: a fixture adapter is selected only by the loopback-host guard the e2e build already uses or by `NODE_ENV=test` on the server; a test fails if a fixture module is reachable from the production import graph (Task 4.14).
- Lighthouse accessibility stays at 100 on the pages the e2e suite checks; the sponsored card has an accessible name that starts with "Sponsored:".
- No change to progress, stats, review scheduling, or the quiz engine.

## Review Focus

Inputs the spec implies that ordinary tests could miss, most likely first. Each has a test in the owning task.

1. **An annual `EXPIRATION` arriving after a lifetime `NON_RENEWING_PURCHASE` for the same user.** The lifetime row stays granted and `hasPro` stays true. Owner: Task 3.4.
2. **A `RENEWAL` with an older `event_timestamp_ms` than an `EXPIRATION` already recorded.** The expiration wins and `expires_at` does not move forward. Owner: Task 3.4.
3. **An annual grant event without `expiration_at_ms`.** Recorded, grants nothing, logs a warning; never Pro forever. Owner: Task 3.4.
4. **A Play subscription reported as `syntactical.pro.annual:yearly`.** The server grants the annual and the app prices and buys it. Owners: Tasks 3.1 and 3.3 (server), Task 4.4 (app).
5. **A free user at the Ask cap who becomes Pro the same day.** The next ask succeeds against the Pro limit without waiting for a new usage date. Owner: Task 3.8.
6. **A Medium bank requested offline with no cached copy, after the Easy bank of the same track played.** The difficulty step shows "Needs a connection to load" and nothing crashes. Owners: Tasks 2.5 and 2.6.
7. **A never-opened Medium bank during the background refresh.** It is not downloaded; a cached one whose hash changed is. Owners: Tasks 2.5 and 2.6.
8. **A manifest that still carries `access` or `productId`.** The validator rejects it with a message naming the key, so a stale pipeline output cannot ship. Owner: Task 1.1.
9. **A static export of `app/[language]/[difficulty]/play.tsx` with empty params at build time.** The page renders its loading state, not the not-found screen, and hydrates to the right bank. Owner: Task 5.1.
10. **The static HTML of the home page.** It carries the language list, not an empty body. Owner: Task 7.1.
11. **A sponsored card rendered while Pro status is unknown (loading).** Nothing renders until the status is ready; a Pro user never sees a flash of the card. Owner: Task 6.3.
12. **A native ad that loads after the results screen unmounted.** No state update on an unmounted component, the ad is destroyed, and no `ad_shown` fires. Owner: Task 6.15.
13. **The EEA consent form declined.** The SDK initialises, requests stay non-personalised, and the house card shows if no ad is served; the app never blocks on consent. Owner: Task 6.14.
14. **A direct sponsor in `content/sponsor.json` whose end date has passed.** The house card shows and the build does not fail. Owner: Task 6.10.
15. **A production build with Google's sample AdMob ids.** `app.config.ts` refuses it, naming the variable. Owner: Task 6.13.
16. **A refusal from the primary model.** The answer is `null` and the secondary is never called. Owner: Task 9.4.
17. **A retired model (404) on the primary.** One slow request, then 15 minutes on the secondary, one error log naming provider, model, and status; the daily availability check catches it before a learner does. Owners: Tasks 9.4 and 9.7.
18. **A fixture purchase store in a production build.** Unreachable: selected only behind the loopback guard and absent from the production import graph. Owner: Task 4.14.

## How to execute this plan

- **Full send.** The work is one ordered list of atomic tasks, executed top to bottom in the order of "The areas". Task ids are `<area>.<n>`. Each task is one behaviour: one RED test file, a GREEN change to as few files as the behaviour needs, and two commits. A task with nothing to test (content import, config, docs) says so and gives a verification command with its expected output.
- **Branches exist for CI, not for review.** CI gates per PR (the content drift check, the server integration suites, the oracle runners), so the areas land as the PRs in "The areas", each opened as a draft at its first RED commit and pushed after every GREEN. Areas 1 and 2 share one branch because area 1's schema change leaves the app, server, and e2e typechecks red until area 2's tasks land; that PR's CI is green only after Task 2.15.
- **No owner gate on the code.** Every external dependency has a fixture (see "Seams and fixtures"), so owner actions outside the repo gate only the cutover checks, never a task.
- **Test-first, by the book.** The RED test is written by the model that will not implement it (pick the provider with `~/.claude/enforce/route.sh`; fall back to a fresh-context `test-author` subagent), run against the unchanged code, and committed alone with the failing command and failure line in the commit body. GREEN is by the implementer, who does not edit RED tests (one `DISPUTE` if a test looks wrong, for example a field name the installed SDK's types contradict).
- **Review and merge without the owner.** At the end of each PR, one fresh-context `pr-reviewer` subagent reviews the diff against this plan and the spec; the implementer fixes what it finds and merges on green. The owner does not review PRs. Two merges wait for the owner's click under the repo's rule for security-touching changes: area 3 (how purchases grant access) and area 5's cutover commit (secrets and the domain).
- RED commit body format:

  ```
  test(<scope>): <behavior>

  RED: <exact command>
  Failure: <first failing assertion or module error line>
  ```

- Commands: content-schema tests `cd packages/content-schema && npx vitest run <path>`; server unit tests `cd server && npx vitest run <path>`; server integration tests `cd server && npx vitest run --config vitest.integration.config.ts <path>` (needs `TEST_DATABASE_URL` or local Docker); server GREEN gate `cd server && npm test && npm run test:integration && npm run typecheck`; pipeline tests `cd pipeline && npx vitest run <path>` (`SKIP_DOCKER_TESTS=1` where Docker is unavailable); app tests `npx jest <path>`; typechecks `npx tsc --noEmit` (root), `npm run typecheck:workspaces`, `npm run typecheck:e2e`; lint `npm run lint`; content drift `npm run content:build && git diff --exit-code content/manifest.json services/content/*.generated.ts`. Run `npx prettier --write` on every file you create or edit before committing.
- Line numbers quoted in a task are from `main` at `6f12b7c`. An earlier task may have shifted them; the quoted text, not the number, identifies the lines to replace.
- Deletions are listed per task. Delete the test with the code it covers in the same commit; CI runs every `scripts/__tests__` file through root Jest.

## Seams and fixtures: build everything first, plug in the real adapters last

The repo already treats every integration as an adapter with a fail-closed stub (`ALLOW_STUBBED_INTEGRATIONS`, `docs/launch-placeholders.md`; a missing client key makes purchases "unavailable" and analytics a no-op). The e2e suite grants entitlements by inserting rows with `source = 'e2e'` straight into `entitlements`, never through a store. Every task builds against these seams, so the only work left when the owner's accounts exist is pasting keys and running the device checks.

## Area 1: schema, content, build, and pipeline (`feat/free-banks`)

These tasks replace the old Tasks 1.1, 1.2, and 1.3. The app, server, and deploy work that completes the free-banks PR follows in area 2 (Tasks 2.1 to 2.15), on the same branch.

### Sequencing inside the free-banks PR (areas 1 and 2)

- Order: 1.1 (schema), 1.2 (import and manifest), 1.3 and 1.4 (content build), 1.5 to 1.7 (pipeline), 1.8 (README). Each task depends on the one before it.
- Task 1.1 changes the shared schema that every workspace reads. From its GREEN commit until the task that fixes each area lands, these suites are knowingly red, and each task's Step 4 states which suites it turns green:
  - root Jest `scripts/__tests__`: red from 1.1 (the shipped manifest still carries `access`) until 1.3.
  - pipeline Vitest and `cd pipeline && npx tsc --noEmit`: red from 1.1 (fixtures build `access` and `schemaVersion: 2` manifests; commands read `BankEntry.access`) until 1.6.
  - root `npx tsc --noEmit`, the app Jest suites, and the server suites: red from 1.1 wherever they read `access` or `productId` or build `schemaVersion: 2` manifests, until the app and server tasks of area 2.
- Do not push the branch for review between 1.2 and 1.4: between them `npm run content:build` would bundle all 36 banks, so the CI drift check would fail.
- Manifest schema version: the manifest moves from 2 to 3. Bank files do not change shape and stay at schema 2, so the version constant is split in two (`SUPPORTED_MANIFEST_SCHEMA_VERSION = 3`, `SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION = 2` for banks). See "Open questions (area 1)", item 1.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**

```ts
// packages/content-schema/src/__tests__/validateManifestFreeBanks.test.ts
// Manifest schema 3: every bank is free, so a bank entry carries path, hash, contentVersion, and topicCounts only.
// An entry that still carries `access` or `productId` (a stale pipeline output, or a manifest from before the
// import) is rejected with a rule naming the key, before any other rule. Bank files keep schema 2.
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';

import { SUPPORTED_MANIFEST_SCHEMA_VERSION, SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION } from '../supportedSchemaVersion.js';
import { validateManifest } from '../validateManifest.js';

const VALID_HASH = 'a'.repeat(32) + '0123456789abcdef'.repeat(2);

function buildBank(difficulty: string, overrides: Record<string, unknown> = {}): Record<string, unknown> {
  return { path: `python/${difficulty}.json`, hash: VALID_HASH, contentVersion: 1, topicCounts: {}, ...overrides };
}

const ALL_BANKS = { easy: buildBank('easy'), medium: buildBank('medium'), hard: buildBank('hard') };

function buildManifest(banks: Record<string, unknown>, schemaVersion: unknown = 3): Record<string, unknown> {
  return {
    schemaVersion,
    languages: [
      {
        id: 'python',
        label: 'Python',
        glyph: 'PY',
        tagline: 'Runtime semantics, stdlib, and the sharp edges.',
        grammar: 'python',
        topics: [{ id: 'strings', label: 'Strings' }],
        misconceptions: [],
        banks,
      },
    ],
  };
}

describe('validateManifest with every bank free', () => {
  it('accepts easy, medium, and hard banks that carry neither access nor productId, unchanged', () => {
    const input = buildManifest(ALL_BANKS);
    expect(validateManifest(input)).toEqual({ isValid: true, manifest: input });
  });

  it.each([
    ['easy', 'access', 'free'],
    ['medium', 'access', 'paid'],
    ['hard', 'access', 'free'],
    ['medium', 'productId', 'syntactical.python.medium'],
    ['easy', 'productId', 'syntactical.python.easy'],
  ])('rejects a %s bank carrying %s %j with a rule naming the key', (difficulty, key, value) => {
    const input = buildManifest({ ...ALL_BANKS, [difficulty]: buildBank(difficulty, { [key]: value }) });
    expect(validateManifest(input)).toEqual({
      isValid: false,
      rule: `languages[0].banks.${difficulty}.${key} is not allowed`,
    });
  });

  it('names access first when a stale paid entry carries both keys', () => {
    const stale = buildBank('medium', { access: 'paid', productId: 'syntactical.python.medium' });
    expect(validateManifest(buildManifest({ ...ALL_BANKS, medium: stale }))).toEqual({
      isValid: false,
      rule: 'languages[0].banks.medium.access is not allowed',
    });
  });

  it('names the retired key before the hash rule, so a stale entry is reported for what is stale', () => {
    const stale = buildBank('hard', { access: 'paid', hash: '' });
    expect(validateManifest(buildManifest({ ...ALL_BANKS, hard: stale }))).toEqual({
      isValid: false,
      rule: 'languages[0].banks.hard.access is not allowed',
    });
  });

  it.each([[2], [4]])('rejects schemaVersion %j even when no bank carries a retired key', (schemaVersion) => {
    expect(validateManifest(buildManifest(ALL_BANKS, schemaVersion))).toEqual({
      isValid: false,
      rule: 'schemaVersion is not supported',
    });
  });

  it('moves the manifest to schema 3 and leaves bank files at schema 2', () => {
    expect(SUPPORTED_MANIFEST_SCHEMA_VERSION).toBe(3);
    expect(SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION).toBe(2);
  });
});
```

`git cat-file blob` writes the committed bytes with no checkout and no textconv, so the private repo's working tree is not touched.

```bash
TRACKS=$(node -p 'require("./content/manifest.json").languages.map(({ id }) => id).join(" ")')
for track in $TRACKS; do

  done
done
```

Expected: `36`.

- [ ] **Step 3: Verify every copied bank against the hash the manifest already holds**

```bash
mismatches=0
for track in $TRACKS; do
  for difficulty in medium hard; do
    expected=$(node -p "require('./content/manifest.json').languages.find(({ id }) => id === '$track').banks.$difficulty.hash")
    actual=$(shasum -a 256 "content/$track/$difficulty.json" | cut -d' ' -f1)
    if [ "$expected" = "$actual" ]; then
      echo "ok $track/$difficulty"
    else
      echo "MISMATCH $track/$difficulty expected=$expected actual=$actual"
      mismatches=$((mismatches + 1))
    fi
  done
done
echo "mismatches: $mismatches"
```

Expected: 24 `ok` lines and `mismatches: 0`. On any mismatch, stop: run `git clean -n content` to list the copied files, remove them with `git clean -f content` after checking the list, and ask the owner which side is stale. Do not edit the manifest.

```bash
const fs = require("fs");
```

```ts
// scripts/__tests__/buildContentManifestEveryBank.test.ts
// Every bank lives under content/: the build hashes Medium and Hard banks from there with no second root, ships the
// misconceptions that cards in any bank link (and drops the rest), and bundles only BUNDLED_DIFFICULTIES, which is
// Easy alone. Medium and Hard reach the app as downloads.
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
import { cp, mkdir, mkdtemp, readFile, rm, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
import { join } from 'node:path';

import { BUNDLED_DIFFICULTIES, buildContentManifest } from '../buildContentManifest.mjs';

import { stripMisconceptionLinks } from './stripMisconceptionLinks';

const REPOSITORY_CONTENT_DIR = join(__dirname, '..', '..', 'content');
const STALE_HASH = 'a'.repeat(64);
const ENTRY_A = { description: 'Believes default arguments are rebuilt on each call.', id: 'python.entry-a' };
const ENTRY_B = { description: 'Believes a list copy is always deep.', id: 'python.entry-b' };

type BankEntry = { contentVersion: number; hash: string; path: string };
type Language = { banks: Record<string, BankEntry>; id: string; misconceptions: { description: string; id: string }[] };
type Manifest = { languages: Language[] };
type Choice = { misconceptionId?: string; rationale?: string };
type Question = { answerIndex?: number; choices?: Choice[]; type: string };

describe('buildContentManifest with every bank under content/', () => {
  let workDir: string;
  let contentDir: string;
  let taxonomyDir: string;
  let outputs: { banksPath: string; manifestPath: string };

  beforeEach(async () => {
    workDir = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), 'content-every-bank-'));
    contentDir = join(workDir, 'content');
    taxonomyDir = join(workDir, 'taxonomy');
    outputs = { banksPath: join(workDir, 'banks.ts'), manifestPath: join(workDir, 'manifest.ts') };
    await cp(REPOSITORY_CONTENT_DIR, contentDir, { recursive: true });
    await mkdir(taxonomyDir);
  });

  afterEach(async () => {
    await rm(workDir, { force: true, recursive: true });
  });

  async function readManifest(): Promise<Manifest> {
    return JSON.parse(await readFile(join(contentDir, 'manifest.json'), 'utf8')) as Manifest;
  }

  async function writeManifest(manifest: Manifest): Promise<void> {
    await writeFile(join(contentDir, 'manifest.json'), `${JSON.stringify(manifest, null, 2)}\n`);
  }

  function findPython(manifest: Manifest): Language {
    return manifest.languages.find(({ id }) => id === 'python') as Language;
  }

  async function hashOf(bankPath: string): Promise<string> {
    return createHash('sha256')
      .update(await readFile(join(contentDir, bankPath)))
      .digest('hex');
  }

  // Makes the first wrong choice of the bank's first multiple-choice question carry `misconceptionId`.
  async function linkFirstCard(bankPath: string, misconceptionId: string): Promise<void> {
    const file = join(contentDir, bankPath);
    const bank = JSON.parse(await readFile(file, 'utf8')) as { questions: Question[] };
    const question = bank.questions.find(({ type }) => type === 'mc') as Question;
    const choice = (question.choices as Choice[])[question.answerIndex === 0 ? 1 : 0];
    choice.misconceptionId = misconceptionId;
    choice.rationale = 'This is the mistaken reading, and the real behavior differs for a stated reason.';
    await writeFile(file, `${JSON.stringify(bank, null, 2)}\n`);
  }

  it('bundles Easy and nothing else', () => {
    expect(BUNDLED_DIFFICULTIES).toEqual(['easy']);
  });

  it('hashes every bank from content/ and bumps the version of only the bank whose recorded hash was stale', async () => {
    const manifest = await readManifest();
    const before = structuredClone(findPython(manifest).banks);
    findPython(manifest).banks.medium.hash = STALE_HASH;
    await writeManifest(manifest);

    await buildContentManifest(contentDir, outputs);

    const after = await readManifest();
    for (const language of after.languages) {
      for (const bank of Object.values(language.banks)) {
        expect(bank.hash).toBe(await hashOf(bank.path));
      }
    }
    expect(findPython(after).banks.medium.contentVersion).toBe(before.medium.contentVersion + 1);
    expect(findPython(after).banks.hard.contentVersion).toBe(before.hard.contentVersion);
  });

  it('bundles the Easy bank of every track and no Medium or Hard bank', async () => {
    await buildContentManifest(contentDir, outputs);

    const bundle = await readFile(outputs.banksPath, 'utf8');
    const bundledKeys = [...bundle.matchAll(/^ {2}'([^']+)': require/gm)].map(([, key]) => key);
    const trackIds = (await readManifest()).languages.map(({ id }) => id);
    expect(bundledKeys.sort()).toEqual(trackIds.map((id) => `${id}/easy`).sort());
  });

  describe('misconceptions', () => {
    beforeEach(async () => {
      // The real banks link the real taxonomy; each test here supplies its own.
      await stripMisconceptionLinks(contentDir);
      await writeFile(join(taxonomyDir, 'python.json'), JSON.stringify([ENTRY_A, ENTRY_B]));
    });

    it('ships an entry that only a Medium card links', async () => {
      await linkFirstCard('python/medium.json', ENTRY_B.id);

      await buildContentManifest(contentDir, outputs, taxonomyDir);

      expect(findPython(await readManifest()).misconceptions).toEqual([ENTRY_B]);
    });

    it('drops an entry the manifest lists when no card in any bank links it', async () => {
      const manifest = await readManifest();
      findPython(manifest).misconceptions = [ENTRY_A];
      await writeManifest(manifest);
      await linkFirstCard('python/hard.json', ENTRY_B.id);

      await buildContentManifest(contentDir, outputs, taxonomyDir);

      expect(findPython(await readManifest()).misconceptions).toEqual([ENTRY_B]);
    });
  });
});
```

  ```js
  // Keeps the entries of each language's owner-approved `<language>.json` that some card in any of its banks links.
  // The `<language>.draft.json` the pipeline writes is never read. Language ids are already validated (they are
  // joined into the path), and a malformed approved file fails the build.
  async function applyApprovedTaxonomies(taxonomyDir, manifest, contentDir, bankCache) {
    for (const language of manifest.languages) {
      const approvedName = `${language.id}.json`;
      const misconceptions = await readApprovedTaxonomy(join(taxonomyDir, approvedName));
      if (misconceptions === undefined) continue;
      const problem = findMisconceptionsProblem(misconceptions, language.id);
      if (problem !== null) throw new Error(`taxonomy ${approvedName} is invalid: ${problem}`);
      const linkedIds = new Set();
      for (const bank of Object.values(language.banks)) {
        const { data } = await readBank(contentDir, bank, bankCache);
        // Check the root shape before iterating; full validation uses the filtered taxonomy below.
        if (!Array.isArray(data?.questions)) assertValidBank(bank.path, data, language);
        for (const question of data.questions) {
          for (const id of collectMisconceptionIds(question)) linkedIds.add(id);
        }
      }
      language.misconceptions = misconceptions.filter(({ id }) => linkedIds.has(id));
    }
  }
  ```

```ts
// scripts/__tests__/buildContentManifestUnlistedBank.test.ts
// The web build copies content/ whole, so a bank file the manifest does not list would ship unhashed and
// unvalidated. The content build fails naming every .json file under a track directory that is not a manifest
// bank path, before it writes anything. Files at the top of content/ and non-JSON files are not banks.
import { cp, mkdir, mkdtemp, readFile, rm, stat, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
import { dirname, join } from 'node:path';

import { buildContentManifest } from '../buildContentManifest.mjs';

const REPOSITORY_CONTENT_DIR = join(__dirname, '..', '..', 'content');

  let contentDir: string;

  beforeEach(async () => {
    workDir = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), 'content-unlisted-'));
    contentDir = join(workDir, 'content');
    outputs = { banksPath: join(workDir, 'banks.ts'), manifestPath: join(workDir, 'manifest.ts') };
    await cp(REPOSITORY_CONTENT_DIR, contentDir, { recursive: true });
  });

  afterEach(async () => {
    await rm(workDir, { force: true, recursive: true });
  });

  async function plantBank(bankPath: string): Promise<void> {

    await cp(join(contentDir, 'python', 'easy.json'), join(contentDir, bankPath));

});
```

  ```js
  // The web build copies content/ whole, so every .json file under a track directory must be a bank the manifest
  // lists; otherwise it would ship unhashed and unvalidated. Files at the top of content/ are not banks.
  async function assertNoUnlistedBanks(contentDir, manifest) {
    const listed = new Set(listBankEntries(manifest).map(({ bank }) => bank.path));
    const entries = await readdir(contentDir, { recursive: true, withFileTypes: true });
    const unlisted = entries
      .filter((entry) => entry.isFile() && entry.name.endsWith('.json'))
      .map((entry) => relative(contentDir, join(entry.parentPath, entry.name)).split(sep).join('/'))
      .filter((bankPath) => bankPath.includes('/') && !listed.has(bankPath))
      .sort();
    if (unlisted.length > 0) throw new Error(`bank file not in the manifest: ${unlisted.join(', ')}`);
  }
  ```

- In `buildContentManifest`, after `assertValidManifest(withPlaceholderHashes(manifest));` add `await assertNoUnlistedBanks(contentDir, manifest);`.

```ts
    await writeJson(join(pipelineDir, 'reports/latest.json'), {
      counts: {},
      finishedAt: 'f',
      questions: [{ bankKey: 'python/medium', id: 'm-1', runtimeVersion: 'python 3.13', status: 'passed' }],
      runId: 'r',
      stage: 'validate',
      startedAt: 's',
    });
    await writeJson(join(pipelineDir, 'classifications/python/medium.json'), {
      'm-1': { confidence: 0.9, topic: 'strings' },
    });
    await writeJson(join(pipelineDir, 'enrichment/python/medium.json'), {
      'm-1': [0, 2].map((choiceIndex) => ({ choiceIndex, misconceptionId: TAG, rationale: `why ${choiceIndex}` })),
    });
    const buildManifest = vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(undefined);

    const { banks } = await publish({
      buildManifest,
      contentDir,
      log: () => undefined,
      newRunId: () => 'run-1',
      now: () => NOW,
      pipelineDir,
    });

    expect(banks['python/medium']).toMatchObject({ isWritten: true });
    const { questions } = await readJson<{ questions: Json[] }>(join(contentDir, 'python/medium.json'));
    expect(questions).toEqual([expect.objectContaining({ id: 'm-1', topic: 'strings' })]);
    expect(buildManifest).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    expect(buildManifest).toHaveBeenCalledWith();
  });

  it('classify stages a Hard bank under pipeline/classifications', async () => {
    const provider: ModelProvider = {
      async generate(request) {
        return { model: 'fake', value: request.schema.parse({ confidence: 0.9, topic: 'strings' }) };
      },
    };

    await classify({
      contentDir,
      log: () => undefined,
      newRunId: () => 'run-1',
      now: () => NOW,
      pipelineDir,
      provider,
    });

    expect(await readJson(join(pipelineDir, 'classifications/python/hard.json'))).toEqual({
      'h-1': { confidence: 0.9, topic: 'strings' },
    });
  });

  it('validate reads a Medium bank from content/ with its oracle from pipeline/oracles', async () => {
    const oracle: Oracle = { code: 'print(1)', language: 'python' };
    await writeJson(join(pipelineDir, 'oracles/python/medium.json'), { 'm-1': oracle });
    const seen = new Map<string, Oracle | null>();

    const report = await validateContent({
      contentDir,
      newRunId: () => 'run-1',
      now: () => NOW,
      pipelineDir,
      reportsDir: join(pipelineDir, 'reports'),
      validate: async ({ id }, given) => {
        seen.set(id, given);
        return { status: 'passed' };
      },
    });

    expect(seen.get('m-1')).toEqual(oracle);
    expect(report.questions.map(({ bankKey, id }) => `${bankKey} ${id}`)).toEqual([
      'python/easy e-1',
      'python/hard h-1',
      'python/medium m-1',
    ]);
  });
});
```

```ts
// Flags from the two-repo content layout. They are refused, not ignored, so a command line from before the import
// fails loudly instead of running against content/ while its caller expects another tree.
const RETIRED_FLAGS: Record<string, string> = {
  '--content-root': '--content-root is not supported: every bank is under content/',
  '--free-only': '--free-only is not supported: every bank is free',
};

function findRetiredFlagMessage(argv: string[]): string | undefined {
  const flag = Object.keys(RETIRED_FLAGS).find((name) =>
    argv.some((arg) => arg === name || arg.startsWith(`${name}=`)),
  );
  return flag === undefined ? undefined : RETIRED_FLAGS[flag];
}
```

and in `runCli`, after `const [command] = argv.slice(FIRST_COMMAND_ARG);`, add

```ts
const retiredFlagMessage = findRetiredFlagMessage(argv);
if (retiredFlagMessage !== undefined) {
  stderr(`${retiredFlagMessage}\n`);
  return 1;
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Replace lines 50-81 with this text**

```markdown
## Content

Questions are not compiled into the app logic. Every bank lives in this repository at `content/<track>/<difficulty>.json`, and `content/manifest.json` lists each one with its SHA-256 hash, content version, and topic counts. The Easy banks are bundled into the app (`services/content/bundledBanks.generated.ts`), so a first round works offline. Medium and Hard banks are downloaded from the content base URL the first time they are played, checked against the manifest hash, and cached; offline with no cached copy, the difficulty step shows "Needs a connection to load".

Each question is multiple choice (`mc`), true/false (`bool`), or A/B (`ab`), and carries a `query` (`title`, `explanation`, optional `syntax`, `tags`, and `docs`: up to three https `{ title, url }` links to official documentation) that backs the query drawer. Before an answer the drawer shows only the title and `docs`, so those must not give the answer away; the syntax, explanation, and tags appear after. Each question also carries `provenance` saying where it came from and how it was validated. The full shape is `packages/content-schema/src/validateQuestionBank.ts`.

### Editing a question

1. Edit the question in `content/<track>/<difficulty>.json`.
2. Run `npm run content:build`. It validates every bank, recomputes every hash and topic count into `content/manifest.json`, bumps the content version of each bank whose bytes changed, lists the misconceptions some card links, and regenerates `services/content/bundledManifest.generated.ts` and `services/content/bundledBanks.generated.ts`. It fails on a `.json` file under a track directory that the manifest does not list.
3. Commit the bank, `content/manifest.json`, and both generated files together. CI fails the pull request if any of them drift from what `npm run content:build` produces.

### Adding a track

1. Add the bank files `content/<track>/easy.json`, `medium.json`, and `hard.json`.
2. Add an entry to `languages` in `content/manifest.json` with `id`, `label`, `glyph`, `tagline`, `grammar` (one of `GRAMMARS` in `packages/content-schema/src/grammars.ts`; any other value renders code as plain text), `kind: 'topic'` for a topic track, `topics`, `misconceptions`, and a `banks` object whose entries each have a `path`, `"hash": ""`, `"contentVersion": 1`, and `"topicCounts": {}`. A bank entry carrying `access` or `productId` is rejected.
3. Run `npm run content:build` to fill in the hashes and regenerate the bundled files, then commit as above.

### The content pipeline

`npm run pipeline -- <command>` reads every bank from `content/` and stages its work under `pipeline/`: `classifications/`, `generated/`, `disputed/`, `oracles/`, `review/`, `review-queue/`, and `reports/` stay local and untracked, while `pipeline/taxonomy/`, `pipeline/enrichment/`, and `pipeline/references/` are committed. Model commands run through `claude -p` unless you pass `--api`, which uses `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (plus `ANTHROPIC_WORKSPACE_ID` when the key is organization-level). The second model, which double-checks each result, is `PIPELINE_SECOND_MODEL` (default `claude-haiku-5-5`). Each step saves as it goes and skips what is already done, so a rerun only pays for what is missing. The `--content-root` and `--free-only` flags from the old two-repository layout are refused.

To add questions to a bank:

1. `npm run pipeline -- classify` assigns each question a topic; `npm run pipeline -- gap-fill` generates questions for thin topics, keeping each only when its executed oracle proves its answer.
2. `npm run pipeline -- validate` runs every oracle in Docker and writes the report the next steps read.
3. `npm run pipeline -- review` writes `pipeline/review/<track>-<difficulty>.md` for the owner to approve or reject; rerun it to record the decisions.
4. `npm run pipeline -- publish` writes each bank that passes `validateBankForPublish` into `content/<track>/<difficulty>.json` and runs the content build. Commit the banks, the manifest, and the generated files together.

To add rationales and before-answer references to existing questions:

1. `npm run pipeline -- enrich --judge-without-oracle [--language python,postgres]` writes a rationale and misconception tag for each wrong choice into `pipeline/enrichment/`. A language needs an approved `pipeline/taxonomy/<language>.json` (draft one with `draft-taxonomy <language>`). A question without a recorded oracle run is grounded in its answer key and explanation, and both models' judges must accept each rationale.
2. `npm run pipeline -- write-references [--language python,postgres]` writes each question's reference into `pipeline/references/`: a broad topic title and links on the track's documentation hosts, shown before an answer, and a syntax reference with examples, shown after (`pipeline/src/services/references/DOC_HOSTS.ts`). Both models must agree the title and link titles do not give the answer away; a reference that does is rewritten once, then left out.
3. `npm run pipeline -- verify-doc-links` fetches every staged link (no model, but it needs network access to the documentation hosts) and records the results in `pipeline/references/doc-links.json`. A link to a `#section` passes only when that section is on the page.
4. `npm run pipeline -- apply-staging` merges the staged rationales and references into every bank without adding or dropping any question, keeping only links that passed step 3, then runs the content build. Commit the banks, the manifest, the generated files, and `pipeline/enrichment` and `pipeline/references` together.
```

```tsx
// Difficulty step route for one language; a language the manifest does not list shows the
// not-found screen. Every bank is free: selecting a difficulty opens its topic step.
import { router, useLocalSearchParams } from 'expo-router';
import { ScrollView, View } from 'react-native';

import NotFoundScreen from '../+not-found';
import { DifficultyStep } from '../../components/menu/DifficultyStep';
import { findLanguageEntry } from '../../services/content/findLanguageEntry';
import { useLanguageManifest } from '../../state/useLanguageManifest';

export default function DifficultyScreen() {
  const { language } = useLocalSearchParams<{ language: string }>();
  const { languages } = useLanguageManifest();
  if (!findLanguageEntry(languages, language)) return <NotFoundScreen />;
  return (
    <ScrollView contentContainerClassName="flex-grow items-center justify-center px-4 py-8">
      <View className="w-full max-w-xl">
        <DifficultyStep
          language={language}
          onSelectDifficulty={(difficulty) => router.push(`/${language}/${difficulty}`)}
          onBack={() => router.replace('/')}
        />
      </View>
    </ScrollView>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// Step 2 of the launch flow: the difficulties the chosen language's
// manifest entry names, labeled from the app's registry, each showing
// whether its bank is ready, downloading, failed, or needs a connection
// (no local copy while offline).
import { DIFFICULTIES } from '@syntactical/content-schema';
import { Pressable, Text, View } from 'react-native';

import { findDifficulty } from '../../services/content/findDifficulty';
import { findLanguageEntry } from '../../services/content/findLanguageEntry';
import { useIsOnline } from '../../state/useIsOnline';
import { useKeyboardNav } from '../../state/useKeyboardNav';
import { useLanguageManifest } from '../../state/useLanguageManifest';
import { useQuestionBank, type QuestionBankState } from '../../state/useQuestionBank';

import { SelectionCard } from './SelectionCard';
import { pickKeyHint } from './pickKeyHint';

type DifficultyOptionProps = {
  difficultyId: string;
  keyHint: number | undefined;
  language: string;
  onSelect: () => void;
};
type DifficultyStepProps = {
  language: string;
  onBack: () => void;
  onSelectDifficulty: (difficultyId: string) => void;
};

function describeBankStatus(bankState: QuestionBankState, isOnline: boolean): string | undefined {
  if (bankState.status === 'ready') return undefined;
  if (!isOnline) return 'Needs a connection to load';
  if (bankState.status === 'error') return 'Download failed. Tap to retry';
  return 'Downloading';
}

function readDifficultyCopy(difficultyId: string) {
  return (
    findDifficulty(difficultyId) ?? {
      description: '',
      label: difficultyId,
    }
  );
}

function DifficultyOption({ difficultyId, keyHint, language, onSelect }: DifficultyOptionProps) {
  const bankState = useQuestionBank(language, difficultyId);
  const isOnline = useIsOnline();
  const { description, label } = readDifficultyCopy(difficultyId);
  const { status } = bankState;
  const isRetryable = status === 'error' && isOnline;
  const isDisabled = status !== 'ready' && !isRetryable;
  const handleSelect = 'retry' in bankState ? bankState.retry : onSelect;
  useKeyboardNav({
    onSelectChoice: (index) => {
      if (keyHint !== undefined && index === keyHint - 1 && !isDisabled) handleSelect();
    },
  });
  return (
    <SelectionCard
      keyHint={keyHint}
      title={label}
      subtitle={description}
      onSelect={handleSelect}
      isDisabled={isDisabled}
      statusLabel={describeBankStatus(bankState, isOnline)}
    />
  );
}

export function DifficultyStep({ language, onBack, onSelectDifficulty }: DifficultyStepProps) {
  const { languages } = useLanguageManifest();
  const languageEntry = findLanguageEntry(languages, language);
  const difficultyIds = DIFFICULTIES.map(({ id }) => id).filter(
    (id) => languageEntry && Object.hasOwn(languageEntry.banks, id),
  );
  useKeyboardNav({ onEscape: onBack });
  return (
    <View>
      <View className="mb-4 flex-row items-center justify-between">
        <Text role="heading" aria-level={1} className="font-mono text-xs uppercase tracking-widest text-muted">
          Step 2 / Select difficulty <Text className="text-signal">{languageEntry?.label ?? language}</Text>
        </Text>
        <Pressable role="button" aria-label="Back" onPress={onBack}>
          <Text className="font-mono text-xs text-muted">Back</Text>
        </Pressable>
      </View>
      <View className="gap-3">
        {difficultyIds.map((difficultyId, index) => (
          <DifficultyOption
            key={difficultyId}
            difficultyId={difficultyId}
            keyHint={pickKeyHint(index + 1)}
            language={language}
            onSelect={() => onSelectDifficulty(difficultyId)}
          />
        ))}
      </View>
    </View>
  );
}
```

### Task 2.5: A Medium bank downloads on first use, caches, and fails without the API (RED, Review Focus 4)

**Files:**

- Test: `state/__tests__/useQuestionBankMedium.test.tsx` (new)
- Test: `components/menu/__tests__/DifficultyStepMediumOffline.test.tsx` (new)

**Interfaces:**

- Consumes: `useQuestionBank(language, difficulty): QuestionBankState`; `ContentProvider({ contentBaseUrl })`; `DifficultyStep`; `prefetchChangedBanks(queryClient, manifest, access)`; `ContentAccess.readLocalBank` (the cached bank, else the bundled one, else null, as `ContentProvider` builds it); the `contentFixtures` helpers.
- Produces: the contract Task 2.6 implements: a Medium bank is `loading` while it downloads from `contentBaseUrl`, `ready` from the download and later from the shared cache key `syntactical.content.v1.bank.python.medium`, `error` with `retry` when it cannot download and nothing is cached, never `locked`, and no request goes to the API for a signed-in user. The prefetch after a manifest refresh refreshes only banks the device already has: a bank whose `readLocalBank` copy (bundled or cached) has a hash other than the manifest's is fetched again, and a bank with no local copy (a Medium or Hard bank never opened on this device) is not fetched.

```tsx
// state/__tests__/useQuestionBankMedium.test.tsx
// Area 2 RED (spec 1, "App"): only Easy banks are bundled, so a Medium bank downloads from the
// content host on first use. It is loading while the download is held, ready from the download,
// ready from the shared cache after a restart with no network, and an error with Retry when it
// cannot download and nothing is cached. It is never locked, and a signed-in user's Medium bank
// asks the API nothing: no entitlement check and no owner-scoped cache.
import type { Manifest } from '@syntactical/content-schema';
import AsyncStorage from '@react-native-async-storage/async-storage';
import { QueryClientProvider, type QueryClient } from '@tanstack/react-query';
import { act, renderHook, waitFor } from '@testing-library/react-native';
import type { ReactNode } from 'react';

import { createQueryClient } from '../../config/queryClient';
import {
  CONTENT_BASE_URL,
  MANIFEST_URL,
  buildBankText,
  cloneBundledManifest,
  countFetchesFor,
  hashUtf8Hex,
  listFetchedUrls,
  type FetchRoute,
  stubFetchRoutes,
} from '../../services/content/__tests__/fixtures/contentFixtures';
import { ContentProvider } from '../ContentProvider';
import { useQuestionBank } from '../useQuestionBank';
import { setExpoExtra } from '../../config/expoConstantsMock';
import { settle } from '../../config/settle';

const mockOwner: { current: string | null } = { current: null };

jest.mock('../AuthProvider', () => ({
  useSignedInUserId: () => mockOwner.current,
}));

jest.mock('expo-secure-store', () => ({
  deleteItemAsync: jest.fn(() => Promise.resolve()),
  getItemAsync: jest.fn(() => Promise.resolve(null)),
  setItemAsync: jest.fn(() => Promise.resolve()),
}));

setExpoExtra({ apiBaseUrl: 'https://api.syntactical.dev/v1/', contentBaseUrl: 'https://example.test/content/' });

jest.mock('../../clients/hashClient', () => ({
  hashTextSha256: async (text: string) =>
    require('crypto').createHash('sha256').update(Buffer.from(text, 'utf8')).digest('hex'),
}));

const API_BASE = 'https://api.syntactical.dev/v1/';
const MEDIUM_URL = `${CONTENT_BASE_URL}python/medium.json`;
const SHARED_KEY = 'syntactical.content.v1.bank.python.medium';
const MEDIUM_IDS = ['py-medium-1', 'py-medium-2', 'py-medium-3'];
const MEDIUM_TEXT = buildBankText(MEDIUM_IDS);
const MEDIUM_HASH = hashUtf8Hex(MEDIUM_TEXT);
const OWNER = 'a6f1d1c2-0000-4000-8000-00000000000a';

let queryClient: QueryClient;
const observedStatuses: string[] = [];
const heldBodyRejections: Array<() => void> = [];

function buildManifest(): Manifest {
  const manifest = cloneBundledManifest();
  const python = manifest.languages.find(({ id }) => id === 'python')!;
  python.banks.medium = { ...python.banks.medium!, hash: MEDIUM_HASH };
  return manifest;
}

function respond(routes: Record<string, FetchRoute>) {
  return stubFetchRoutes(
    { [MANIFEST_URL]: () => Promise.resolve(JSON.stringify(buildManifest())), ...routes },
    { shouldRejectUnrouted: true },
  );
}

function holdBody(): Promise<string> {
  return new Promise<string>((_resolve, reject) => {
    heldBodyRejections.push(() => reject(new TypeError('Network request failed')));
  });
}

function Wrapper({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
      <ContentProvider contentBaseUrl={CONTENT_BASE_URL}>{children}</ContentProvider>
    </QueryClientProvider>
  );
}

function readIds(state: unknown): string[] | undefined {
  return (state as { bank?: { questions: { id: string }[] } }).bank?.questions.map(({ id }) => id);
}

async function renderMedium() {
  const rendered = await renderHook(
    () => {
      const state = useQuestionBank('python', 'medium');
      observedStatuses.push(state.status);
      return state;
    },
    { wrapper: Wrapper },
  );
  await settle();
  return rendered;
}

function listApiRequests(): string[] {
  return listFetchedUrls().filter((url) => url.startsWith(API_BASE));
}

describe('useQuestionBank for a Medium bank that is not bundled', () => {
  beforeEach(async () => {
    await AsyncStorage.clear();
    queryClient = createQueryClient();
    mockOwner.current = null;
    observedStatuses.length = 0;
    jest.spyOn(console, 'warn').mockImplementation(() => {});
  });

  afterEach(async () => {
    heldBodyRejections.splice(0).forEach((rejectHeldBody) => rejectHeldBody());
    await settle();
    queryClient.clear();
    jest.restoreAllMocks();
  });

  it('downloads from the content host for a signed-in user, caches it under the shared key, and asks the API nothing', async () => {
    mockOwner.current = OWNER;
    respond({ [MEDIUM_URL]: () => Promise.resolve(MEDIUM_TEXT) });

    const { result } = await renderMedium();

    await waitFor(() => expect(readIds(result.current)).toEqual(MEDIUM_IDS));
    expect(listApiRequests()).toEqual([]);
    const cached = JSON.parse((await AsyncStorage.getItem(SHARED_KEY)) ?? 'null') as { hash: string } | null;
    expect(cached?.hash).toBe(MEDIUM_HASH);
    expect(observedStatuses).not.toContain('locked');
  });

  it('is loading while the download is held open', async () => {
    respond({ [MEDIUM_URL]: holdBody });

    const { result } = await renderMedium();

    await waitFor(() => expect(countFetchesFor(MEDIUM_URL)).toBe(1));
    expect(result.current.status).toBe('loading');
  });

  it('plays the cached copy after a restart with no network', async () => {
    respond({ [MEDIUM_URL]: () => Promise.resolve(MEDIUM_TEXT) });
    const first = await renderMedium();
    await waitFor(() => expect(readIds(first.result.current)).toEqual(MEDIUM_IDS));
    await first.unmount();
    queryClient.clear();

    queryClient = createQueryClient();
    stubFetchRoutes({}, { shouldRejectUnrouted: true });
    const { result } = await renderMedium();

    await waitFor(() => expect(readIds(result.current)).toEqual(MEDIUM_IDS));
    expect(countFetchesFor(MEDIUM_URL)).toBe(0);
  });

  it('is an error with Retry when it cannot download and nothing is cached, and Retry downloads it', async () => {
    let isReachable = false;
    respond({
      [MEDIUM_URL]: () =>
        isReachable ? Promise.resolve(MEDIUM_TEXT) : Promise.reject(new TypeError('Network request failed')),
    });

    const { result } = await renderMedium();

    await waitFor(() => expect(result.current.status).toBe('error'));
    isReachable = true;
    await act(async () => {
      if (result.current.status === 'error') result.current.retry();
    });
    await waitFor(() => expect(readIds(result.current)).toEqual(MEDIUM_IDS));
    expect(observedStatuses).not.toContain('locked');
  });
});
```

```ts
// services/content/__tests__/prefetchChangedBanksFirstUse.test.ts
// Area 2 RED (spec 1, "App"): Medium and Hard banks download on first use, so the prefetch after a
// manifest refresh refreshes only banks the device already has. A local copy is whatever
// `readLocalBank` returns: the cached bank, else the bundled one, as `ContentProvider` builds it.
// A bundled Easy bank and a cached Medium bank whose manifest hash changed are fetched again; a
// Medium bank never opened on this device has no local copy and is not fetched.
import type { CachedBank, Manifest, Question } from '@syntactical/content-schema';
import AsyncStorage from '@react-native-async-storage/async-storage';
import type { QueryClient } from '@tanstack/react-query';
import { waitFor } from '@testing-library/react-native';

import { createQueryClient } from '../../../config/queryClient';
import { settle } from '../../../config/settle';
import { prefetchChangedBanks } from '../prefetchChangedBanks';
import type { ContentAccess } from '../types/ContentAccess';

import {
  CONTENT_BASE_URL,
  buildBankText,
  buildBoolQuestion,
  cloneBundledManifest,
  countFetchesFor,
  hashUtf8Hex,
  listFetchedUrls,
  stubFetchRoutes,
} from './fixtures/contentFixtures';

jest.mock('../../../clients/hashClient', () => ({
  hashTextSha256: async (text: string) =>
    require('crypto').createHash('sha256').update(Buffer.from(text, 'utf8')).digest('hex'),
}));

const EASY_URL = `${CONTENT_BASE_URL}python/easy.json`;
const MEDIUM_URL = `${CONTENT_BASE_URL}python/medium.json`;
const NEW_EASY_TEXT = buildBankText(['py-easy-new-1', 'py-easy-new-2']);
const NEW_MEDIUM_TEXT = buildBankText(['py-medium-new-1', 'py-medium-new-2']);
const NEW_EASY_HASH = hashUtf8Hex(NEW_EASY_TEXT);
const NEW_MEDIUM_HASH = hashUtf8Hex(NEW_MEDIUM_TEXT);
const OLD_MEDIUM_HASH = hashUtf8Hex(buildBankText(['py-medium-old-1']));

let queryClient: QueryClient;

function findPython(manifest: Manifest) {
  return manifest.languages.find(({ id }) => id === 'python')!;
}

const BUNDLED_EASY_HASH = findPython(cloneBundledManifest()).banks.easy!.hash;

// The python track alone, with the given Easy and Medium hashes, so any fetch the prefetch makes
// is one of python's three banks.
function buildPythonManifest(hashes: { easy: string; medium: string }): Manifest {
  const manifest = cloneBundledManifest();
  const python = findPython(manifest);
  python.banks.easy = { ...python.banks.easy!, hash: hashes.easy };
  python.banks.medium = { ...python.banks.medium!, hash: hashes.medium };
  return { ...manifest, languages: [python] };
}

function buildLocalBank(hash: string): CachedBank {
  return { hash, questions: ['local-1', 'local-2'].map(buildBoolQuestion) as Question[] };
}

// The device's local copies by `language/difficulty`. A bank that is neither cached nor bundled
// reads as null, as it does in ContentProvider.
function prefetch(manifest: Manifest, localBanks: Record<string, CachedBank>): void {
  const access: ContentAccess = {
    baselineManifest: manifest,
    contentBaseUrl: CONTENT_BASE_URL,
    readLocalBank: (language, difficulty) => localBanks[`${language}/${difficulty}`] ?? null,
  };
  queryClient.setQueryData(['manifest'], manifest);
  prefetchChangedBanks(queryClient, manifest, access);
}

describe('prefetchChangedBanks before a bank is first used', () => {
  beforeEach(async () => {
    await AsyncStorage.clear();
    queryClient = createQueryClient();
    jest.spyOn(console, 'warn').mockImplementation(() => {});
  });

  afterEach(async () => {
    await settle();
    queryClient.clear();
    jest.restoreAllMocks();
  });

  it('does not fetch a Medium bank the device has never opened', async () => {
    stubFetchRoutes({});
    const manifest = buildPythonManifest({ easy: BUNDLED_EASY_HASH, medium: NEW_MEDIUM_HASH });

    prefetch(manifest, { 'python/easy': buildLocalBank(BUNDLED_EASY_HASH) });
    await settle();

    expect(countFetchesFor(MEDIUM_URL)).toBe(0);
    expect(listFetchedUrls()).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('fetches a cached Medium bank again when its manifest hash changed', async () => {
    stubFetchRoutes({ [MEDIUM_URL]: async () => NEW_MEDIUM_TEXT });
    const manifest = buildPythonManifest({ easy: BUNDLED_EASY_HASH, medium: NEW_MEDIUM_HASH });

    prefetch(manifest, {
      'python/easy': buildLocalBank(BUNDLED_EASY_HASH),
      'python/medium': buildLocalBank(OLD_MEDIUM_HASH),
    });

    await waitFor(() => expect(countFetchesFor(MEDIUM_URL)).toBe(1));
    expect(countFetchesFor(EASY_URL)).toBe(0);
  });

  it('fetches the bundled Easy bank again when its manifest hash changed', async () => {
    stubFetchRoutes({ [EASY_URL]: async () => NEW_EASY_TEXT });
    const manifest = buildPythonManifest({ easy: NEW_EASY_HASH, medium: NEW_MEDIUM_HASH });

    prefetch(manifest, { 'python/easy': buildLocalBank(BUNDLED_EASY_HASH) });

    await waitFor(() => expect(countFetchesFor(EASY_URL)).toBe(1));
  });
});
```

- [ ] **Step 1: Replace `state/useQuestionBank.ts`**

```ts
// One bank's load state. A local copy (cached or bundled) whose hash
// matches the manifest is used directly; otherwise the bank downloads from
// the content host, keyed by its hash so overlapping requests share one
// fetch. Only Easy banks are bundled, so a Medium or Hard bank with no cached
// copy is loading while it downloads and an error with Retry when it fails.
import type { BankEntry, CachedBank } from '@syntactical/content-schema';
import { useQuery, useQueryClient } from '@tanstack/react-query';

import { buildBankQuery } from '../services/content/buildBankQuery';
import { findBankEntry } from '../services/content/findBankEntry';

import { useContentContext } from './ContentProvider';
import { useLanguageManifest } from './useLanguageManifest';

export type QuestionBankState =
  | { bank: CachedBank; status: 'ready' }
  | { status: 'loading' }
  | { retry: () => void; status: 'error' }
  | { status: 'unknown' };

const PLACEHOLDER_ENTRY: BankEntry = {
  contentVersion: 0,
  hash: 'none',
  path: '',
  topicCounts: {},
};

export function useQuestionBank(language: string, difficulty: string): QuestionBankState {
  const queryClient = useQueryClient();
  const access = useContentContext();
  const manifest = useLanguageManifest();
  const entry = findBankEntry(manifest, language, difficulty);
  const localBank = access.readLocalBank(language, difficulty);
  const needsDownload = entry !== undefined && localBank?.hash !== entry.hash;
  const query = useQuery({
    ...buildBankQuery(queryClient, access, language, difficulty, entry ?? PLACEHOLDER_ENTRY),
    enabled: needsDownload && access.contentBaseUrl !== null,
  });
  const { data, isError } = query;
  if (!entry) return { status: 'unknown' };
  if (needsDownload && data) return { bank: data, status: 'ready' };
  if (localBank) return { bank: localBank, status: 'ready' };
  if (isError) return { retry: () => void query.refetch(), status: 'error' };
  return { status: 'loading' };
}
```

```ts
export function buildBankQuery(
  queryClient: QueryClient,
  access: ContentAccess,
  language: string,
  difficulty: string,
  entry: BankEntry,
) {
  const { contentBaseUrl } = access;
  const { hash: entryHash } = entry;
  return {
    enabled: contentBaseUrl !== null,
    queryFn: () => {
      if (contentBaseUrl === null) return Promise.reject(new Error('no content base URL'));
      const context = readBankContext(queryClient, access, language);
      if (context === null) return Promise.reject(new Error(`no manifest entry for ${language}`));
      return loadQuestionBank({
        contentBaseUrl,
        context,
        difficulty,
        entry,
        isHashCurrent: (hash: string) => readCurrentHash(queryClient, access, language, difficulty) === hash,
        language,
      });
    },
    queryKey: ['bank', language, difficulty, entryHash],
  };
}
```

```ts
// Area 2: the API starts from one public content directory holding every bank, with no
// PAID_CONTENT_DIR. The paid bank route is gone (404, not 401), and a Medium bank whose bytes do
// not match the manifest still refuses the start. Every secret is generated at run time.
import { createHash, randomBytes } from 'node:crypto';
import { mkdir, mkdtemp, rm, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
import { dirname, join } from 'node:path';

import { SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION } from '@syntactical/content-schema';
import { pino } from 'pino';
import { afterAll, afterEach, beforeAll, beforeEach, describe, expect, inject, it } from 'vitest';

import { startServer } from '../startServer.js';
import type { RunningServer } from '../startServer.js';

import { createMigratedDatabase } from './integration/createMigratedDatabase.js';
import { SKIP_DATABASE_TESTS } from './integration/skipDatabaseTests.js';

const SETUP_TIMEOUT_MS = 120_000;
const SECRET_BYTES = 24;
const HTTP_OK = 200;
const HTTP_NOT_FOUND = 404;
const DIFFICULTIES = ['easy', 'medium', 'hard'] as const;
const PROVENANCE = { isHumanReviewed: false, source: 'original', validation: { method: 'judged', status: 'pending' } };

function serializeBank(id: string): Buffer {
  const question = {
    answerIndex: 1,
    choices: [{ text: 'one' }, { text: 'two' }, { text: 'three' }],
    id,
    prompt: 'A prompt',
    provenance: PROVENANCE,
    query: { explanation: 'Because.', title: 'A rule' },
    type: 'mc',
  };
  return Buffer.from(`${JSON.stringify({ questions: [question], schemaVersion: SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION })}\n`, 'utf8');
}

function sha256Hex(bytes: Buffer): string {
  return createHash('sha256').update(bytes).digest('hex');
}

async function writeUnder(root: string, relativePath: string, bytes: Buffer | string): Promise<void> {
  const file = join(root, relativePath);
  await mkdir(dirname(file), { recursive: true });
  await writeFile(file, bytes);
}

// Every bank in the one public directory; the manifest carries no access or productId.
async function writePublicContent(contentDir: string): Promise<void> {
  const banks: Record<string, unknown> = {};
  for (const difficulty of DIFFICULTIES) {
    const bytes = serializeBank(`py-${difficulty}-1`);
    const path = `python/${difficulty}.json`;
    await writeUnder(contentDir, path, bytes);
    banks[difficulty] = { contentVersion: 1, hash: sha256Hex(bytes), path, topicCounts: {} };
  }
  const language = {
    banks,
    glyph: 'PY',
    grammar: 'python',
    id: 'python',
    label: 'Python',
    misconceptions: [],
    tagline: 'Tagline.',
    topics: [],
  };
  await writeUnder(
    contentDir,
    'manifest.json',
    JSON.stringify({ languages: [language], schemaVersion: SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION }),
  );
}
```

```ts
// server/src/__tests__/routes/askAllBanks.integration.test.ts
// Area 2: POST /v1/ask finds a Medium or Hard question in the index readServerQuestions builds from
// the one public content directory, and answers it for a user with any granted entitlement. There
// is no paidBanks dependency and no per-bank gate (area 3 replaces the remaining gate with Pro).
// The model is a fake that records each prompt.
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
import { mkdir, mkdtemp, rm, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
import { dirname, join } from 'node:path';

import { SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION } from '@syntactical/content-schema';
import request from 'supertest';
import { afterAll, afterEach, beforeAll, beforeEach, describe, expect, inject, it } from 'vitest';

import { readServerQuestions } from '../../services/readServerQuestions.js';
import { createFakeModelProvider } from '../../testing/fakeModelProvider.js';
import { createMigratedDatabase } from '../integration/createMigratedDatabase.js';
import { createTestApp } from '../integration/createTestApp.js';
import { insertSession } from '../integration/insertSession.js';
import { SKIP_DATABASE_TESTS } from '../integration/skipDatabaseTests.js';

const SETUP_TIMEOUT_MS = 120_000;
const ALLOWED_ORIGIN = 'https://syntactical.dev';
const ANY_PRODUCT = 'syntactical.go.medium';
const MESSAGE = 'Why is this the answer?';
const DIFFICULTIES = ['easy', 'medium', 'hard'] as const;
const PROVENANCE = { isHumanReviewed: true, source: 'original', validation: { method: 'judged', status: 'passed' } };

let database: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof createMigratedDatabase>>;
let contentDir: string;

function serializeBank(difficulty: string): Buffer {
  const question = {
    answerIndex: 0,
    choices: [{ text: 'yes' }, { text: 'no' }],
    id: `py-${difficulty}-0`,
    prompt: 'Is this so?',
    provenance: PROVENANCE,
    query: { explanation: `${difficulty}-explanation-marker`, title: 'A rule' },
    type: 'mc',
  };
  return Buffer.from(JSON.stringify({ questions: [question], schemaVersion: SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION }), 'utf8');
}

async function writeUnder(relativePath: string, bytes: Buffer | string): Promise<void> {
  const file = join(contentDir, relativePath);
  await mkdir(dirname(file), { recursive: true });
  await writeFile(file, bytes);
}

async function writePublicContent(): Promise<void> {
  const banks: Record<string, unknown> = {};
  for (const difficulty of DIFFICULTIES) {
    const bytes = serializeBank(difficulty);
    const path = `python/${difficulty}.json`;
    await writeUnder(path, bytes);
    banks[difficulty] = {
      contentVersion: 1,
      hash: createHash('sha256').update(bytes).digest('hex'),
      path,
      topicCounts: {},
    };
  }
  const language = {
    banks,
    glyph: 'PY',
    grammar: 'python',
    id: 'python',
    label: 'Python',
    misconceptions: [],
    tagline: 'Tagline.',
    topics: [],
  };
  await writeUnder('manifest.json', JSON.stringify({ languages: [language], schemaVersion: SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION }));
}

async function signInEntitled() {
  const model = createFakeModelProvider();
  const questions = await readServerQuestions(contentDir);
  const { app, clock } = createTestApp({ ask: { modelProvider: model, questions }, pool: database.pool });
  const { sessionToken, userId } = await insertSession(database.pool, { createdAt: clock.now() });
  await database.pool.query('INSERT INTO entitlements (user_id, product_id, status, source) VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4)', [
    userId,
    ANY_PRODUCT,
    'granted',
    'test',
  ]);
  return { app, model, sessionToken };
}

    expect([...questions.keys()].sort()).toEqual(['python/easy', 'python/hard', 'python/medium']);
  });

  it.each(['medium', 'hard'])('answers a %s question for a user with any granted entitlement', async (difficulty) => {
    const { app, model, sessionToken } = await signInEntitled();

    const response = await request(app)
      .post('/v1/ask')
      .set('Authorization', `Bearer ${sessionToken}`)
      .set('Origin', ALLOWED_ORIGIN)
      .send({ bankKey: `python/${difficulty}`, message: MESSAGE, questionId: `py-${difficulty}-0` });

    expect(response.status).toBe(200);
    expect(model.prompts[0]?.user).toContain(`${difficulty}-explanation-marker`);
  });
});
```

```ts
// Loads every bank's validated questions from the content directory's manifest and bank files,
// checked against the manifest hash. A bank the manifest lists but the directory lacks is skipped;
// the image build (copyContent.mjs) refuses to ship one.
import { buildBankContext, validateQuestionBank } from '@syntactical/content-schema';
import type { BankEntry, LanguageEntry, Question } from '@syntactical/content-schema';

import type { QuestionIndex } from '../types/QuestionIndex.js';

import { readBankBytes } from './readBankBytes.js';
import { readManifest } from './readManifest.js';
import { sha256 } from './sha256.js';

async function readBank(
  contentDir: string,
  language: LanguageEntry,
  entry: BankEntry,
): Promise<Map<string, Question> | null> {
  const { hash, path } = entry;
  const bytes = await readBankBytes(contentDir, entry);
  if (bytes === null) return null;
  if (sha256(bytes).toString('hex') !== hash) {
    throw new Error(`Bank hash mismatch: ${path}`);
  }
  const validation = validateQuestionBank(JSON.parse(bytes.toString('utf8')) as unknown, buildBankContext(language));
  if ('rule' in validation) throw new Error(`Invalid bank ${path}: ${validation.rule}`);
  const { questions } = validation;
  return new Map(questions.map((question) => [question.id, question]));
}

async function readServerQuestions(contentDir: string): Promise<QuestionIndex> {
  const manifest = await readManifest(contentDir);
  const index = new Map<string, ReadonlyMap<string, Question>>();
  for (const language of manifest.languages) {
    const { banks, id } = language;
    for (const [difficulty, entry] of Object.entries(banks)) {
      const bank = await readBank(contentDir, language, entry);
      if (bank) index.set(`${id}/${difficulty}`, bank);
    }
  }
  return index;
}

export { readServerQuestions };
```

`server/src/services/readBankBytes.ts`:

```ts
// Reads one manifest bank's exact bytes from a root directory, refusing an unsafe path; null when
// the file is absent.
import { readFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { join } from 'node:path';

import { isSafeBankPath } from '@syntactical/content-schema';
import type { BankEntry } from '@syntactical/content-schema';

async function readBankBytes(root: string, { path }: BankEntry): Promise<Buffer | null> {
  if (!isSafeBankPath(path)) throw new Error(`Unsafe bank path: ${path}`);
  try {
    return await readFile(join(root, path));
  } catch (error) {
    if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === 'ENOENT') return null;
    throw error;
  }
}

export { readBankBytes };
```

```ts
// Pins that the clock createTestApp returns is the one every mounted session-guarded router
// reads (PR #186 review, r1 #1): a session live at the clock's start answers 200 on the admin and
// sync routes, and 401 on both once the clock advances past the idle TTL. The webhook router
// takes no clock, so it has nothing to pin here.
import request from 'supertest';
import { afterAll, beforeAll, describe, expect, inject, it } from 'vitest';

import { AUTH } from '../../constants/auth.js';
import { getAccess, signInUser } from './adminAccessRequests.js';
import { createMigratedDatabase } from './createMigratedDatabase.js';
import { createTestApp } from './createTestApp.js';
import { SKIP_DATABASE_TESTS } from './skipDatabaseTests.js';

const HTTP_OK = 200;
const HTTP_UNAUTHORIZED = 401;
const SETUP_TIMEOUT_MS = 120_000;
const DAY_MS = 86_400_000;
const ALLOWED_ORIGIN = 'https://syntactical.dev';
const PRODUCT_ID = 'syntactical.python.medium';
const ME_ROUTE = '/v1/me';

let database: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof createMigratedDatabase>>;

describe.skipIf(SKIP_DATABASE_TESTS)('createTestApp clock', () => {
  beforeAll(async () => {
    database = await createMigratedDatabase(inject('testDatabaseUrl'));
  }, SETUP_TIMEOUT_MS);

  afterAll(async () => {
    await database.drop();
  });

  it('expires a session on every mounted session-guarded router once the clock advances', async () => {
    const paidProductIds: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set([PRODUCT_ID]);
    const { app, clock } = createTestApp({
      admin: { paidProductIds },
      pool: database.pool,
      sync: { answerKey: new Map() },
    });
    const admin = await signInUser(database.pool, clock.now(), true);
    const getWithBearer = (path: string) =>
      request(app).get(path).set('Authorization', `Bearer ${admin.sessionToken}`).set('Origin', ALLOWED_ORIGIN);
    async function statuses(): Promise<{ admin: number; me: number }> {
      return {
        admin: (await getAccess(app, admin)).status,
        me: (await getWithBearer(ME_ROUTE)).status,
      };
    }

    const live = await statuses();
    clock.advance(AUTH.SESSION.IDLE_TTL_MS + DAY_MS);
    const expired = await statuses();

    expect(live).toEqual({ admin: HTTP_OK, me: HTTP_OK });
    expect(expired).toEqual({ admin: HTTP_UNAUTHORIZED, me: HTTP_UNAUTHORIZED });
  });
});
```

```ts
// The app with the /v1/admin routes wired to a real database for one integration test, mounted
// beside the routes an admin grant must reach: the /v1 sync routes (GET /v1/me) and the
// RevenueCat webhook. One injectable clock serves every router, and the rate-limit key secret
// and webhook authorization value are generated at run time. The product ids handed to the admin
// and webhook routes are two legacy per-bank ids, as startServer passes LEGACY_PAID_PRODUCT_IDS.
import type pg from 'pg';

import { createTestApp } from './createTestApp.js';
import type { AnswerKey } from '../../types/AnswerKey.js';

export const ADMIN_TEST_PRODUCTS = {
  HARD: 'syntactical.python.hard',
  MEDIUM: 'syntactical.python.medium',
} as const;

interface AdminTestAppOptions {
  pool: pg.Pool;
}

export function createAdminTestApp(options: AdminTestAppOptions) {
  const { pool } = options;
  const paidProductIds: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set(Object.values(ADMIN_TEST_PRODUCTS));
  const answerKey: AnswerKey = new Map();
  const { app, clock, rateLimitKeySecret, revenueCatAuth } = createTestApp({
    admin: { paidProductIds },
    pool,
    sync: { answerKey },
    webhooks: { paidProductIds },
  });
  return { app, clock, paidProductIds, rateLimitKeySecret, revenueCatAuth };
}
```

```ts
// copyContent.mjs gates what the API image ships: every bank the manifest lists must match its
// hash, a manifest path must stay inside the source, nothing the manifest does not name is copied,
// and the manifest itself is copied. stageBuildContent.sh stages build/content alone, from this
// repository's content or the CI fixture, and refuses the retired private mode.
import { execFileSync, spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
import { cpSync, existsSync, mkdirSync, mkdtempSync, readdirSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';

import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';

const serverDir = fileURLToPath(new URL('../../../', import.meta.url));
const copyScript = join(serverDir, 'scripts', 'copyContent.mjs');
const stageScript = join(serverDir, 'scripts', 'stageBuildContent.sh');
const fixtureDir = join(serverDir, 'ci-fixture');

let work: string;

beforeEach(() => {
  work = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'copy-content-test-'));
});
afterEach(() => {
  rmSync(work, { force: true, recursive: true });
});

function sha256(text: string): string {
  return createHash('sha256').update(text).digest('hex');
}

function writeManifest(entries: Record<string, { hash: string; path: string }>): string {
  const manifestPath = join(work, 'manifest.json');
  writeFileSync(manifestPath, JSON.stringify({ languages: [{ banks: entries }] }));
  return manifestPath;
}

function runCopy(manifestPath: string) {
  return spawnSync('node', [copyScript, manifestPath, join(work, 'from'), join(work, 'to')], { encoding: 'utf8' });
}

function writeSource(path: string, text: string): void {
  const file = join(work, 'from', path);
  mkdirSync(join(file, '..'), { recursive: true });
  writeFileSync(file, text);
}

function listFiles(dir: string): string[] {
  return readdirSync(dir, { recursive: true, withFileTypes: true })
    .filter((entry) => entry.isFile())
    .map((entry) => join(entry.parentPath, entry.name).slice(dir.length))
    .sort();
}

function copyStageInputs(): void {
  mkdirSync(join(work, 'server', 'scripts'), { recursive: true });
  cpSync(copyScript, join(work, 'server', 'scripts', 'copyContent.mjs'));
  cpSync(stageScript, join(work, 'server', 'scripts', 'stageBuildContent.sh'));
}

  it('copies every bank the manifest lists, Easy, Medium, and Hard, and the manifest', () => {
    writeSource('python/easy.json', '{"e":1}');
    writeSource('python/medium.json', '{"m":1}');
    writeSource('python/hard.json', '{"h":1}');
    const manifest = writeManifest({
      easy: { hash: sha256('{"e":1}'), path: 'python/easy.json' },
      hard: { hash: sha256('{"h":1}'), path: 'python/hard.json' },
      medium: { hash: sha256('{"m":1}'), path: 'python/medium.json' },
    });

    const result = runCopy(manifest);

    expect(result.status).toBe(0);
    expect(listFiles(join(work, 'to'))).toEqual([
      '/manifest.json',
      '/python/easy.json',
      '/python/hard.json',
      '/python/medium.json',
    ]);
  });

  it('fails naming a bank the manifest lists but the source lacks', () => {
    writeSource('python/easy.json', 'x');
    const manifest = writeManifest({
      easy: { hash: sha256('x'), path: 'python/easy.json' },
      medium: { hash: sha256('y'), path: 'python/medium.json' },
    });

    const result = runCopy(manifest);

    expect(result.status).toBe(1);
    expect(result.stderr).toContain('bank missing: python/medium.json');
  });

  it('fails with a hash mismatch when the bytes were tampered with', () => {
    writeSource('python/easy.json', '{"ok":2}');
    const manifest = writeManifest({ easy: { hash: sha256('{"ok":1}'), path: 'python/easy.json' } });

    const result = runCopy(manifest);

    expect(result.status).toBe(1);
    expect(result.stderr).toContain('hash mismatch');
    expect(existsSync(join(work, 'to', 'python', 'easy.json'))).toBe(false);
  });

  it.each(['../escape.json', '/etc/passwd', 'a/../../escape.json', 'a\\b.json'])(
    'rejects the manifest path %s',
    (path) => {
      writeSource('python/easy.json', 'x');
      const manifest = writeManifest({ easy: { hash: sha256('x'), path } });

      const result = runCopy(manifest);

      expect(result.status).toBe(1);
      expect(result.stderr).toContain('unsafe bank path');
    },
  );

  it('does not copy a file the manifest does not name', () => {
    writeSource('python/easy.json', 'x');
    writeSource('python/extra.json', 'not in the manifest');
    writeSource('.git/config', 'git internals');
    const manifest = writeManifest({ easy: { hash: sha256('x'), path: 'python/easy.json' } });

    const result = runCopy(manifest);

    expect(result.status).toBe(0);
    expect(readdirSync(join(work, 'to', 'python'))).toEqual(['easy.json']);
    expect(existsSync(join(work, 'to', '.git'))).toBe(false);
  });
});
```
