- [ ] **Step 1: Replace `server/scripts/copyContent.mjs`**

```js
// Copies the manifest and every bank it lists, and nothing else, out of a content directory for the
// server image. Used by server/scripts/stageBuildContent.sh and server/Dockerfile.
//
//   node copyContent.mjs <manifest.json> <fromDir> <toDir>
//
// Every bank the manifest lists must exist under fromDir and match the manifest hash, or the build
// fails here rather than the server skipping it at startup. Files outside the manifest (a .git
// directory, notes, stray banks) are never copied.
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
import { copyFileSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { dirname, join, posix } from 'node:path';

const [manifestPath, fromDir, toDir] = process.argv.slice(2);
if (!manifestPath || !fromDir || !toDir) {
  console.error('usage: copyContent.mjs <manifest.json> <fromDir> <toDir>');
  process.exit(2);
}

function fail(message) {
  console.error(`copyContent: ${message}`);
  process.exit(1);
}

function isSafeRelativePath(path) {
  return (
    typeof path === 'string' &&
    path.length > 0 &&
    !path.startsWith('/') &&
    !path.includes('\\') &&
    posix.normalize(path) === path &&
    !path.split('/').includes('..')
  );
}

const manifest = JSON.parse(readFileSync(manifestPath, 'utf8'));
const entries = manifest.languages.flatMap(({ banks }) => Object.values(banks));
if (entries.length === 0) {
  fail('the manifest lists no banks');
}

for (const { hash, path } of entries) {
  if (!isSafeRelativePath(path)) {
    fail(`unsafe bank path ${path}`);
  }
  let bytes;
  try {
    bytes = readFileSync(join(fromDir, path));
  } catch {
    fail(`bank missing: ${path}`);
  }
  if (createHash('sha256').update(bytes).digest('hex') !== hash) {
    fail(`bank hash mismatch: ${path}`);
  }
  const target = join(toDir, path);
  mkdirSync(dirname(target), { recursive: true });
  copyFileSync(join(fromDir, path), target);
}

mkdirSync(toDir, { recursive: true });
copyFileSync(manifestPath, join(toDir, 'manifest.json'));
console.log(`copyContent: copied ${entries.length} bank(s) and the manifest`);
```

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Stages the content the API image bakes in, under <repo>/build/content, which server/Dockerfile
# copies. Every bank is public, so no key and no second repository are involved.
#
#   server/scripts/stageBuildContent.sh public    this repository's content/ (deploys and CI)
#   server/scripts/stageBuildContent.sh fixture   the tiny content set under server/ci-fixture/public
#
# Only the manifest and the banks it names are copied, each bank checked against its manifest hash.
set -euo pipefail

mode="${1:?usage: stageBuildContent.sh <public|fixture>}"
root="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." && pwd)"
out="$root/build"
copy="$root/server/scripts/copyContent.mjs"

case "$mode" in
  public) source_dir="$root/content" ;;
  fixture) source_dir="$root/server/ci-fixture/public" ;;
  *)
    echo "stageBuildContent: unknown mode '$mode' (expected public or fixture)" >&2
    exit 2
    ;;
esac

rm -rf "${out:?}/content" "${out:?}/paid-content"
mkdir -p "$out"
node "$copy" "$source_dir/manifest.json" "$source_dir" "$out/content"
echo "stageBuildContent: staged $mode content under build/content"
```

- Produces: `writeFixtureContent(options: { contentSource: string; publicDir: string }): Promise<void>`, copying the manifest and every bank it lists unchanged; `E2eState` without `paidContentDir`; the e2e API runs without `PAID_CONTENT_DIR`.

- [ ] **Step 1: Replace `e2e/support/writeFixtureContent.ts`**

```ts
// Builds the content the e2e run serves: one public directory holding the repository's manifest and
// every bank it lists, Easy, Medium, and Hard, copied unchanged, so the web bundle's bundled Easy
// banks and the served manifest's hashes match. The API reads it and the web host serves it.
import { cp, mkdir, readFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { dirname, join } from 'node:path';

interface Manifest {
  languages: Array<{ banks: Record<string, { path: string }> }>;
}

async function copyUnder(contentSource: string, publicDir: string, path: string): Promise<void> {
  await mkdir(dirname(join(publicDir, path)), { recursive: true });
  await cp(join(contentSource, path), join(publicDir, path));
}

async function writeFixtureContent(options: { contentSource: string; publicDir: string }): Promise<void> {
  const { contentSource, publicDir } = options;
  const manifest = JSON.parse(await readFile(join(contentSource, 'manifest.json'), 'utf8')) as Manifest;
  for (const language of manifest.languages) {
    for (const { path } of Object.values(language.banks)) await copyUnder(contentSource, publicDir, path);
  }
  await copyUnder(contentSource, publicDir, 'manifest.json');
}

export { writeFixtureContent };
```

```ts
test('a Medium bank cached by its first use still plays when the API and the content host refuse it', async ({
  page,
}) => {
  await signIn(page, createUniqueEmail());

  // First use, with the API and the content host up. Nothing prefetches a bank the device has
  // never opened, so this visit is what downloads the Medium bank and caches it on the device.
  const mediumDownload = page.waitForResponse((response) => response.url().endsWith(MEDIUM_BANK_PATH) && response.ok());
  await page.goto('python');
  await expect(page.getByText('Step 2 / Select difficulty')).toBeVisible();
  await mediumDownload;
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /^Medium/ }).click();
  await pickAllQuestions(page);
  await answerQuestions(page, 1);
  await page.keyboard.press('Escape');

  // The API is down and the content host refuses the Medium bank: only the cached copy is left.
  await page.route(API_PATTERN, (route) => route.abort('connectionrefused'));
  await page.route(MEDIUM_BANK_PATTERN, (route) => route.abort('connectionrefused'));
  await page.goto('python');
  await expect(page.getByText('Step 2 / Select difficulty')).toBeVisible();
  const medium = page.getByRole('button', { name: /^Medium/ });
  await expect(medium).toBeEnabled();
  await medium.click();
  await pickAllQuestions(page);
  await answerQuestions(page, 2);
  await page.keyboard.press('Escape');

  // The account page still opens, and a delete attempt fails with a message and changes nothing.
  await page.goto('settings');
  await page.getByRole('button', { exact: true, name: 'Delete account' }).click();
  const dialog = page.getByRole('dialog', { name: 'Delete account' });
  await dialog.getByLabel('Type DELETE to confirm').fill('DELETE');
  await dialog.getByRole('button', { name: 'Delete my account' }).click();
  await expect(dialog.getByRole('alert')).toContainText('could not be deleted');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Cancel' }).click();
  await expect(page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Sign out' }).first()).toBeVisible();

  // When both are back, no difficulty reports a failed download.
  await page.unroute(API_PATTERN);
  await page.unroute(MEDIUM_BANK_PATTERN);
  await page.goto('python');
  await expect(page.getByRole('button', { name: /^Medium/ })).toBeEnabled();
  await expect(page.getByText('Download failed. Tap to retry')).toHaveCount(0);
});
```

`server/src/constants/proProducts.ts`:

```ts
// The two Pro products (spec "2. Pro"): an auto-renewing annual subscription, whose entitlement row
// carries expires_at, and a lifetime non-consumable, whose row never expires. Both fit the app's
// PRODUCT_ID_PATTERN. The webhook, hasPro, the profile, and the admin toggle match these exactly.
// RevenueCat reports a Google Play subscription as `<subscription id>:<base plan id>` (the annual
// arrives as `syntactical.pro.annual:yearly`), so the webhook normalises an id before matching it.
const PRO_PRODUCT_IDS = {
  ANNUAL: 'syntactical.pro.annual',
  LIFETIME: 'syntactical.pro.lifetime',
} as const;

const PRO_PRODUCT_ID_LIST = [PRO_PRODUCT_IDS.ANNUAL, PRO_PRODUCT_IDS.LIFETIME] as const;

// Exactly one colon, a store id before it and a base plan id after it. Anything else is left as is.
const PLAY_BASE_PLAN_ID_PATTERN = /^[a-z0-9.]+:[a-z0-9-]+$/;

type ProProductId = (typeof PRO_PRODUCT_ID_LIST)[number];

// The subscription id of a Play `<subscription id>:<base plan id>`; any other id unchanged.
function normalizeProductId(productId: string): string {
  if (!PLAY_BASE_PLAN_ID_PATTERN.test(productId)) {
    return productId;
  }
  return productId.slice(0, productId.indexOf(':'));
}

export { normalizeProductId, PRO_PRODUCT_ID_LIST, PRO_PRODUCT_IDS };
export type { ProProductId };
```

`server/migrations/1790985600018_entitlements-expires-at.js`:

```js
/**
 * When a Pro entitlement ends: the annual subscription's current period end, from RevenueCat's
 * expiration_at_ms. NULL for the lifetime product, for admin grants, and for rows written before
 * Pro. hasPro counts a granted row only while expires_at is NULL or later than now.
 *
 * @param {import('node-pg-migrate').MigrationBuilder} pgm
 */
export const up = (pgm) => {
  pgm.addColumn('entitlements', {
    expires_at: { type: 'timestamptz' },
  });
};
```

```ts
// Sets the (user, product) entitlement from the latest grant or revoke event by occurred_at
// among the stores that can change it; a revoke wins a tie. On the annual Pro product CANCELLATION
// is expiry-only and never changes the status; on any other product it revokes. The row is
// written with source 'revenuecat' only when the status differs, so a redelivery leaves
// updated_at untouched. Callers hold the (user, product) advisory lock so the read sees every
// committed event.
import type pg from 'pg';

import { PRO_PRODUCT_IDS } from '../constants/proProducts.js';
import { REVENUECAT_EVENTS } from '../constants/revenueCatEvents.js';

const { ENTITLEMENT_SOURCE, EXPIRY_ONLY_TYPES, GRANT_TYPES, PROVIDER, REVOKE_TYPES, STORES } = REVENUECAT_EVENTS;

// The event types that revoke this product: CANCELLATION too, except on the annual subscription.
function revokeTypesFor(productId: string): string[] {
  return productId === PRO_PRODUCT_IDS.ANNUAL ? [...REVOKE_TYPES] : [...REVOKE_TYPES, ...EXPIRY_ONLY_TYPES];
}

async function recomputeEntitlement(client: pg.PoolClient, userId: string, productId: string): Promise<void> {
  const revokeTypes = revokeTypesFor(productId);
  const { rows } = await client.query<{ status: string }>(
    `SELECT CASE WHEN kind = ANY($3::text[]) THEN 'revoked' ELSE 'granted' END AS status
     FROM purchase_events
     WHERE provider = $4 AND user_id = $1 AND product_id = $2
       AND kind = ANY($5::text[])
       AND payload->>'store' = ANY($6::text[])
     ORDER BY occurred_at DESC, (kind = ANY($3::text[])) DESC
     LIMIT 1`,
    [userId, productId, revokeTypes, PROVIDER, [...GRANT_TYPES, ...revokeTypes], [...STORES]],
  );
  const [latest] = rows;
  if (!latest) {
    return;
  }
  await client.query(
    `INSERT INTO entitlements (user_id, product_id, source, status)
     VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4)
     ON CONFLICT (user_id, product_id) DO UPDATE SET source = EXCLUDED.source, status = EXCLUDED.status
     WHERE entitlements.status IS DISTINCT FROM EXCLUDED.status
        OR entitlements.source IS DISTINCT FROM EXCLUDED.source`,
    [userId, productId, ENTITLEMENT_SOURCE, latest.status],
  );
}

export { recomputeEntitlement };
```

### Task 3.4: `expires_at` from the webhook, with annual and lifetime independent

**Files:**

- Modify: `server/src/services/recomputeEntitlement.ts` (whole file as left by Task 3.3)
- Modify: `server/src/services/recordPurchaseEvent.ts` (header, the `proProducts.js` import, and the `if (!isProProduct)` block, as left by Task 3.1)
- Test: `server/src/__tests__/routes/revenueCatWebhookProExpiry.integration.test.ts` (new)

**Interfaces:**

- Behaviour: while the row is `granted`, `expires_at` is `to_timestamp(expiration_at_ms / 1000)` of the latest grant or expiry-only event by `occurred_at`; a lifetime `NON_RENEWING_PURCHASE` carries none, so the lifetime row keeps `expires_at` NULL. A revoke leaves `expires_at` as it was.
- Fail closed on the annual product: a grant event (`INITIAL_PURCHASE`, `RENEWAL`, `UNCANCELLATION`, or any other grant type) on `syntactical.pro.annual` with no `expiration_at_ms` is recorded in `purchase_events` as usual (idempotency unchanged) and answered 200 `recorded`, but `recomputeEntitlement` ignores it for status and expiry, and `recordPurchaseEvent` logs one `warn` `{ productId, type }` with the message `annual grant without expiration ignored`. Annual events without `expiration_at_ms` are also skipped when picking the expiry, so a granted annual row never has a NULL `expires_at` (which would mean Pro forever). An expiry-only event never changes `status` and never creates a row. The `(user_id, product_id)` key keeps the annual and lifetime rows apart (Review Focus 1). A `RENEWAL` older than a recorded `EXPIRATION` neither re-grants nor moves `expires_at` (Review Focus 2).

```ts
    .set('Authorization', target.revenueCatAuth)
    .set('Content-Type', 'application/json')
    .send(JSON.stringify({ event: buildEvent({ app_user_id: target.userId, ...overrides }) }));
  expect(response.body).toEqual({ data: { status: 'recorded' } });
}

function annual(type: string, at: number, expirationAtMs?: number): Record<string, unknown> {
  return { event_timestamp_ms: at, expiration_at_ms: expirationAtMs, product_id: ANNUAL, type };
}

function lifetime(type: string, at: number): Record<string, unknown> {
  return { event_timestamp_ms: at, product_id: LIFETIME, type };
}

async function rowOf(userId: string, productId: string): Promise<RowState | undefined> {
  const { rows } = await database.pool.query<{ expires_at: Date | null; status: string }>(
    'SELECT status, expires_at FROM entitlements WHERE user_id = $1 AND product_id = $2',
    [userId, productId],
  );
  const [row] = rows;
  return row ? { expiresAtMs: row.expires_at?.getTime() ?? null, status: row.status } : undefined;
}
```

`server/src/services/recomputeEntitlement.ts`, replaced whole:

```ts
// Sets the (user, product) entitlement from the purchase events of the stores that can change it.
// Status: the latest grant or revoke event by occurred_at wins, a revoke winning a tie. On the
// annual Pro product CANCELLATION is expiry-only (auto-renew off, access continues) and never
// changes the status or creates a row; on any other product it revokes. Expiry: while granted,
// expires_at is the expiration_at_ms of the latest grant or expiry-only event; a revoke leaves
// expires_at as it was, so a RENEWAL stamped before a recorded EXPIRATION cannot move it. The
// lifetime product's events carry no expiration_at_ms, so its row keeps expires_at NULL. The
// annual product fails closed: an annual event without expiration_at_ms is ignored for status (a
// grant) and for expiry (any event), so a granted annual row never has a NULL expires_at, which
// would mean Pro forever; recordPurchaseEvent still records such an event and warns about it. The
// (user_id, product_id) key keeps the annual and lifetime rows independent. The row is written
// with source 'revenuecat' only when something differs, so a redelivery leaves updated_at
// untouched. Callers hold the (user, product) advisory lock so the reads see every committed event.
import type pg from 'pg';

import { PRO_PRODUCT_IDS } from '../constants/proProducts.js';
import { REVENUECAT_EVENTS } from '../constants/revenueCatEvents.js';

const { ENTITLEMENT_SOURCE, EXPIRY_ONLY_TYPES, GRANT_TYPES, PROVIDER, REVOKE_TYPES, STORES } = REVENUECAT_EVENTS;

type Status = 'granted' | 'revoked';

interface EventKinds {
  expiryOnly: string[];
  // True on the annual product: an event there counts only when it carries expiration_at_ms.
  requiresExpiry: boolean;
  revoke: string[];
}

function kindsFor(productId: string): EventKinds {
  if (productId === PRO_PRODUCT_IDS.ANNUAL) {
    return { expiryOnly: [...EXPIRY_ONLY_TYPES], requiresExpiry: true, revoke: [...REVOKE_TYPES] };
  }
  return { expiryOnly: [], requiresExpiry: false, revoke: [...REVOKE_TYPES, ...EXPIRY_ONLY_TYPES] };
}

// The latest grant or revoke wins. When requiresExpiry, a grant without expiration_at_ms is skipped;
// a revoke never needs one.
async function readStatus(
  client: pg.PoolClient,
  userId: string,
  productId: string,
  kinds: EventKinds,
): Promise<Status | undefined> {
  const { requiresExpiry, revoke } = kinds;
  const { rows } = await client.query<{ status: Status }>(
    `SELECT CASE WHEN kind = ANY($3::text[]) THEN 'revoked' ELSE 'granted' END AS status
     FROM purchase_events
     WHERE provider = $4 AND user_id = $1 AND product_id = $2
       AND kind = ANY($5::text[])
       AND payload->>'store' = ANY($6::text[])
       AND NOT ($7::boolean AND kind = ANY($8::text[]) AND payload->>'expiration_at_ms' IS NULL)
     ORDER BY occurred_at DESC, (kind = ANY($3::text[])) DESC
     LIMIT 1`,
    [userId, productId, revoke, PROVIDER, [...GRANT_TYPES, ...revoke], [...STORES], requiresExpiry, [...GRANT_TYPES]],
  );
  return rows[0]?.status;
}

// The latest grant or expiry-only event's expiration_at_ms, or null when it carries none (the
// lifetime product). When requiresExpiry, events without one are skipped, and the grant that made
// the row granted carries one, so the answer is never null. Only read while granted: the latest
// grant is then later than every revoke, so this event is too.
async function readExpiryMs(
  client: pg.PoolClient,
  userId: string,
  productId: string,
  kinds: EventKinds,
): Promise<number | null> {
  const { expiryOnly, requiresExpiry } = kinds;
  const { rows } = await client.query<{ expiration_at_ms: number | null }>(
    `SELECT (payload->>'expiration_at_ms')::double precision AS expiration_at_ms
     FROM purchase_events
     WHERE provider = $3 AND user_id = $1 AND product_id = $2
       AND kind = ANY($4::text[])
       AND payload->>'store' = ANY($5::text[])
       AND NOT ($6::boolean AND payload->>'expiration_at_ms' IS NULL)
     ORDER BY occurred_at DESC, (payload->>'expiration_at_ms')::double precision DESC NULLS LAST
     LIMIT 1`,
    [userId, productId, PROVIDER, [...GRANT_TYPES, ...expiryOnly], [...STORES], requiresExpiry],
  );
  return rows[0]?.expiration_at_ms ?? null;
}

async function recomputeEntitlement(client: pg.PoolClient, userId: string, productId: string): Promise<void> {
  const kinds = kindsFor(productId);
  const status = await readStatus(client, userId, productId, kinds);
  if (!status) {
    return;
  }
  const expiryMs = status === 'granted' ? await readExpiryMs(client, userId, productId, kinds) : null;
  await client.query(
    `INSERT INTO entitlements (user_id, product_id, source, status, expires_at)
     VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, to_timestamp($5::double precision / 1000))
     ON CONFLICT (user_id, product_id) DO UPDATE SET
       source = EXCLUDED.source,
       status = EXCLUDED.status,
       expires_at = CASE WHEN EXCLUDED.status = 'granted' THEN EXCLUDED.expires_at ELSE entitlements.expires_at END
     WHERE entitlements.status IS DISTINCT FROM EXCLUDED.status
        OR entitlements.source IS DISTINCT FROM EXCLUDED.source
        OR (EXCLUDED.status = 'granted' AND entitlements.expires_at IS DISTINCT FROM EXCLUDED.expires_at)`,
    [userId, productId, ENTITLEMENT_SOURCE, status, expiryMs],
  );
}

export { recomputeEntitlement };
```

node-pg parses `double precision` to a JavaScript number, and `to_timestamp(NULL / 1000)` is NULL, so a lifetime row (no expiry on its events) writes NULL. An annual row only reaches the upsert as `granted` through a grant that carries `expiration_at_ms`, so it never writes NULL while granted.

`server/src/services/hasPro.ts`:

```ts
// Whether a user has Pro at `now` (spec "2. Pro", Server): a granted entitlement row for either Pro
// product, from any source, whose expires_at is NULL (lifetime and admin grants) or later than
// `now` (an annual period still running). `now` is a parameter so expiry is testable without
// waiting. One parameterized query; any other row answers false.
import type { Database } from '../clients/database.js';
import { PRO_PRODUCT_ID_LIST } from '../constants/proProducts.js';

async function hasPro(database: Database, userId: string, now: Date): Promise<boolean> {
  const { rowCount } = await database.query(
    `SELECT 1 FROM entitlements
     WHERE user_id = $1 AND product_id = ANY($2::text[]) AND status = 'granted'
       AND (expires_at IS NULL OR expires_at > $3)
     LIMIT 1`,
    [userId, [...PRO_PRODUCT_ID_LIST], now],
  );
  return (rowCount ?? 0) > 0;
}

export { hasPro };
```

**Interfaces:**

- `PUT /v1/admin/access` body: `{ isGranted: boolean }`, strict (a `productId`, `userId`, or `isAdmin` field is 400 `INPUT_INVALID_BODY`). Answers `{ data: AdminProductEntry }`, the same entry GET reports after the write.
- `GET /v1/admin/access` answers `{ data: AdminProductEntry }` (one entry, no array).
- `AdminProductEntry` is unchanged: `{ grantSource: 'admin' | 'purchase' | null; isGranted: boolean; productId: string }`, with `productId` always `'syntactical.pro.lifetime'` and `isGranted` true exactly when `grantSource` is not null. `toAdminProductEntry(productId, grantedSource)` keeps its signature and file.
- `grantSource` rule (GET and PUT): `'purchase'` when the user has any `granted` `revenuecat`-source row on either Pro product that is active by the `hasPro` rule (`expires_at IS NULL OR expires_at > now`); else `'admin'` when the user's `admin`-source lifetime row is granted; else null.
- `listAdminAccess(queryable: Database | pg.PoolClient, userId: string, now: Date): Promise<AdminProductEntry>`.
- `setAdminAccess(database: Database, userId: string, isGranted: boolean, now: Date): Promise<AdminProductEntry | undefined>`; a grant writes `source 'admin'`, `status 'granted'`, `expires_at NULL` on the lifetime product. As today, it writes only the `admin`-source lifetime row: a granted `revenuecat` row (lifetime or annual) is never changed, an annual row is never read or written, and only a revoked lifetime row (a refunded purchase) may be re-granted as `admin`. It answers `listAdminAccess` read inside the same transaction.
- `export const adminSchemas = { updateAccess }` replaces `createAdminSchemas(paidProductIds)`.
- `AdminDeps = { database; now?; rateLimitKeySecret }`; `createTestApp` option `admin?: boolean`.

```ts
// The app with the /v1/admin routes wired to a real database for one integration test, mounted
// beside the routes an admin grant must reach: the /v1 sync routes (GET /v1/me) and the RevenueCat
// webhook. One injectable clock serves every router, and the rate-limit key secret and webhook
// authorization value are generated at run time. The toggle manages the lifetime Pro product.
import type pg from 'pg';

import { createTestApp } from './createTestApp.js';
import type { AnswerKey } from '../../types/AnswerKey.js';

export const ADMIN_TEST_PRODUCTS = {
  ANNUAL: 'syntactical.pro.annual',
  LIFETIME: 'syntactical.pro.lifetime',
} as const;

interface AdminTestAppOptions {
  pool: pg.Pool;
}

export function createAdminTestApp(options: AdminTestAppOptions) {
  const { pool } = options;
  const answerKey: AnswerKey = new Map();
  const { app, clock, rateLimitKeySecret, revenueCatAuth } = createTestApp({
    admin: true,
    pool,
    sync: { answerKey },
    webhooks: true,
  });
  return { app, clock, rateLimitKeySecret, revenueCatAuth };
}
```

```ts
// Requests and database reads shared by the /v1/admin/access integration tests: sign in a user
// (an admin when the test sets users.is_admin directly, the only way the flag is ever set), call
// the admin routes by bearer token or by cookie, and read or insert a user's entitlement rows,
// expiry included.
import type pg from 'pg';
import request from 'supertest';

import { insertSession } from './insertSession.js';

export const ADMIN_ACCESS_ROUTE = '/v1/admin/access';
const COOKIE_NAME = 'syntactical_session';

export interface Caller {
  sessionToken: string;
  transport: 'bearer' | 'cookie';
  userId: string;
}

export interface EntitlementRow {
  expires_at: Date | null;
  product_id: string;
  source: string;
  status: string;
  updated_at: Date;
}

type App = Parameters<typeof request>[0];

export async function signInUser(pool: pg.Pool, now: Date, isAdmin: boolean): Promise<Caller> {
  const { sessionToken, userId } = await insertSession(pool, { createdAt: now });
  if (isAdmin) {
    await pool.query('UPDATE users SET is_admin = true WHERE id = $1', [userId]);
  }
  return { sessionToken, transport: 'bearer', userId };
}

export function asCookie(caller: Caller): Caller {
  return { ...caller, transport: 'cookie' };
}

export function authorize(pending: request.Test, caller: Caller, withCsrfHeader = true): request.Test {
  if (caller.transport === 'bearer') {
    return pending.set('Authorization', `Bearer ${caller.sessionToken}`);
  }
  const withCookie = pending.set('Cookie', `${COOKIE_NAME}=${caller.sessionToken}`);
  return withCsrfHeader ? withCookie.set('X-Requested-With', 'XMLHttpRequest') : withCookie;
}

export function getAccess(app: App, caller: Caller): Promise<request.Response> {
  return authorize(request(app).get(ADMIN_ACCESS_ROUTE), caller).then((response) => response);
}

export function putAccess(app: App, caller: Caller, body: unknown): Promise<request.Response> {
  return authorize(request(app).put(ADMIN_ACCESS_ROUTE), caller)
    .send(body as object)
    .then((response) => response);
}

export async function readEntitlementRows(pool: pg.Pool, userId: string): Promise<EntitlementRow[]> {
  const { rows } = await pool.query<EntitlementRow>(
    `SELECT product_id, source, status, expires_at, updated_at FROM entitlements
     WHERE user_id = $1 ORDER BY product_id`,
    [userId],
  );
  return rows;
}

export async function insertEntitlement(
  pool: pg.Pool,
  row: { expiresAt?: Date | null; productId: string; source: string; status: 'granted' | 'revoked'; userId: string },
): Promise<void> {
  await pool.query(
    'INSERT INTO entitlements (user_id, product_id, source, status, expires_at) VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5)',
    [row.userId, row.productId, row.source, row.status, row.expiresAt ?? null],
  );
}

export async function readIsAdmin(pool: pg.Pool, userId: string): Promise<boolean | undefined> {
  const { rows } = await pool.query<{ is_admin: boolean }>('SELECT is_admin FROM users WHERE id = $1', [userId]);
  return rows[0]?.is_admin;
}
```

```ts
// Admin access as a Pro toggle (spec "2. Pro", Server): GET /v1/admin/access answers one entry in
// today's AdminProductEntry shape, { grantSource, isGranted, productId: 'syntactical.pro.lifetime' }.
// grantSource is 'purchase' when a granted RevenueCat row on either Pro product is active (expires_at
// NULL or later than now), else 'admin' for the admin's own lifetime grant, else null; isGranted is
// true exactly when grantSource is set. PUT /v1/admin/access { isGranted } grants or revokes an
// 'admin'-source lifetime row with no expiry for the session user only and answers the same entry.
// A granted 'revenuecat' row is never overwritten. A request needs a session (401
// AUTH_SESSION_REQUIRED) and users.is_admin (403 ADMIN_REQUIRED). Every token is built at run time.
import request from 'supertest';
import { afterAll, beforeAll, beforeEach, describe, expect, inject, it } from 'vitest';

import { hasPro } from '../../services/hasPro.js';
import {
  ADMIN_ACCESS_ROUTE,
  getAccess,
  insertEntitlement,
  putAccess,
  readEntitlementRows,
  readIsAdmin,
  signInUser,
} from '../integration/adminAccessRequests.js';
import { ADMIN_TEST_PRODUCTS, createAdminTestApp } from '../integration/createAdminTestApp.js';
import { createMigratedDatabase } from '../integration/createMigratedDatabase.js';
import { insertSession } from '../integration/insertSession.js';
import { SKIP_DATABASE_TESTS } from '../integration/skipDatabaseTests.js';

const HTTP_OK = 200;
const HTTP_BAD_REQUEST = 400;
const HTTP_UNAUTHORIZED = 401;
const HTTP_FORBIDDEN = 403;
const SETUP_TIMEOUT_MS = 120_000;
const DAY_MS = 86_400_000;
const { ANNUAL, LIFETIME } = ADMIN_TEST_PRODUCTS;

let database: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof createMigratedDatabase>>;

function entry(grantSource: 'admin' | 'purchase' | null) {
  return { data: { grantSource, isGranted: grantSource !== null, productId: LIFETIME } };
}

function setup() {
  const testApp = createAdminTestApp({ pool: database.pool });
  return { ...testApp, now: testApp.clock.now() };
}

function shape(rows: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof readEntitlementRows>>) {
  return rows.map(({ expires_at, product_id, source, status }) => ({ expires_at, product_id, source, status }));
}

describe.skipIf(SKIP_DATABASE_TESTS)('/v1/admin/access as a Pro toggle', () => {
  beforeAll(async () => {
    database = await createMigratedDatabase(inject('testDatabaseUrl'));
  }, SETUP_TIMEOUT_MS);

  afterAll(async () => {
    await database?.drop();
  });

  beforeEach(async () => {
    await database.reset();
  });

  it('answers GET and PUT with 401 AUTH_SESSION_REQUIRED without a session or with an expired one', async () => {
    const { app, now } = setup();
    const expired = await insertSession(database.pool, {
      createdAt: new Date(now.getTime() - 31 * DAY_MS),
      expiresAt: new Date(now.getTime() - DAY_MS),
      lastUsedAt: new Date(now.getTime() - DAY_MS),
    });
    await database.pool.query('UPDATE users SET is_admin = true WHERE id = $1', [expired.userId]);

    const responses = [
      await request(app).get(ADMIN_ACCESS_ROUTE),
      await request(app).put(ADMIN_ACCESS_ROUTE).send({ isGranted: true }),
      await request(app).get(ADMIN_ACCESS_ROUTE).set('Authorization', `Bearer ${expired.sessionToken}`),
      await request(app)
        .put(ADMIN_ACCESS_ROUTE)
        .set('Authorization', `Bearer ${expired.sessionToken}`)
        .send({ isGranted: true }),
    ];

    for (const response of responses) {
      expect(response.status).toBe(HTTP_UNAUTHORIZED);
      expect(response.body.error.code).toBe('AUTH_SESSION_REQUIRED');
    }
    expect(await readEntitlementRows(database.pool, expired.userId)).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('answers a signed-in non-admin with 403 ADMIN_REQUIRED on GET and PUT and writes nothing', async () => {
    const { app, now } = setup();
    const learner = await signInUser(database.pool, now, false);

    const listed = await getAccess(app, learner);
    const granted = await putAccess(app, learner, { isGranted: true });

    for (const response of [listed, granted]) {
      expect(response.status).toBe(HTTP_FORBIDDEN);
      expect(response.body.error.code).toBe('ADMIN_REQUIRED');
      expect(response.body.data).toBeUndefined();
    }
    expect(await readEntitlementRows(database.pool, learner.userId)).toEqual([]);
    expect(await readIsAdmin(database.pool, learner.userId)).toBe(false);
  });

  it('GET answers the lifetime entry, not granted, for an admin with no entitlements', async () => {
    const { app, now } = setup();
    const admin = await signInUser(database.pool, now, true);

    const response = await getAccess(app, admin);

    expect(response.status).toBe(HTTP_OK);
    expect(response.body).toEqual(entry(null));
  });

  it("GET reports an admin grant as 'admin', a RevenueCat lifetime grant as 'purchase', and a revoked row as null", async () => {
    const { app, now } = setup();
    const adminGranted = await signInUser(database.pool, now, true);
    const purchased = await signInUser(database.pool, now, true);
    const revoked = await signInUser(database.pool, now, true);
    await insertEntitlement(database.pool, {
      productId: LIFETIME,
      source: 'admin',
      status: 'granted',
      userId: adminGranted.userId,
    });
    await insertEntitlement(database.pool, {
      productId: LIFETIME,
      source: 'revenuecat',
      status: 'granted',
      userId: purchased.userId,
    });
    await insertEntitlement(database.pool, {
      productId: LIFETIME,
      source: 'admin',
      status: 'revoked',
      userId: revoked.userId,
    });

    expect((await getAccess(app, adminGranted)).body).toEqual(entry('admin'));
    expect((await getAccess(app, purchased)).body).toEqual(entry('purchase'));
    expect((await getAccess(app, revoked)).body).toEqual(entry(null));
  });

  it("GET reports an active annual RevenueCat grant as 'purchase', and an expired one as not granted", async () => {
    const { app, now } = setup();
    const active = await signInUser(database.pool, now, true);
    const expired = await signInUser(database.pool, now, true);
    await insertEntitlement(database.pool, {
      expiresAt: new Date(now.getTime() + DAY_MS),
      productId: ANNUAL,
      source: 'revenuecat',
      status: 'granted',
      userId: active.userId,
    });
    await insertEntitlement(database.pool, {
      expiresAt: new Date(now.getTime() - DAY_MS),
      productId: ANNUAL,
      source: 'revenuecat',
      status: 'granted',
      userId: expired.userId,
    });

    const activeResponse = await getAccess(app, active);
    const expiredResponse = await getAccess(app, expired);

    expect(activeResponse.status).toBe(HTTP_OK);
    expect(activeResponse.body).toEqual({
      data: { grantSource: 'purchase', isGranted: true, productId: 'syntactical.pro.lifetime' },
    });
    expect(expiredResponse.status).toBe(HTTP_OK);
    expect(expiredResponse.body).toEqual(entry(null));
  });

  it("GET reports 'purchase' over an admin grant while an annual purchase is active, and 'admin' once it expires", async () => {
    const { app, clock, now } = setup();
    const admin = await signInUser(database.pool, now, true);
    await insertEntitlement(database.pool, {
      productId: LIFETIME,
      source: 'admin',
      status: 'granted',
      userId: admin.userId,
    });
    await insertEntitlement(database.pool, {
      expiresAt: new Date(now.getTime() + DAY_MS),
      productId: ANNUAL,
      source: 'revenuecat',
      status: 'granted',
      userId: admin.userId,
    });

    const whileActive = await getAccess(app, admin);
    clock.advance(2 * DAY_MS);
    const afterExpiry = await getAccess(app, admin);

    expect(whileActive.body).toEqual(entry('purchase'));
    expect(afterExpiry.status).toBe(HTTP_OK);
    expect(afterExpiry.body).toEqual(entry('admin'));
  });

  it("GET ignores a revoked annual row and another user's lifetime grant", async () => {
    const { app, now } = setup();
    const admin = await signInUser(database.pool, now, true);
    const other = await signInUser(database.pool, now, false);
    await insertEntitlement(database.pool, {
      expiresAt: new Date(now.getTime() + DAY_MS),
      productId: ANNUAL,
      source: 'revenuecat',
      status: 'revoked',
      userId: admin.userId,
    });
    await insertEntitlement(database.pool, {
      productId: LIFETIME,
      source: 'admin',
      status: 'granted',
      userId: other.userId,
    });

    const response = await getAccess(app, admin);

    expect(response.status).toBe(HTTP_OK);
    expect(response.body).toEqual(entry(null));
  });

  it("PUT isGranted true creates a granted 'admin' lifetime row with no expiry, and the user has Pro", async () => {
    const { app, now } = setup();
    const admin = await signInUser(database.pool, now, true);

    const response = await putAccess(app, admin, { isGranted: true });
    const listed = await getAccess(app, admin);

    expect(response.status).toBe(HTTP_OK);
    expect(response.body).toEqual(entry('admin'));
    expect(listed.body).toEqual(entry('admin'));
    expect(shape(await readEntitlementRows(database.pool, admin.userId))).toEqual([
      { expires_at: null, product_id: LIFETIME, source: 'admin', status: 'granted' },
    ]);
    expect(await hasPro(database.pool, admin.userId, now)).toBe(true);
  });

  it("PUT isGranted false revokes the admin's row, and true again re-grants the same row", async () => {
    const { app, now } = setup();
    const admin = await signInUser(database.pool, now, true);
    await putAccess(app, admin, { isGranted: true });

    const revoked = await putAccess(app, admin, { isGranted: false });
    const afterRevoke = await readEntitlementRows(database.pool, admin.userId);
    const hasProAfterRevoke = await hasPro(database.pool, admin.userId, now);
    const regranted = await putAccess(app, admin, { isGranted: true });

    expect(revoked.status).toBe(HTTP_OK);
    expect(revoked.body).toEqual(entry(null));
    expect(afterRevoke.filter(({ status }) => status === 'granted')).toEqual([]);
    expect(hasProAfterRevoke).toBe(false);
    expect(regranted.body).toEqual(entry('admin'));
    expect(shape(await readEntitlementRows(database.pool, admin.userId))).toEqual([
      { expires_at: null, product_id: LIFETIME, source: 'admin', status: 'granted' },

  it('PUT isGranted false with no row answers not granted and grants nothing', async () => {
    const { app, now } = setup();
    const admin = await signInUser(database.pool, now, true);

    const response = await putAccess(app, admin, { isGranted: false });

    expect(response.status).toBe(HTTP_OK);

  it("PUT leaves an active annual row alone, writes only the lifetime row, and answers 'purchase'", async () => {
    const { app, now } = setup();

    for (const response of [turnedOn, turnedOff]) {
```

`server/src/__tests__/routes/adminAccessEntitlements.integration.test.ts`, replaced whole:

```ts
// The admin Pro toggle end to end (spec "2. Pro", Server): an admin's self-grant through PUT
// /v1/admin/access makes hasPro true with no expiry, and a revoke makes it false again. Purchases
// win: a RevenueCat lifetime purchase delivered through the webhook takes over an admin-granted row
// (granted, source 'revenuecat'), and a later toggle off leaves the purchase in force. An annual
// purchase is a separate row the toggle never touches, and GET reports it as 'purchase' while it is
// active. Every token is built at run time.
import { randomBytes, randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';

import request from 'supertest';
import { afterAll, beforeAll, beforeEach, describe, expect, inject, it } from 'vitest';

import { hasPro } from '../../services/hasPro.js';
import { getAccess, putAccess, readEntitlementRows, signInUser } from '../integration/adminAccessRequests.js';
import { ADMIN_TEST_PRODUCTS, createAdminTestApp } from '../integration/createAdminTestApp.js';
import { createMigratedDatabase } from '../integration/createMigratedDatabase.js';
import { SKIP_DATABASE_TESTS } from '../integration/skipDatabaseTests.js';

const HTTP_OK = 200;
const SETUP_TIMEOUT_MS = 120_000;
const WEBHOOK_ROUTE = '/v1/webhooks/revenuecat';
const TRANSACTION_BYTES = 12;
const YEAR_MS = 31_536_000_000;
const { ANNUAL, LIFETIME } = ADMIN_TEST_PRODUCTS;
// The toggle's entry while a purchase is in force (today's AdminProductEntry shape).
const PURCHASED = { data: { grantSource: 'purchase', isGranted: true, productId: LIFETIME } };

let database: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof createMigratedDatabase>>;

type App = ReturnType<typeof createAdminTestApp>['app'];

function setup() {
  const testApp = createAdminTestApp({ pool: database.pool });
  return { ...testApp, now: testApp.clock.now() };
}

function deliverPurchase(app: App, revenueCatAuth: string, userId: string, productId: string, at: Date) {
  const isAnnual = productId === ANNUAL;
  const event = {
    app_user_id: userId,
    environment: 'SANDBOX',
    event_timestamp_ms: at.getTime(),
    ...(isAnnual ? { expiration_at_ms: at.getTime() + YEAR_MS } : {}),
    id: randomUUID(),
    product_id: productId,
    purchased_at_ms: at.getTime(),
    store: 'APP_STORE',
    transaction_id: randomBytes(TRANSACTION_BYTES).toString('hex'),
    type: isAnnual ? 'INITIAL_PURCHASE' : 'NON_RENEWING_PURCHASE',
  };
  return request(app)
    .post(WEBHOOK_ROUTE)
    .set('Authorization', revenueCatAuth)
    .set('Content-Type', 'application/json')
    .send(JSON.stringify({ event }));
}

function shape(rows: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof readEntitlementRows>>) {
  return rows.map(({ product_id, source, status }) => ({ product_id, source, status }));
}

    expect(shape(await readEntitlementRows(database.pool, admin.userId))).toEqual([

    for (const response of [toggledOff, listed]) {

  });
```

```ts
// Guards on PUT /v1/admin/access (spec "2. Pro", Server): a cookie request needs the CSRF header;
// the body is JSON only; malformed, oversized, mistyped, and injection-shaped bodies are refused
// and write nothing; a productId, userId, or isAdmin field is refused and never reaches another
// user or the admin flag; the admin flag is read on every request; and the PUT is rate limited per
// user at 60 an hour, the 61st answering 429 RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED and changing nothing. Every token
// is built at run time.

  authorize,

const HTTP_UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE = 415;

const RATE_LIMIT_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000;
const HOUR_MS = 3_600_000;

const PUTS_PER_HOUR = 60;
const OVERSIZED_BYTES = 20_000;

let database: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof createMigratedDatabase>>;

  return { ...testApp, now: testApp.clock.now() };
}

function grantedProductIds(rows: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof readEntitlementRows>>): string[] {
  return rows.filter(({ status }) => status === 'granted').map(({ product_id }) => product_id);
}

    const revokeForOther = await putAccess(app, admin, { isGranted: false, userId: target.userId });
    const snakeCase = await putAccess(app, admin, { isGranted: false, user_id: target.userId });

    async () => {

        const response = await putAccess(app, admin, { isGranted: index % 2 === 0 });
        expect({ index, status: response.status }).toEqual({ index, status: HTTP_OK });

      expect(otherUser.status).toBe(HTTP_OK);

      clock.advance(HOUR_MS);

      expect(grantedProductIds(await readEntitlementRows(database.pool, admin.userId))).toEqual([LIFETIME]);
```

`server/src/services/listAdminAccess.ts`, replaced whole:

```ts
// The admin's Pro toggle state, in the AdminProductEntry shape the app parses, always for the
// lifetime product. 'purchase' when a granted RevenueCat row on either Pro product is active by the
// hasPro rule (expires_at NULL or later than now), so an annual purchaser sees their purchase; else
// 'admin' when the admin's own lifetime grant is in force; else not granted. Takes a pooled client
// too, so setAdminAccess can answer from inside its transaction.
import type pg from 'pg';

import type { Database } from '../clients/database.js';
import { PRO_PRODUCT_ID_LIST, PRO_PRODUCT_IDS } from '../constants/proProducts.js';
import { REVENUECAT_EVENTS } from '../constants/revenueCatEvents.js';
import type { AdminProductEntry } from '../types/AdminProductEntry.js';

import { toAdminProductEntry } from './toAdminProductEntry.js';

type Queryable = Database | pg.PoolClient;

interface ActiveRow {
  product_id: string;
  source: string;
}

// The source the entry reports: a purchase first, then the admin's lifetime grant, else none.
function grantedSourceOf(rows: ActiveRow[]): string | undefined {
  if (rows.some(({ source }) => source === REVENUECAT_EVENTS.ENTITLEMENT_SOURCE)) {
    return REVENUECAT_EVENTS.ENTITLEMENT_SOURCE;
  }
  const isAdminGranted = rows.some(
    ({ product_id: productId, source }) => productId === PRO_PRODUCT_IDS.LIFETIME && source === 'admin',
  );
  return isAdminGranted ? 'admin' : undefined;
}

async function listAdminAccess(queryable: Queryable, userId: string, now: Date): Promise<AdminProductEntry> {
  const { rows } = await queryable.query<ActiveRow>(
    `SELECT product_id, source FROM entitlements
     WHERE user_id = $1 AND product_id = ANY($2::text[]) AND status = 'granted'
       AND (expires_at IS NULL OR expires_at > $3)`,
    [userId, [...PRO_PRODUCT_ID_LIST], now],
  );
  return toAdminProductEntry(PRO_PRODUCT_IDS.LIFETIME, grantedSourceOf(rows));
}

export { listAdminAccess };
```

`server/src/services/setAdminAccess.ts`, replaced whole (the lock and the "purchases win" rule are unchanged; the product is fixed, a grant writes no expiry, and the answer is the GET entry read in the same transaction):

```ts
// PUT /v1/admin/access's write: in one transaction, under the user's row lock, grants or revokes
// the session user's 'admin'-source entitlement on the lifetime Pro product, with expires_at NULL.
// A granted 'revenuecat' row is never changed (the purchase stays in force); a revoked one (a
// refunded purchase) may be re-granted as 'admin'. Revoking touches only an 'admin' row. An annual
// row is never written here. The answer is listAdminAccess read inside the transaction, so a PUT
// reports exactly what a GET would, an active annual purchase included. Undefined when the user is
// gone.
//
// Serialization with the RevenueCat webhook: lockUserRow takes FOR UPDATE on the users row, which
// conflicts with the FOR KEY SHARE that recordPurchaseEvent takes on the same row
// (SELECT id FROM users WHERE id = $1 FOR KEY SHARE) before it writes the entitlement. So a PUT
// waits for an in-flight webhook transaction to commit and then reads its result, and the
// webhook waits for the PUT. The upsert's WHERE is defense in depth for the same rule.
//
// After a refund an admin re-grant (source 'admin') is removed by any later RevenueCat revoke
// event for the same product, because recomputeEntitlement rewrites source and status. This
// fails closed and is intended.
import type { Database } from '../clients/database.js';
import { withTransaction } from '../clients/withTransaction.js';
import { PRO_PRODUCT_IDS } from '../constants/proProducts.js';
import type { AdminProductEntry } from '../types/AdminProductEntry.js';

import { listAdminAccess } from './listAdminAccess.js';
import { lockUserRow } from './lockUserRow.js';

const PRODUCT_ID = PRO_PRODUCT_IDS.LIFETIME;

async function setAdminAccess(
  database: Database,
  userId: string,
  isGranted: boolean,
  now: Date,
): Promise<AdminProductEntry | undefined> {
  return withTransaction(
    database,
    async (client) => {
      if (!(await lockUserRow(client, userId))) {
        return undefined;
      }
      const { rows } = await client.query<{ source: string; status: string }>(
        'SELECT source, status FROM entitlements WHERE user_id = $1 AND product_id = $2',
        [userId, PRODUCT_ID],
      );
      const [row] = rows;
      const isPurchaseInForce = row?.status === 'granted' && row.source !== 'admin';
      if (isGranted && !isPurchaseInForce) {
        await client.query(
          `INSERT INTO entitlements (user_id, product_id, source, status, expires_at)
           VALUES ($1, $2, 'admin', 'granted', NULL)
           ON CONFLICT (user_id, product_id) DO UPDATE SET source = 'admin', status = 'granted', expires_at = NULL
           WHERE entitlements.source = 'admin' OR entitlements.status = 'revoked'`,
          [userId, PRODUCT_ID],
        );
      }
      if (!isGranted && row?.source === 'admin' && row.status === 'granted') {
        await client.query(
          "UPDATE entitlements SET status = 'revoked' WHERE user_id = $1 AND product_id = $2 AND source = 'admin'",
          [userId, PRODUCT_ID],
        );
      }
      return listAdminAccess(client, userId, now);
    },
    { hasTimeouts: true },
  );
}

export { setAdminAccess };
```

`server/src/routes/adminAccess.ts`, replaced whole:

```ts
// GET and PUT /v1/admin/access: an admin reads the Pro toggle (the lifetime product, whether they
// have Pro, and whether it comes from a purchase or their own grant) and grants or revokes their own
// 'admin' access to it. Order: session (401), admin flag read fresh (403 ADMIN_REQUIRED), then for
// PUT the per-user rate limit (429) and the strict { isGranted } body (400). Only the session user's
// rows are ever read, and only their lifetime row written. Every response is no-store. Both answer
// { data: AdminProductEntry }, one entry, by the clock in deps.
import { Router } from 'express';

import { ADMIN } from '../constants/admin.js';
import { HTTP } from '../constants/http.js';
import { ERROR_CODES, sendError } from '../errors.js';
import { createRateLimit } from '../middleware/rateLimit.js';
import { keyOfUser } from '../middleware/rateLimitKeys.js';
import { createRequireAdmin } from '../middleware/requireAdmin.js';
import { createRequireSession } from '../middleware/requireSession.js';
import { adminSchemas } from '../schemas/adminSchemas.js';
import { listAdminAccess } from '../services/listAdminAccess.js';
import { setAdminAccess } from '../services/setAdminAccess.js';

import type { ResolvedAdminDeps } from './adminDeps.js';

const {
  STATUS: { BAD_REQUEST, OK, UNAUTHORIZED },
} = HTTP;

function createAdminAccessRouter(deps: ResolvedAdminDeps): Router {
  const { database, now, rateLimitKeySecret } = deps;
  const router = Router();
  const requireSession = createRequireSession({ database, now });
  const requireAdmin = createRequireAdmin(database);
  const perUser = createRateLimit({
    database,
    keyOf: keyOfUser,
    keySecret: rateLimitKeySecret,
    limit: ADMIN.RATE_LIMIT.ACCESS_UPDATE_PER_USER,
    now,
    scope: ADMIN.RATE_LIMIT_SCOPE.ACCESS_UPDATE,
    windowMs: ADMIN.RATE_LIMIT.WINDOW_MS,
  });

  router.use('/admin/access', (_req, res, next) => {
    res.set('Cache-Control', 'private, no-store');
    next();
  });

  router.get('/admin/access', requireSession, requireAdmin, async (_req, res) => {
    const { session } = res.locals as { session: { userId: string } };
    const entry = await listAdminAccess(database, session.userId, now());
    res.status(OK).json({ data: entry });
  });

  router.put('/admin/access', requireSession, requireAdmin, perUser, async (req, res) => {
    const { session } = res.locals as { session: { userId: string } };
    const { data, success } = adminSchemas.updateAccess.safeParse(req.body);
    if (!success) {
      sendError(res, BAD_REQUEST, ERROR_CODES.INPUT.INVALID_BODY, 'Invalid request body');
      return;
    }
    const entry = await setAdminAccess(database, session.userId, data.isGranted, now());
    if (!entry) {
      sendError(res, UNAUTHORIZED, ERROR_CODES.AUTH.SESSION_REQUIRED, 'Sign-in required');
      return;
    }
    res.status(OK).json({ data: entry });
  });

  return router;
}

export { createAdminAccessRouter };
```

  ```ts
  const INACTIVE: ProStatus = { expiresAt: null, isActive: false, product: null };

  // The same rule as hasPro: a granted row for either Pro product whose expires_at is NULL or later than now.
  async function readPro(queryable: Queryable, userId: string, now: Date): Promise<ProStatus> {
    const { rows } = await queryable.query<{ expires_at: Date | null; product_id: string }>(
      `SELECT product_id, expires_at FROM entitlements
       WHERE user_id = $1 AND product_id = ANY($2::text[]) AND status = 'granted'
         AND (expires_at IS NULL OR expires_at > $3)`,
      [userId, [...PRO_PRODUCT_ID_LIST], now],
    );
    const lifetime = rows.find(({ product_id: productId }) => productId === PRO_PRODUCT_IDS.LIFETIME);
    const annual = rows.find(({ product_id: productId }) => productId === PRO_PRODUCT_IDS.ANNUAL);
    const winner = lifetime ?? annual;
    if (!winner) {
      return INACTIVE;
    }
    return {
      expiresAt: winner.expires_at?.toISOString() ?? null,
      isActive: true,
      product: winner === lifetime ? 'lifetime' : 'annual',
    };
  }
  ```

```ts
// POST /v1/ask by tier (spec "2. Pro", Server): any signed-in user may ask about any bank's
// question, Easy to Hard, with no purchase. A free user gets 5 answers per UTC day and a Pro user
// (hasPro, read on every ask) 20; the 200 body and the 429 ASK_DAILY_LIMIT_REACHED body both carry
// the limit. Review Focus 3: a free user at the cap who becomes Pro gets the next answer the same
// day, against the Pro limit, with no new usage date. A failed or declined model call does not use
// an answer up. The model is a fake that records each prompt.
import type { Question } from '@syntactical/content-schema';
import request from 'supertest';
import { afterAll, beforeAll, beforeEach, describe, expect, inject, it } from 'vitest';

import { ASK } from '../../constants/ask.js';
import type { ModelProvider } from '../../clients/modelProvider.js';
import { createFakeModelProvider } from '../../testing/fakeModelProvider.js';
import { createMigratedDatabase } from '../integration/createMigratedDatabase.js';
import { createTestApp } from '../integration/createTestApp.js';
import { insertSession } from '../integration/insertSession.js';
import { SKIP_DATABASE_TESTS } from '../integration/skipDatabaseTests.js';

const SETUP_TIMEOUT_MS = 120_000;
const LONG_TEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000;
const DAY_MS = 86_400_000;
const MINUTE_MS = 60_000;
// The chosen limits, written out so the test does not borrow the code's constant.
const FREE_LIMIT = 5;
const PRO_LIMIT = 20;
const ALLOWED_ORIGIN = 'https://syntactical.dev';
const EASY_BANK = 'python/easy';
const HARD_BANK = 'python/hard';
const LIFETIME = 'syntactical.pro.lifetime';
const ANNUAL = 'syntactical.pro.annual';
const MESSAGE = 'Why does the list keep its old value here?';
const PROVENANCE: Question['provenance'] = {
  isHumanReviewed: true,
  source: 'original',
  validation: { method: 'judged', status: 'passed' },
};

const easyQuestion: Question = {
  answerIndex: 1,
  choices: [{ rationale: 'Assignment copies the reference, not the list.', text: '[1, 2]' }, { text: '[1, 2, 3]' }],
  code: 'a = [1, 2]\nb = a\nb.append(3)\nprint(a)',
  id: 'py-easy-0',
  prompt: 'What does this print?',
  provenance: PROVENANCE,
  query: { explanation: 'b and a name the same list.', title: 'Names and objects' },
  type: 'mc',
};

const boolQuestion: Question = {
  answer: false,
  id: 'py-easy-1',
  prompt: 'Strings are mutable in Python.',
  provenance: PROVENANCE,
  query: { explanation: 'Strings are immutable.', title: 'Strings' },
  rationale: 'String methods return new strings.',
  type: 'bool',
};

const hardQuestion: Question = {
  ...easyQuestion,
  id: 'fixture-hard-0',
  query: { explanation: 'hard-explanation-marker', title: 'Hard' },
};

const questions = new Map<string, ReadonlyMap<string, Question>>([
  [
    EASY_BANK,
    new Map<string, Question>([
      [easyQuestion.id, easyQuestion],
      [boolQuestion.id, boolQuestion],
    ]),
  ],
  [HARD_BANK, new Map([[hardQuestion.id, hardQuestion]])],
]);

let database: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof createMigratedDatabase>>;

function createAskApp(modelProvider: ModelProvider | undefined) {
  return createTestApp({
    ask: { ...(modelProvider ? { modelProvider } : {}), questions },
    pool: database.pool,
  });
}

// null mounts the route with no model provider, as with no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.
async function signIn(modelProvider: ModelProvider | null = createFakeModelProvider()) {
  const { app, clock } = createAskApp(modelProvider ?? undefined);
  const { sessionToken, userId } = await insertSession(database.pool, { createdAt: clock.now() });
  return { app, clock, sessionToken, userId };
}

async function grant(
  userId: string,
  productId: string,
  options: { expiresAt?: Date | null; status?: 'granted' | 'revoked' } = {},
): Promise<void> {
  const { expiresAt = null, status = 'granted' } = options;
  await database.pool.query(
    'INSERT INTO entitlements (user_id, product_id, status, source, expires_at) VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5)',
    [userId, productId, status, 'test', expiresAt],
  );
}

type Signed = Awaited<ReturnType<typeof signIn>>;

function ask(signed: Signed, body: object) {
  return request(signed.app)
    .post('/v1/ask')
    .set('Authorization', `Bearer ${signed.sessionToken}`)
    .set('Origin', ALLOWED_ORIGIN)
    .send(body);
}

function askEasy(signed: Signed, extra: object = {}) {
  return ask(signed, { bankKey: EASY_BANK, message: MESSAGE, questionId: easyQuestion.id, ...extra });
}

// Asks `count` times, moving the clock a minute after every burst-limit's worth so only the daily
// limit can refuse; each answer must be 200 with the limit and the answers left.
async function useAnswers(signed: Signed, count: number, limit: number, alreadyUsed = 0): Promise<void> {
  for (let index = 0; index < count; index += 1) {
    if (index > 0 && index % ASK.RATE_LIMIT.PER_USER === 0) signed.clock.advance(MINUTE_MS);
    const response = await askEasy(signed);
    expect({ index, status: response.status }).toEqual({ index, status: 200 });
    expect(response.body.data).toMatchObject({ limit, remaining: limit - alreadyUsed - index - 1 });
  }
  signed.clock.advance(MINUTE_MS);
}

async function usage(userId: string): Promise<Array<{ count: number; usage_date: string }>> {
  const { rows } = await database.pool.query<{ count: number; usage_date: string }>(
    "SELECT to_char(usage_date, 'YYYY-MM-DD') AS usage_date, count FROM ask_usage WHERE user_id = $1",
    [userId],
  );
  return rows;
}

    }
    const refused = await askEasy(signed);
```

`server/src/routes/revenueCatEventHandler.ts`:

```ts
// The RevenueCat event handling both webhook routes share: the JSON-only guard, and the handler
// that checks the body (400 when it is not a RevenueCat event), answers a type outside the grant,
// revoke, and expiry-only sets with 200 ignored, and records a handled event once with its
// entitlement recomputed (recordPurchaseEvent) in one transaction. Authentication is the mounting
// router's job: POST /v1/webhooks/revenuecat checks Authorization first; POST /v1/test/webhook,
// mounted only under NODE_ENV=test, has none. The payload and the app user id are never logged.
import type { NextFunction, Request, RequestHandler, Response } from 'express';
import type { Logger } from 'pino';

import type { Database } from '../clients/database.js';
import { HTTP } from '../constants/http.js';
import { REVENUECAT_EVENTS } from '../constants/revenueCatEvents.js';
import { ERROR_CODES, sendError } from '../errors.js';
import { isJsonMediaType } from '../middleware/isJsonMediaType.js';
import { requestLog } from '../middleware/requestLogger.js';
import { revenueCatSchemas } from '../schemas/revenueCatSchemas.js';
import { recordPurchaseEvent } from '../services/recordPurchaseEvent.js';

const {
  STATUS: { BAD_REQUEST, OK, UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE },
} = HTTP;

const { EXPIRY_ONLY_TYPES, GRANT_TYPES, REVOKE_TYPES } = REVENUECAT_EVENTS;

const HANDLED_TYPES: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set([...GRANT_TYPES, ...REVOKE_TYPES, ...EXPIRY_ONLY_TYPES]);

function requireJsonBody(req: Request, res: Response, next: NextFunction): void {
  if (isJsonMediaType(req.headers['content-type'])) {
    next();
    return;
  }
  sendError(
    res,
    UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE,
    ERROR_CODES.INPUT.UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE,
    'Content-Type must be application/json',
  );
}

function createRevenueCatEventHandler(database: Database, logger: Logger): RequestHandler {
  return async (req: Request, res: Response) => {
    const { data, success } = revenueCatSchemas.webhook.safeParse(req.body);
    if (!success) {
      sendError(res, BAD_REQUEST, ERROR_CODES.INPUT.INVALID_BODY, 'Invalid request body');
      return;
    }
    const { event } = data;
    if (!HANDLED_TYPES.has(event.type)) {
      res.status(OK).json({ data: { status: 'ignored' } });
      return;
    }
    const status = await recordPurchaseEvent({ database, event, logger: requestLog(res, logger) });
    res.status(OK).json({ data: { status } });
  };
}

export { createRevenueCatEventHandler, requireJsonBody };
```

`server/src/routes/revenueCatWebhook.ts`, replaced whole:

```ts
// POST /v1/webhooks/revenuecat (B-39a): authenticates by the Authorization header before the
// body is read (401 WEBHOOK_UNAUTHORIZED), then reads its own 64 KB JSON body: a Content-Type
// that is not application/json is 415, malformed or empty JSON is 400, over the limit is 413, a
// body that is not a RevenueCat event is 400. A secret under 32 trimmed characters is refused
// when the router is built.
// An event type outside the grant, revoke, and expiry-only sets is 200 ignored and recorded
// nowhere. A handled event is recorded once and its entitlement recomputed (B-39b) in one
// transaction; a failure answers 500 so RevenueCat redelivers. The header, the payload, and the
// app user id are never logged. The handling after authentication is shared with the test-only
// route (revenueCatEventHandler.ts).
import { timingSafeEqual } from 'node:crypto';

import express, { Router } from 'express';
import type { NextFunction, Request, Response } from 'express';
import type { Logger } from 'pino';

import { HTTP } from '../constants/http.js';
import { WEBHOOKS } from '../constants/webhooks.js';
import { ERROR_CODES, sendError } from '../errors.js';
import { sha256 } from '../services/sha256.js';

import { createRevenueCatEventHandler, requireJsonBody } from './revenueCatEventHandler.js';
import type { WebhookDeps } from './webhookDeps.js';

const {
  STATUS: { UNAUTHORIZED },
} = HTTP;

const { BODY_LIMIT, MIN_AUTH_LENGTH } = WEBHOOKS;

function createRevenueCatWebhookRouter(deps: WebhookDeps, logger: Logger): Router {
  const { database, revenueCatAuth } = deps;
  if (revenueCatAuth.trim().length < MIN_AUTH_LENGTH) {
    throw new Error(`webhooks.revenueCatAuth must be at least ${MIN_AUTH_LENGTH} characters`);
  }
  const expectedDigest = sha256(revenueCatAuth);
  const router = Router();

  // Digests have equal length, so the compare takes the same time whatever the sent value.
  function requireWebhookAuth(req: Request, res: Response, next: NextFunction): void {
    const sent = req.headers.authorization ?? '';
    if (timingSafeEqual(sha256(sent), expectedDigest)) {
      next();
      return;
    }
    sendError(res, UNAUTHORIZED, ERROR_CODES.WEBHOOK.UNAUTHORIZED, 'Unauthorized');
  }

  router.post(
    '/revenuecat',
    requireWebhookAuth,
    requireJsonBody,
    express.json({ limit: BODY_LIMIT }),
    createRevenueCatEventHandler(database, logger),
  );

  return router;
}

export { createRevenueCatWebhookRouter };
```

Insert before `## Post-deploy checks`:

```md
## RevenueCat webhook

RevenueCat posts every purchase event to `https://api.syntactical.dev/v1/webhooks/revenuecat` with the `Authorization` header set to `REVENUECAT_WEBHOOK_AUTH`. A wrong or missing header answers 401 before the body is read.

Two products change an entitlement: `syntactical.pro.annual` (auto-renewing, one year) and `syntactical.pro.lifetime` (non-consumable). RevenueCat reports a Google Play subscription as `<subscription id>:<base plan id>`, so the annual bought on Play arrives as `syntactical.pro.annual:yearly`; the server strips the base-plan suffix before matching and stores `syntactical.pro.annual`. Any other product id is recorded and changes nothing. For each product the server keeps one `entitlements` row per user:

- `INITIAL_PURCHASE`, `RENEWAL`, `UNCANCELLATION`, and `NON_RENEWING_PURCHASE` grant. On the annual product the row's `expires_at` is the event's `expiration_at_ms`; the lifetime row has none.
- An annual grant without `expiration_at_ms` is recorded and answered 200 but grants nothing (it would otherwise mean Pro forever), and the server logs a warning, `annual grant without expiration ignored`. Look into any such warning in the logs.
- `EXPIRATION` and `REFUND` revoke.
- `CANCELLATION` on the annual product only updates `expires_at` (auto-renew is off and Pro lasts to the period end); on the lifetime product it revokes.
- Any other type (`BILLING_ISSUE`, `PRODUCT_CHANGE`, and the rest) answers 200 `ignored` and is not stored.

Events apply in `event_timestamp_ms` order, not arrival order, and a revoke wins a tie. A user has Pro while either row is granted and its `expires_at` is empty or in the future. The annual and lifetime rows never affect each other.

A server started with `NODE_ENV=test` also mounts `POST /v1/test/webhook`, which takes the same body with no `Authorization` header (for the fixture purchase client and e2e). Railway runs `NODE_ENV=production`, so it never exists there.

To check a deploy: send a RevenueCat test event from the dashboard and expect 200 `ignored`; a sandbox purchase of either product then shows `"pro": { "isActive": true, ... }` on `GET /v1/me` for that account.
```

### Open questions (area 3)

1. **Unhandled event types: recorded or not.** The spec says `BILLING_ISSUE` and `PRODUCT_CHANGE` are "recorded and ignored for status", and the plan's Global Constraints say "everything else is recorded and ignored"; the brief and today's code answer them 200 `ignored` without storing a row. Assumption: not stored (Task 3.3 pins it). Recording them would mean adding them to `HANDLED_TYPES` while `recomputeEntitlement` ignores them.
2. **Area 2's leftovers I could not read.** I assumed `startServer.ts` has a `LEGACY_PAID_PRODUCT_IDS` constant plus a derived `paidProductIds`, that `AskDeps.paidBanks` and the `ask.ts` gate still exist under some type, and that `createAdminTestApp.ts` still passes `webhooks: { paidProductIds }`. Line numbers I quote are from `main` today. The admin suites and `ask.integration.test.ts` are replaced whole, so they do not depend on what area 2 did to them.
3. **Migration number.** `1790985600018` assumes area 2 adds no migration.
4. **Admin PUT body.** The strict `{ isGranted }` body means an app build that still sends `productId` gets 400 until area 4 ships. The entry shape does not change: GET and PUT answer one `AdminProductEntry` (`{ grantSource, isGranted, productId }`), which `services/admin/parseAccessEntry.ts` already parses; area 4 reads `data` as that one entry instead of `data.products`.
5. **`docs/user-stories/quiz.md:125-128`.** The old Task 2.5 rewrote these lines. They describe the app drawer too (sign-in only, no purchase), so I left them for area 4, which changes `useCanAsk`.
6. **Test-only route gating.** `createApp` reads no env, so the guard is in `startServer` (`NODE_ENV === 'test'` from the parsed env), and `createApp` mounts the route only when given `testWebhook` deps. The RED test boots `startServer` on the repository's `content/` directory (no `CONTENT_DIR`), so it relies on area 2's content passing validation.

```tsx
// useProStatus reads data.pro from GET me under the ['me', userId, 'pro'] key: a guest makes no
// request; a free user, an annual subscriber, and a lifetime owner read as ready with the server's

import { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';
import type { PropsWithChildren } from 'react';

import { QueryClientProvider } from '@tanstack/react-query';
import { act, renderHook, waitFor } from '@testing-library/react-native';

import { fakeAuth } from '../../components/purchase/__tests__/purchaseFlowFakes';
import { setExpoExtra } from '../../config/expoConstantsMock';
import { createQueryClient } from '../../config/queryClient';
import { buildProStatusKey, useProStatus } from '../useProStatus';

import { installRoutedFetch, type FakeReply } from './authTestSupport';

setExpoExtra({ apiBaseUrl: 'https://api.syntactical.dev/v1/' });

jest.mock('expo-secure-store', () => ({
  deleteItemAsync: jest.fn(() => Promise.resolve()),
  getItemAsync: jest.fn(() => Promise.resolve(null)),

}));

  require('../../components/purchase/__tests__/purchaseFlowFakes').buildAuthModule(),
);

// Noon UTC, so the date is the same in every time zone a CI runner uses.
const ANNUAL_EXPIRY = '2027-10-27T12:00:00.000Z';
const FREE = { expiresAt: null, isActive: false, product: null };
const ANNUAL = { expiresAt: ANNUAL_EXPIRY, isActive: true, product: 'annual' };
const LIFETIME = { expiresAt: null, isActive: true, product: 'lifetime' };

let queryClient: ReturnType<typeof createQueryClient>;

function QueryWrapper({ children }: PropsWithChildren) {
  return <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>{children}</QueryClientProvider>;
}

function meReply(pro: unknown): FakeReply {
  return {
    status: 200,
    body: { data: { dailyGoal: 20, dayStreak: 0, email: 'reader@example.test', pro, xpToday: 0, xpTotal: 0 } },
  };
}

beforeEach(() => {
  fakeAuth.userId = randomUUID();
  queryClient = createQueryClient();
});

afterEach(() => {
  queryClient.clear();
});

describe('useProStatus', () => {
  it('is guest for a guest and sends no request', async () => {
    fakeAuth.userId = null;
    const { requests } = installRoutedFetch({ 'GET me': meReply(ANNUAL) });
    const { result } = await renderHook(() => useProStatus(), { wrapper: QueryWrapper });
    expect(result.current).toEqual({ status: 'guest' });
    expect(requests).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  it.each([
    ['a free user', FREE, { expiresAt: null, isPro: false, product: null, status: 'ready' }],
    ['an annual subscriber', ANNUAL, { expiresAt: ANNUAL_EXPIRY, isPro: true, product: 'annual', status: 'ready' }],
    ['a lifetime owner', LIFETIME, { expiresAt: null, isPro: true, product: 'lifetime', status: 'ready' }],
  ])('reads %s from data.pro', async (_label, pro, expected) => {
    installRoutedFetch({ 'GET me': meReply(pro) });
    const { result } = await renderHook(() => useProStatus(), { wrapper: QueryWrapper });
    await waitFor(() => expect(result.current).toEqual(expected));
  });

  it("caches the status under ['me', userId, 'pro']", async () => {
    installRoutedFetch({ 'GET me': meReply(ANNUAL) });
    const { result } = await renderHook(() => useProStatus(), { wrapper: QueryWrapper });
    await waitFor(() => expect(result.current.status).toBe('ready'));
    expect(buildProStatusKey(fakeAuth.userId)).toEqual(['me', fakeAuth.userId, 'pro']);
    expect(queryClient.getQueryData(buildProStatusKey(fakeAuth.userId))).toEqual({
      expiresAt: ANNUAL_EXPIRY,
      isPro: true,
      product: 'annual',
    });
  });

  it.each([
    ['the old entitlements shape', { status: 200, body: { data: { entitlements: [] } } }],
    ['a non-boolean isActive', meReply({ ...FREE, isActive: 'false' })],
    ['an unknown product', meReply({ ...ANNUAL, product: 'monthly' })],
    ['an expiry that is not a date', meReply({ ...ANNUAL, expiresAt: 'soon' })],
    ['a 503', { status: 503 }],
  ])('is an error for %s', async (_label, reply) => {
    installRoutedFetch({ 'GET me': reply as FakeReply });
    const { result } = await renderHook(() => useProStatus(), { wrapper: QueryWrapper });
    await waitFor(() => expect(result.current.status).toBe('error'));
  });

  it('asks again on retry after an error', async () => {
    const { setRoute } = installRoutedFetch({ 'GET me': { status: 503 } });
    const { result } = await renderHook(() => useProStatus(), { wrapper: QueryWrapper });
    await waitFor(() => expect(result.current.status).toBe('error'));
    setRoute('GET me', meReply(LIFETIME));
    await act(async () => {
      if (result.current.status === 'error') result.current.retry();
    });
    await waitFor(() => expect(result.current).toMatchObject({ isPro: true, product: 'lifetime', status: 'ready' }));
  });

  it("refetches when the ['me'] queries are invalidated, as an admin change does", async () => {
    const { setRoute } = installRoutedFetch({ 'GET me': meReply(FREE) });
    const { result } = await renderHook(() => useProStatus(), { wrapper: QueryWrapper });
    await waitFor(() => expect(result.current).toMatchObject({ isPro: false, status: 'ready' }));
    setRoute('GET me', meReply(LIFETIME));
    await act(async () => {
      await queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['me'] });
    });
    await waitFor(() => expect(result.current).toMatchObject({ isPro: true, product: 'lifetime' }));
  });
});
```

```ts
// The two Pro products the stores sell and the plan each one is. A product id outside these is
// not Pro. The ids match PRODUCT_ID_PATTERN in constants/appConfig.ts.
export const PRO_PRODUCT_IDS = {
  ANNUAL: 'syntactical.pro.annual',
  LIFETIME: 'syntactical.pro.lifetime',
} as const;

export type ProPlan = 'annual' | 'lifetime';

export function readProPlan(productId: string): ProPlan | null {
  if (productId === PRO_PRODUCT_IDS.ANNUAL) return 'annual';
  if (productId === PRO_PRODUCT_IDS.LIFETIME) return 'lifetime';
  return null;
}
```

`state/useProStatus.ts`:

```ts
// The signed-in user's Pro status from GET /me's data.pro, keyed by user id so one account's
// status never answers for another. A guest makes no request. The key sits under the 'me' root, so
// useAdminAccess's invalidation of ['me'] refetches it after an admin grant or revoke.
import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query';

import { apiFetch } from '../clients/apiClient';
import { HTTP_STATUS_OK } from '../constants/appConfig';
import type { ProPlan } from '../constants/proProducts';

import { useSignedInUserId } from './AuthProvider';

export type ProStatus = { expiresAt: string | null; isPro: boolean; product: ProPlan | null };

export type ProStatusState =
  | { status: 'guest' }
  | { status: 'loading' }
  | { retry: () => void; status: 'error' }
  | ({ status: 'ready' } & ProStatus);

function isExpiry(value: unknown): value is string | null {
  return value === null || (typeof value === 'string' && !Number.isNaN(Date.parse(value)));
}

function isPlan(value: unknown): value is ProPlan | null {
  return value === null || value === 'annual' || value === 'lifetime';
}

// The pro object of a GET /me body, or null when it is missing or any field has the wrong shape.
function parseProStatus(body: unknown): ProStatus | null {
  const pro = (body as { data?: { pro?: unknown } } | null)?.data?.pro;
  if (typeof pro !== 'object' || pro === null) return null;
  const { expiresAt, isActive, product } = pro as Record<string, unknown>;
  if (typeof isActive !== 'boolean' || !isExpiry(expiresAt) || !isPlan(product)) return null;
  return { expiresAt, isPro: isActive, product };
}

export async function fetchProStatus(): Promise<ProStatus> {
  const { body, status } = await apiFetch('me');
  const pro = status === HTTP_STATUS_OK ? parseProStatus(body) : null;
  if (pro === null) throw new Error(`profile request failed with ${status}`);
  return pro;
}

export function buildProStatusKey(userId: string | null) {
  return ['me', userId, 'pro'] as const;
}

export function useProStatus(): ProStatusState {
  const userId = useSignedInUserId();
  const { data, isError, refetch } = useQuery({
    enabled: userId !== null,
    queryFn: fetchProStatus,
    queryKey: buildProStatusKey(userId),
  });
  if (userId === null) return { status: 'guest' };
  if (data) return { ...data, status: 'ready' };
  if (isError) return { retry: () => void refetch(), status: 'error' };
  return { status: 'loading' };
}
```
