```tsx
// The admin route, app/admin.tsx, on native. The real AdminScreen, AuthProvider, StatsProvider,
// query client, useProStatus, and apiFetch/apiPut run against a routed fetch stand-in:
// - an admin sees one h1 "Admin" and one switch, "Pro (admin grant)", checked when isGranted;
// - Pro bought through a store shows as "Pro (purchased)", checked and disabled;
// - a toggle sends one PUT admin/access { isGranted }, keeps the switch disabled while it is in
//   flight, and shows what the response says; a 400, 429, 503, or network failure puts the switch
//   back and shows one alert with no code, message, request id, or status;
// - a signed-in non-admin, and an admin the server answers 403, see "not available" with no switch
//   and send no PUT; a guest, or an admin who signs out, is sent to "/" with one router.replace;
// - after a toggle the user's Pro status (useProStatus) follows without a reload;
// - a malformed GET admin/access reply shows the load-failed state;
// - after admin A signs out and non-admin B signs in on the same query client, B sees no Admin
//   link and the not-available state, and sends no PUT.
// Identities, passwords, and request ids are built at run time.
import { randomBytes } from 'node:crypto';

import AsyncStorage from '@react-native-async-storage/async-storage';
import { QueryClientProvider, type QueryClient } from '@tanstack/react-query';
import { act, fireEvent, render, screen, waitFor, within } from '@testing-library/react-native';

import { escapeForRegExp } from '../../components/auth/__tests__/passwordSettingsTestSupport';
import { setExpoExtra } from '../../config/expoConstantsMock';
import { createQueryClient } from '../../config/queryClient';
import { settle } from '../../config/settle';
import {
  AUTH_STORAGE_KEY,
  SESSION_TOKEN_KEY,
  buildIdentity,
  holdReply,
  installRoutedFetch,
  type FakeReply,
  type RouteReply,
  type SignInIdentity,
} from '../../state/__tests__/authTestSupport';
import { AuthProvider, useAuth } from '../../state/AuthProvider';
import { ContentProvider } from '../../state/ContentProvider';
import { OwnedStatsProvider } from '../../state/OwnedStatsProvider';
import { useProStatus } from '../../state/useProStatus';
import AdminScreen from '../admin';
import SettingsScreen from '../settings';

import {
  ACCESS_PATH,
  ACCESS_ROUTE,
  ACCESS_UPDATE_ROUTE,
  ADMIN_GRANT_NAME,
  NOT_AVAILABLE_TEXT,
  PROFILE_ROUTE,
  PURCHASED_NAME,
  buildEntry,
  buildErrorReply,
  entryReply,
  meReply,
  rawEntryReply,
  sessionReply,
} from './adminAccessTestSupport';

setExpoExtra({ apiBaseUrl: 'https://api.syntactical.dev/v1/' });

jest.mock('expo-secure-store', () => {
  const values = new Map<string, string>();
  return {
    mockValues: values,
    getItemAsync: jest.fn((key: string) => Promise.resolve(values.get(key) ?? null)),
    setItemAsync: jest.fn((key: string, value: string) => {
      values.set(key, value);
      return Promise.resolve();
    }),
    deleteItemAsync: jest.fn((key: string) => {
      values.delete(key);
      return Promise.resolve();
    }),
  };
});

jest.mock('../../state/SyncProvider', () => ({
  useSync: () => ({
    cancelPass: () => undefined,
    isSyncing: false,
    isUploadCapReached: false,
    syncNow: () => Promise.resolve(true),
  }),
}));

const mockReplace = jest.fn();

jest.mock('expo-router', () =>
  require('../../config/buildExpoRouterMock').buildExpoRouterMock({
    replace: (...args: unknown[]) => mockReplace(...args),
    readParams: () => ({}),
  }),
);

type SecureStoreMock = { mockValues: Map<string, string> };
const secureStore = jest.requireMock('expo-secure-store') as SecureStoreMock;

type Element = ReturnType<typeof screen.getByRole>;

let queryClient: QueryClient;
const latestPro: { status: string } = { status: '' };

// Shows what useProStatus reads, so a test can see it follow an admin change.
function ProStatusProbe() {
  const state = useProStatus();
  latestPro.status = state.status === 'ready' ? (state.isPro ? 'pro' : 'free') : state.status;
  return null;
}

async function signIn(identity: SignInIdentity): Promise<void> {
  await AsyncStorage.setItem(
    AUTH_STORAGE_KEY,
    JSON.stringify({ knownUserIds: [identity.userId], userId: identity.userId }),
  );
  secureStore.mockValues.set(SESSION_TOKEN_KEY, identity.sessionValue);
}

async function renderAdmin(): Promise<void> {
  await render(
    <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
      <ContentProvider contentBaseUrl={null}>
        <AuthProvider>
          <OwnedStatsProvider>
            <AdminScreen />
            <ProStatusProbe />
          </OwnedStatsProvider>
        </AuthProvider>
      </ContentProvider>
    </QueryClientProvider>,
  );
}

function readIsDisabled(element: Element): boolean {
  const { accessibilityState, disabled } = element.props as {
    accessibilityState?: { disabled?: boolean };
    disabled?: boolean;
  };
  return disabled === true || accessibilityState?.disabled === true || element.props['aria-disabled'] === true;
}

async function renderSignedInAdmin(routes: Record<string, RouteReply | RouteReply[]>, name = ADMIN_GRANT_NAME) {
  const identity = buildIdentity();
  const routed = installRoutedFetch({ [PROFILE_ROUTE]: meReply(identity.email, { isAdmin: true }), ...routes });
  await signIn(identity);
  await renderAdmin();
  await screen.findByRole('switch', { name });
  return { ...routed, identity };
}

function listAccessUpdates(requests: { method: string; path: string; body: unknown }[]) {
  return requests.filter(({ method, path }) => method === 'PUT' && path === ACCESS_PATH);
}

beforeEach(async () => {
  await AsyncStorage.clear();
  secureStore.mockValues.clear();
  queryClient = createQueryClient();
  latestPro.status = '';
  mockReplace.mockClear();
});

afterEach(async () => {
  await settle();
  queryClient.clear();
});

describe('admin route for an admin', () => {
  it('shows one h1 "Admin" and one switch, "Pro (admin grant)", unchecked and enabled with no grant', async () => {
    await renderSignedInAdmin({ [ACCESS_ROUTE]: entryReply(buildEntry(null)) });
    const level1 = screen
      .getAllByRole('heading')
      .filter((heading) => (heading.props['aria-level'] ?? heading.props.accessibilityLevel) === 1);
    expect(level1).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(level1[0]).toHaveTextContent(/^Admin$/);
    expect(screen.getAllByRole('switch')).toHaveLength(1);
    const proSwitch = screen.getByRole('switch', { name: ADMIN_GRANT_NAME });
    expect(proSwitch).not.toBeChecked();
    expect(readIsDisabled(proSwitch)).toBe(false);
  });

  it('checks the switch for an admin grant and leaves it enabled', async () => {
    await renderSignedInAdmin({ [ACCESS_ROUTE]: entryReply(buildEntry('admin')) });
    const proSwitch = screen.getByRole('switch', { name: ADMIN_GRANT_NAME });
    expect(proSwitch).toBeChecked();
    expect(readIsDisabled(proSwitch)).toBe(false);
  });

  it('shows store-bought Pro as "Pro (purchased)": checked and disabled', async () => {
    await renderSignedInAdmin({ [ACCESS_ROUTE]: entryReply(buildEntry('purchase')) }, PURCHASED_NAME);
    const proSwitch = screen.getByRole('switch', { name: PURCHASED_NAME });
    expect(proSwitch).toBeChecked();
    expect(readIsDisabled(proSwitch)).toBe(true);
    expect(screen.queryByRole('switch', { name: ADMIN_GRANT_NAME })).toBeNull();
  });

  it('draws the switch as a track and thumb hidden from assistive technology, still role switch', async () => {
    await renderSignedInAdmin({ [ACCESS_ROUTE]: entryReply(buildEntry(null)) });
    const proSwitch = screen.getByRole('switch', { name: ADMIN_GRANT_NAME });
    for (const testID of ['switch-track-off', 'switch-thumb-off']) {
      const part = within(proSwitch).getByTestId(testID, { includeHiddenElements: true });
      expect(part.props['aria-hidden']).toBe(true);
    }
    const track = within(proSwitch).getByTestId('switch-track-off', { includeHiddenElements: true });
    expect(track.props.importantForAccessibility).toBe('no-hide-descendants');
    expect(within(proSwitch).queryByTestId('switch-track-off')).toBeNull();
  });
});

describe('admin route toggles', () => {
  it('grants with one PUT { isGranted: true }, disabled while in flight, then checked', async () => {
    const held = holdReply();
    const { requests } = await renderSignedInAdmin({
      [ACCESS_ROUTE]: entryReply(buildEntry(null)),
      [ACCESS_UPDATE_ROUTE]: held,
    });
    await fireEvent.press(screen.getByRole('switch', { name: ADMIN_GRANT_NAME }));
    await waitFor(() => expect(listAccessUpdates(requests)).toHaveLength(1));
    expect(readIsDisabled(screen.getByRole('switch', { name: ADMIN_GRANT_NAME }))).toBe(true);
    expect(listAccessUpdates(requests)[0].body).toEqual({ isGranted: true });

    await act(async () => {
      held.release(entryReply(buildEntry('admin')) as FakeReply);
    });
    await waitFor(() => expect(readIsDisabled(screen.getByRole('switch', { name: ADMIN_GRANT_NAME }))).toBe(false));
    expect(screen.getByRole('switch', { name: ADMIN_GRANT_NAME })).toBeChecked();
    await settle();
    expect(listAccessUpdates(requests)).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(screen.queryByRole('alert')).toBeNull();
  });

  it('revokes an admin grant with one PUT { isGranted: false }, then unchecked', async () => {
    const { requests } = await renderSignedInAdmin({
      [ACCESS_ROUTE]: entryReply(buildEntry('admin')),
      [ACCESS_UPDATE_ROUTE]: entryReply(buildEntry(null)),
    });
    await fireEvent.press(screen.getByRole('switch', { name: ADMIN_GRANT_NAME }));
    await waitFor(() => expect(screen.getByRole('switch', { name: ADMIN_GRANT_NAME })).not.toBeChecked());
    await settle();
    expect(listAccessUpdates(requests).map(({ body }) => body)).toEqual([{ isGranted: false }]);
  });

  it('shows what the response says: a revoke answered as purchased becomes "Pro (purchased)", checked and disabled', async () => {
    await renderSignedInAdmin({
      [ACCESS_ROUTE]: entryReply(buildEntry('admin')),
      [ACCESS_UPDATE_ROUTE]: entryReply(buildEntry('purchase')),
    });
    await fireEvent.press(screen.getByRole('switch', { name: ADMIN_GRANT_NAME }));
    const purchased = await screen.findByRole('switch', { name: PURCHASED_NAME });
    expect(purchased).toBeChecked();
    expect(readIsDisabled(purchased)).toBe(true);
  });

  const failures: { label: string; build: () => { reply: FakeReply; secrets: string[] } }[] = [
    {
      label: '400 INVALID_BODY',
      build: () => {
        const error = buildErrorReply(400, 'INVALID_BODY', 'Invalid request body');
        return { reply: error.reply, secrets: [error.code, error.message, error.requestId, '400'] };
      },
    },
    {
      label: '429 RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED',
      build: () => {
        const error = buildErrorReply(429, 'RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED', 'Too many requests');
        return { reply: error.reply, secrets: [error.code, error.message, error.requestId, '429'] };
      },
    },
    {
      label: '503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE',
      build: () => {
        const error = buildErrorReply(503, 'SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE', 'Database unavailable');
        return { reply: error.reply, secrets: [error.code, error.message, error.requestId, '503'] };
      },
    },
    {
      label: 'a network failure',
      build: () => ({ reply: 'reject', secrets: ['Network request failed', 'TypeError'] }),
    },
    {
      label: 'a malformed 200',
      build: () => ({ reply: rawEntryReply({ isGranted: 'yes' }), secrets: ['yes'] }),
    },
  ];

  it.each(failures)('puts the switch back and shows one alert with no internal detail on $label', async ({ build }) => {
    const { reply, secrets } = build();
    const { requests } = await renderSignedInAdmin({
      [ACCESS_ROUTE]: entryReply(buildEntry(null)),
      [ACCESS_UPDATE_ROUTE]: reply,
    });
    await fireEvent.press(screen.getByRole('switch', { name: ADMIN_GRANT_NAME }));
    const alert = await screen.findByRole('alert');
    await waitFor(() => expect(readIsDisabled(screen.getByRole('switch', { name: ADMIN_GRANT_NAME }))).toBe(false));
    await settle();
    expect(screen.getByRole('switch', { name: ADMIN_GRANT_NAME })).not.toBeChecked();
    expect(screen.getAllByRole('alert')).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(listAccessUpdates(requests)).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(alert).toHaveTextContent(/\S/);
    for (const secret of secrets) expect(alert).not.toHaveTextContent(new RegExp(escapeForRegExp(secret)));
  });
});

describe('admin route keeps the Pro status current', () => {
  it('makes useProStatus read Pro after a grant and free after a revoke, without a reload', async () => {
    const identity = buildIdentity();
    const { setRoute } = installRoutedFetch({
      [ACCESS_ROUTE]: entryReply(buildEntry(null)),
      [ACCESS_UPDATE_ROUTE]: entryReply(buildEntry('admin')),
      [PROFILE_ROUTE]: meReply(identity.email, { isAdmin: true }),
    });
    await signIn(identity);
    await renderAdmin();
    await screen.findByRole('switch', { name: ADMIN_GRANT_NAME });
    await waitFor(() => expect(latestPro.status).toBe('free'));

    // The server's state once the grant commits.
    setRoute(PROFILE_ROUTE, meReply(identity.email, { isAdmin: true, isPro: true }));
    await fireEvent.press(screen.getByRole('switch', { name: ADMIN_GRANT_NAME }));
    await waitFor(() => expect(screen.getByRole('switch', { name: ADMIN_GRANT_NAME })).toBeChecked());
    await waitFor(() => expect(latestPro.status).toBe('pro'));

    // And once the revoke commits.
    setRoute(ACCESS_UPDATE_ROUTE, entryReply(buildEntry(null)));
    setRoute(PROFILE_ROUTE, meReply(identity.email, { isAdmin: true }));
    await waitFor(() => expect(readIsDisabled(screen.getByRole('switch', { name: ADMIN_GRANT_NAME }))).toBe(false));
    await fireEvent.press(screen.getByRole('switch', { name: ADMIN_GRANT_NAME }));
    await waitFor(() => expect(screen.getByRole('switch', { name: ADMIN_GRANT_NAME })).not.toBeChecked());
    await waitFor(() => expect(latestPro.status).toBe('free'));
  });
});

describe('admin route for anyone who is not an admin', () => {
  async function expectNotAvailable(requests: { method: string; path: string; body: unknown }[]): Promise<void> {
    await screen.findByText(NOT_AVAILABLE_TEXT);
    await settle();
    expect(screen.queryAllByRole('switch')).toHaveLength(0);
    expect(listAccessUpdates(requests)).toHaveLength(0);
  }

  it('shows a signed-in non-admin the not-available state with no switch and no PUT, and no replace', async () => {
    const identity = buildIdentity();
    const { requests } = installRoutedFetch({
      [ACCESS_ROUTE]: buildErrorReply(403, 'ADMIN_REQUIRED', 'Admin required').reply,
      [PROFILE_ROUTE]: meReply(identity.email, { isAdmin: false }),
    });
    await signIn(identity);
    await renderAdmin();
    await expectNotAvailable(requests);
    expect(mockReplace).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  it('shows the same state when GET me says admin but GET admin/access answers 403, with no server detail', async () => {
    const identity = buildIdentity();
    const forbidden = buildErrorReply(403, 'ADMIN_REQUIRED', 'Admin required');
    const { requests } = installRoutedFetch({
      [ACCESS_ROUTE]: forbidden.reply,
      [PROFILE_ROUTE]: meReply(identity.email, { isAdmin: true }),
    });
    await signIn(identity);
    await renderAdmin();
    await expectNotAvailable(requests);
    expect(screen.queryByText(/ADMIN_REQUIRED/)).toBeNull();
    expect(screen.queryByText(new RegExp(forbidden.requestId))).toBeNull();
  });

  it('sends a guest to the home page with one replace, no GET admin/access, and no PUT', async () => {
    const { requests } = installRoutedFetch({
      [ACCESS_ROUTE]: buildErrorReply(401, 'SESSION_REQUIRED', 'Sign-in required').reply,
    });
    await renderAdmin();
    await waitFor(() => expect(mockReplace).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1));
    await settle();
    expect(mockReplace).toHaveBeenCalledWith('/');
    expect(screen.queryByText(NOT_AVAILABLE_TEXT)).toBeNull();
    expect(requests.some(({ method, path }) => method === 'GET' && path === ACCESS_PATH)).toBe(false);
    expect(listAccessUpdates(requests)).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});

describe('admin route with a malformed access entry', () => {
  it.each([
    ['a non-boolean isGranted', { grantSource: 'admin', isGranted: 'true', productId: 'syntactical.pro.lifetime' }],
    ['an unknown grantSource', { grantSource: 'gift', isGranted: true, productId: 'syntactical.pro.lifetime' }],
    ['a list instead of one entry', [buildEntry('admin')]],
  ])('shows the load-failed state with no switch and no PUT for %s', async (_label, data) => {
    const identity = buildIdentity();
    const { requests } = installRoutedFetch({
      [ACCESS_ROUTE]: rawEntryReply(data),
      [PROFILE_ROUTE]: meReply(identity.email, { isAdmin: true }),
    });
    await signIn(identity);
    await renderAdmin();
    await screen.findByText(/could not be loaded/i);
    expect(screen.queryByText(NOT_AVAILABLE_TEXT)).toBeNull();
    expect(screen.queryAllByRole('switch')).toHaveLength(0);
    expect(listAccessUpdates(requests)).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  it('ignores an extra field on the entry and shows its value nowhere', async () => {
    const marker = `marker-${randomBytes(6).toString('hex')}`;
    await renderSignedInAdmin({ [ACCESS_ROUTE]: rawEntryReply({ ...buildEntry(null), displayName: marker }) });
    expect(screen.getByRole('switch', { name: ADMIN_GRANT_NAME })).not.toBeChecked();
    expect(screen.queryByText(new RegExp(escapeForRegExp(marker)))).toBeNull();
  });
});

describe('admin route when the admin signs out', () => {
  const authHandle: { current: ReturnType<typeof useAuth> | null } = { current: null };

  function AuthHandle() {
    authHandle.current = useAuth();
    return null;
  }

  it('replaces to the home page once, with no not-available text', async () => {
    const identity = buildIdentity();
    installRoutedFetch({
      [ACCESS_ROUTE]: entryReply(buildEntry(null)),
      [PROFILE_ROUTE]: meReply(identity.email, { isAdmin: true }),
      'DELETE auth/sessions/current': { status: 204 },
    });
    await signIn(identity);
    await render(
      <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
        <ContentProvider contentBaseUrl={null}>
          <AuthProvider>
            <OwnedStatsProvider>
              <AuthHandle />
              <AdminScreen />
            </OwnedStatsProvider>
          </AuthProvider>
        </ContentProvider>
      </QueryClientProvider>,
    );
    await screen.findByRole('switch', { name: ADMIN_GRANT_NAME });
    expect(mockReplace).not.toHaveBeenCalled();

    await act(async () => {
      await authHandle.current?.signOut();
    });
    await waitFor(() => expect(mockReplace).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1));
    await settle();
    expect(mockReplace).toHaveBeenCalledWith('/');
    expect(screen.queryByText(NOT_AVAILABLE_TEXT)).toBeNull();
  });

  it('shows non-admin B no Admin link and the not-available state after admin A signs out', async () => {
    const adminA = buildIdentity();
    const memberB = buildIdentity();
    const { requests, setRoute } = installRoutedFetch({
      [ACCESS_ROUTE]: entryReply(buildEntry(null)),
      [PROFILE_ROUTE]: meReply(adminA.email, { isAdmin: true }),
      'DELETE auth/sessions/current': { status: 204 },
      'POST auth/sessions/password': sessionReply(memberB),
    });
    await signIn(adminA);
    await render(
      <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
        <ContentProvider contentBaseUrl={null}>
          <AuthProvider>
            <OwnedStatsProvider>
              <AuthHandle />
              <AdminScreen />
              <SettingsScreen />
            </OwnedStatsProvider>
          </AuthProvider>
        </ContentProvider>
      </QueryClientProvider>,
    );
    await screen.findByRole('switch', { name: ADMIN_GRANT_NAME });
    await screen.findByRole('link', { name: 'Admin' });

    await act(async () => {
      await authHandle.current?.signOut();
    });
    await waitFor(() => expect(screen.queryByRole('link', { name: 'Admin' })).toBeNull());

    setRoute(PROFILE_ROUTE, meReply(memberB.email, { isAdmin: false }));
    setRoute(ACCESS_ROUTE, buildErrorReply(403, 'ADMIN_REQUIRED', 'Admin required').reply);
    const password = randomBytes(12).toString('hex');
    await act(async () => {
      const result = await authHandle.current?.signInWithPassword(memberB.email, password);
      expect(result).toEqual({ isOk: true });
    });

    await screen.findByLabelText('New password');
    await screen.findByText(NOT_AVAILABLE_TEXT);
    await settle();
    expect(screen.queryByRole('link', { name: 'Admin' })).toBeNull();
    expect(screen.queryAllByRole('switch')).toHaveLength(0);
    expect(listAccessUpdates(requests)).toHaveLength(0);
    const accessReads = requests.filter(({ method, path }) => method === 'GET' && path === ACCESS_PATH);
    expect(accessReads[accessReads.length - 1].headers.authorization).toContain(memberB.sessionValue);
  });
});
```

`app/__tests__/adminRoute.web.test.tsx`, rewritten in full:

```tsx
// The admin route on the web. The real AdminScreen, AuthProvider, StatsProvider, query client, and
// apiFetch/apiPut run in the DOM against a routed fetch stand-in:
// - the page has one h1, "Admin", and no element with a positive tabindex;
// - the one switch is reachable by keyboard (natively focusable or tabindex 0) and operable with
//   Space or Enter: one PUT admin/access { isGranted } goes out with the cookie credentials and the
//   CSRF header, and the switch shows the response;
// - "Pro (purchased)" is disabled, so a key press on it sends nothing.
// A browser activates a focused native checkbox on Space and a native button on Space or Enter by
// dispatching a click; jsdom does not, so pressKey dispatches that click for those elements when
// the key event was not cancelled. Any other element must handle the key itself.
import AsyncStorage from '@react-native-async-storage/async-storage';
import { QueryClientProvider, type QueryClient } from '@tanstack/react-query';
import { act, fireEvent, render, screen, waitFor } from '@testing-library/react';

import { setExpoExtra } from '../../config/expoConstantsMock';
import { createQueryClient } from '../../config/queryClient';
import { settle } from '../../config/settle';
import {
  AUTH_STORAGE_KEY,
  buildIdentity,
  installRoutedFetch,
  type RoutedRequest,
} from '../../state/__tests__/authTestSupport';
import { AuthProvider } from '../../state/AuthProvider';
import { ContentProvider } from '../../state/ContentProvider';
import { OwnedStatsProvider } from '../../state/OwnedStatsProvider';
import AdminScreen from '../admin';

import {
  ACCESS_PATH,
  ACCESS_ROUTE,
  ACCESS_UPDATE_ROUTE,
  ADMIN_GRANT_NAME,
  PROFILE_ROUTE,
  PURCHASED_NAME,
  buildEntry,
  entryReply,
  meReply,

let queryClient: QueryClient;

type KeyName = ' ' | 'Enter';
const KEY_CODES: Record<KeyName, string> = { ' ': 'Space', Enter: 'Enter' };

async function renderSignedInAdmin(routes: Parameters<typeof installRoutedFetch>[0], name = ADMIN_GRANT_NAME) {
  const identity = buildIdentity();
  const routed = installRoutedFetch({ [PROFILE_ROUTE]: meReply(identity.email, { isAdmin: true }), ...routes });
  await AsyncStorage.setItem(
    AUTH_STORAGE_KEY,
    JSON.stringify({ knownUserIds: [identity.userId], userId: identity.userId }),
  );
  const rendered = render(
    <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
      <ContentProvider contentBaseUrl={null}>
        <AuthProvider>
          <OwnedStatsProvider>
            <AdminScreen />
          </OwnedStatsProvider>
        </AuthProvider>
      </ContentProvider>
    </QueryClientProvider>,
  );
  await screen.findByRole('switch', { name });
  return { ...routed, rendered };
}

function readIsChecked(element: HTMLElement): boolean {
  if (element instanceof HTMLInputElement) return element.checked;
  return element.getAttribute('aria-checked') === 'true';
}

function readIsDisabled(element: HTMLElement): boolean {
  return (element as HTMLInputElement).disabled === true || element.getAttribute('aria-disabled') === 'true';
}

function readsAsNativeActivation(element: HTMLElement, key: KeyName): boolean {
  if (element instanceof HTMLInputElement && element.type === 'checkbox') return key === ' ';
  return element instanceof HTMLButtonElement;
}

async function pressKey(element: HTMLElement, key: KeyName): Promise<void> {
  await act(async () => {
    element.focus();
    const code = KEY_CODES[key];
    const isNotCancelled = fireEvent.keyDown(element, { code, key });
    fireEvent.keyUp(element, { code, key });
    if (isNotCancelled && readsAsNativeActivation(element, key) && !readIsDisabled(element)) fireEvent.click(element);
  });
}

function listAccessUpdates(requests: RoutedRequest[]): RoutedRequest[] {
  return requests.filter(({ method, path }) => method === 'PUT' && path === ACCESS_PATH);
}

// Space first; Enter only when Space sent nothing, so a switch that answers either key sends one PUT.
async function operateByKeyboard(element: HTMLElement, requests: RoutedRequest[]): Promise<void> {
  const before = listAccessUpdates(requests).length;
  await pressKey(element, ' ');
  await settle();
  if (listAccessUpdates(requests).length === before) {
    await pressKey(element, 'Enter');
    await settle();
  }
}

afterEach(async () => {

      (element) => Number(element.getAttribute('tabindex')) > 0,
    );

  });

  it('grants by keyboard with one PUT { isGranted: true } carrying the CSRF header and cookie credentials', async () => {

    const proSwitch = screen.getByRole('switch', { name: ADMIN_GRANT_NAME });
    expect(['BUTTON', 'INPUT'].includes(proSwitch.tagName) || proSwitch.getAttribute('tabindex') === '0').toBe(true);
    await operateByKeyboard(proSwitch, requests);
```

`services/admin/parseAccessEntry.ts`, replaced in full:

```ts
// The admin's one Pro access entry from GET and PUT admin/access, or null when the shape is wrong.
// grantSource 'purchase' means an active store purchase of either Pro product (annual or lifetime),
// which the admin cannot switch.
export type AccessEntry = { grantSource: 'admin' | 'purchase' | null; isGranted: boolean; productId: string };

export function parseAccessEntry(value: unknown): AccessEntry | null {
  if (typeof value !== 'object' || value === null || Array.isArray(value)) return null;
  const { grantSource, isGranted, productId } = value as Record<string, unknown>;
  if (typeof productId !== 'string' || typeof isGranted !== 'boolean') return null;
  if (grantSource !== 'admin' && grantSource !== 'purchase' && grantSource !== null) return null;
  return { grantSource, isGranted, productId };
}
```

`state/useAdminAccess.ts`, replaced in full:

```ts
// The admin's own Pro grant: GET admin/access reads the one entry, and setAccess sends PUT
// admin/access { isGranted }. The entry changes only from the server's reply to a PUT, so a refused
// or failed change leaves the switch where it was. A change refreshes the 'me' queries, so
// useProStatus follows without a reload. Only a 401 or 403 means the page is not available to this
// account; any other failed load can be retried.
import { useCallback, useState } from 'react';

import { useQuery, useQueryClient } from '@tanstack/react-query';

import { apiFetch, apiPut } from '../clients/apiClient';
import { HTTP_STATUS_FORBIDDEN, HTTP_STATUS_OK, HTTP_STATUS_UNAUTHORIZED } from '../constants/appConfig';
import { parseAccessEntry, type AccessEntry } from '../services/admin/parseAccessEntry';

import { useSignedInUserId } from './AuthProvider';

export type AdminAccessState =
  | { status: 'loading' }
  | { status: 'unavailable' }
  | { retry: () => void; status: 'failed' }
  | { entry: AccessEntry; status: 'ready' };

const ACCESS_PATH = 'admin/access';

class AccessRefused extends Error {}

function readEntry(body: unknown): AccessEntry | null {
  return parseAccessEntry((body as { data?: unknown } | null)?.data);
}

async function fetchAccessEntry(): Promise<AccessEntry> {
  const { body, status } = await apiFetch(ACCESS_PATH);
  if (status === HTTP_STATUS_UNAUTHORIZED || status === HTTP_STATUS_FORBIDDEN) {
    throw new AccessRefused(`admin access request answered ${status}`);
  }
  const entry = status === HTTP_STATUS_OK ? readEntry(body) : null;
  if (entry === null) throw new Error(`admin access request answered ${status}`);
  return entry;
}

export function buildAdminAccessKey(userId: string | null) {
  return ['admin', 'access', userId] as const;
}

export function useAdminAccess() {
  const userId = useSignedInUserId();
  const queryClient = useQueryClient();
  const [isPending, setIsPending] = useState(false);
  const [isFailed, setIsFailed] = useState(false);

  const { data, error, isError, refetch } = useQuery({
    enabled: userId !== null,
    queryFn: fetchAccessEntry,
    queryKey: buildAdminAccessKey(userId),
    refetchOnMount: 'always',
  });

  const setAccess = useCallback(
    async (isGranted: boolean): Promise<void> => {
      setIsFailed(false);
      setIsPending(true);
      try {
        const { body, status } = await apiPut(ACCESS_PATH, { isGranted });
        const entry = status === HTTP_STATUS_OK ? readEntry(body) : null;
        if (entry === null) throw new Error(`admin access update answered ${status}`);
        queryClient.setQueryData<AccessEntry>(buildAdminAccessKey(userId), entry);
        void queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['me'] });
      } catch {
        setIsFailed(true);
      } finally {
        setIsPending(false);
      }
    },
    [queryClient, userId],
  );

  let state: AdminAccessState = { status: 'loading' };
  const isRefused = isError && error instanceof AccessRefused;
  if (userId === null || isRefused) state = { status: 'unavailable' };
  else if (data !== undefined) state = { entry: data, status: 'ready' };
  else if (isError) state = { retry: () => void refetch(), status: 'failed' };
  return { isFailed, isPending, setAccess, state };
}
```

`app/admin.tsx`, replaced in full:

```tsx
// Admin route: an admin grants or revokes Pro on their own account. The server decides who is an
// admin; a signed-in non-admin (the server answers 403) sees the not-available text, and any other
// failed load shows a load-failed text with a Retry button. Every state shows the one h1. Until the
// stored sign-in is read the page shows the loading state. With no signed-in user (a guest, or
// after sign-out) the screen replaces itself with the home page. Pro bought through a store shows
// as "Pro (purchased)" and cannot be switched here. A refused or failed change is announced in one
// fixed message.
import { useEffect } from 'react';
import { Pressable, ScrollView, Text, View } from 'react-native';

import { router } from 'expo-router';

import { AuthButton } from '../components/auth/AuthButton';
import type { AccessEntry } from '../services/admin/parseAccessEntry';
import { useAuth, useSignedInUserId } from '../state/AuthProvider';
import { useAdminAccess } from '../state/useAdminAccess';

const CHANGE_FAILED = 'The change was not saved. Check your connection and try again.';
const NOT_AVAILABLE = 'This page is not available.';
const LOAD_FAILED = 'Your access could not be loaded. Check your connection and try again.';
const ADMIN_GRANT_LABEL = 'Pro (admin grant)';
const PURCHASED_LABEL = 'Pro (purchased)';

type ProSwitchProps = { entry: AccessEntry; isPending: boolean; onToggle: (isGranted: boolean) => void };

function ProSwitch({ entry, isPending, onToggle }: ProSwitchProps) {
  const { grantSource, isGranted } = entry;
  const isPurchased = grantSource === 'purchase';
  const isDisabled = isPurchased || isPending;
  const label = isPurchased ? PURCHASED_LABEL : ADMIN_GRANT_LABEL;
  return (
    <View className="flex-row items-center justify-between border-b border-line py-3">
      <Text className="text-sm text-ink">{label}</Text>
      <Pressable
        role="switch"
        aria-label={label}
        aria-checked={isGranted}
        aria-disabled={isDisabled}
        disabled={isDisabled}
        onPress={() => onToggle(!isGranted)}
        className={`flex-row items-center gap-2 rounded-full ${isDisabled ? 'opacity-50' : ''}`}
      >
        <View
          testID={isGranted ? 'switch-track-on' : 'switch-track-off'}
          aria-hidden
          importantForAccessibility="no-hide-descendants"
          className={`h-7 w-12 justify-center rounded-full border-2 px-0.5 ${isGranted ? 'border-signal bg-signal' : 'border-ink bg-surface-raised'}`}
        >
          <View
            testID={isGranted ? 'switch-thumb-on' : 'switch-thumb-off'}
            aria-hidden
            className={`h-5 w-5 rounded-full ${isGranted ? 'self-end bg-obsidian' : 'self-start bg-ink'}`}
          />
        </View>
        <Text className="w-8 font-mono text-xs uppercase tracking-widest text-ink">{isGranted ? 'On' : 'Off'}</Text>
      </Pressable>
    </View>
  );
}

export default function AdminScreen() {
  const { isFailed, isPending, setAccess, state: loadedState } = useAdminAccess();
  const { isHydrated } = useAuth();
  const isSignedOut = useSignedInUserId() === null;
  const shouldLeave = isHydrated && isSignedOut;
  const state = isHydrated ? loadedState : ({ status: 'loading' } as const);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (shouldLeave) router.replace('/');
  }, [shouldLeave]);

  if (shouldLeave) return null;

  return (
    <ScrollView contentContainerClassName="flex-grow items-center px-4 py-8">
      <View className="w-full max-w-xl">
        <Text role="heading" aria-level={1} className="font-mono text-3xl text-ink">
          Admin
        </Text>
        {state.status === 'unavailable' ? (
          <Text className="mt-6 font-mono text-sm text-ink">{NOT_AVAILABLE}</Text>
        ) : null}
        {state.status === 'failed' ? (
          <View className="mt-6">
            <Text role="alert" className="font-mono text-sm text-ink">
              {LOAD_FAILED}
            </Text>
            <AuthButton isPrimary={false} label="Retry" onPress={state.retry} />
          </View>
        ) : null}
        {state.status === 'ready' ? (
          <View className="mt-6">
            <ProSwitch entry={state.entry} isPending={isPending} onToggle={(isGranted) => void setAccess(isGranted)} />
          </View>
        ) : null}
        {isFailed ? (
          <Text role="alert" className="mt-3 text-sm text-ink">
            {CHANGE_FAILED}
          </Text>
        ) : null}
      </View>
    </ScrollView>
  );
}
```

`clients/isLoopbackUrl.ts`:

```ts
// True for an http URL on a loopback host, any port: the only kind of API base URL the e2e build
// can carry (app.config.ts accepts no other for E2E_API_BASE_URL, and its LOOPBACK_HOSTS list must
// match this one; a test checks it). The fixture purchase store is chosen only under such a URL.
// Parsed with patterns, not URL, so it reads the same under Hermes and Node.
export const LOOPBACK_HOSTS: readonly string[] = ['127.0.0.1', 'localhost', '[::1]'];

// The authority of an http URL; no user info is allowed, so a loopback name cannot hide a host.
const HTTP_AUTHORITY = /^http:\/\/([^/?#@]+)(?:[/?#]|$)/i;
const HOST_AND_PORT = /^(\[[^\]]+\]|[^:]+)(?::\d{1,5})?$/;

export function isLoopbackUrl(value: string | null): boolean {
  if (value === null) return false;
  const authority = HTTP_AUTHORITY.exec(value)?.[1];
  const host = authority === undefined ? undefined : HOST_AND_PORT.exec(authority)?.[1];
  return host !== undefined && LOOPBACK_HOSTS.includes(host.toLowerCase());
}
```

`clients/types/PurchaseStoreClient.ts`:

```ts
// What usePurchases needs from a store: localized prices by product id, a purchase that says only
// whether the store call finished (never whether Pro is active; GET /me says that), and a restore.
// appUserId is the signed-in user's server id; the real stores know it from the purchaser identity
// and ignore it, and the fixture store puts it in its synthetic webhook event.
import type { WebPurchaseOutcome } from './WebPurchaseOutcome';

export type PurchaseStoreClient = {
  buyStoreProduct: (productId: string, appUserId: string | null) => Promise<WebPurchaseOutcome>;
  readStorePrices: () => Promise<Record<string, string>>;
  restoreStorePurchases: () => Promise<boolean>;
};
```

`clients/purchaseStoreClient.fixture.ts`:

```ts
// The fixture store for the e2e build, chosen only when the API base URL is an http loopback URL
// (clients/selectPurchaseStoreClient.ts) and never imported statically
// (scripts/__tests__/noFixtureInProduction.test.ts). Prices are fixed. A purchase posts a
// synthetic RevenueCat event for the signed-in user to the test-mode POST /v1/test/webhook, so the
// server's real webhook handling grants Pro and GET /me reports it, as a store purchase would; the
// app still confirms only through GET /me. There is nothing to restore.
import { HTTP_STATUS_OK } from '../constants/appConfig';
import { PRO_PRODUCT_IDS } from '../constants/proProducts';

import { apiFetch } from './apiClient';
import type { WebPurchaseOutcome } from './types/WebPurchaseOutcome';
import { generateUuid } from './uuidClient';

const ONE_YEAR_MS = 365 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;
const FIXTURE_PRICES: Readonly<Record<string, string>> = {
  [PRO_PRODUCT_IDS.ANNUAL]: '$19.99',
  [PRO_PRODUCT_IDS.LIFETIME]: '$39.99',
};

export function readStorePrices(): Promise<Record<string, string>> {
  return Promise.resolve({ ...FIXTURE_PRICES });
}

function buildEvent(productId: string, appUserId: string): Record<string, string | number> {
  const now = Date.now();
  const isAnnual = productId === PRO_PRODUCT_IDS.ANNUAL;
  return {
    app_user_id: appUserId,
    event_timestamp_ms: now,
    id: `fixture-${generateUuid()}`,
    product_id: productId,
    store: 'APP_STORE',
    type: isAnnual ? 'INITIAL_PURCHASE' : 'NON_RENEWING_PURCHASE',
    ...(isAnnual ? { expiration_at_ms: now + ONE_YEAR_MS } : {}),
  };
}

export async function buyStoreProduct(productId: string, appUserId: string | null): Promise<WebPurchaseOutcome> {
  if (appUserId === null || !Object.hasOwn(FIXTURE_PRICES, productId)) return 'unavailable';
  try {
    const { status } = await apiFetch('test/webhook', {
      body: { event: buildEvent(productId, appUserId) },
      method: 'POST',
    });
    return status === HTTP_STATUS_OK ? 'purchased' : 'unavailable';
  } catch {
    return 'unavailable';
  }
}

export function restoreStorePurchases(): Promise<boolean> {
  return Promise.resolve(false);
}
```

```ts
// scripts/__tests__/noFixtureInProduction.test.ts
// The fixture purchase store (clients/purchaseStoreClient.fixture.ts) is reachable only through
// the lazy require in clients/selectPurchaseStoreClient.ts, behind the loopback API URL guard. No
// file outside __tests__ directories, other than the fixture itself, may import it with a static
// import or export-from statement, so no production code path can pick it up by accident.
import { readFile, readdir } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { join, relative } from 'node:path';

const REPO_DIR = join(__dirname, '..', '..');
const SKIPPED_DIRS = new Set([
  'node_modules',
  'dist',
  '.git',
  '.expo',
  '.claude',
  'coverage',
  '__tests__',
  'packages',
  'pipeline',
  'server',
  'e2e',
]);
const SOURCE_FILE = /\.(ts|tsx|js|jsx|mjs|cjs)$/;
const FIXTURE_FILE = join('clients', 'purchaseStoreClient.fixture.ts');
const SELECTOR_FILE = join(REPO_DIR, 'clients', 'selectPurchaseStoreClient.ts');
const STATIC_IMPORT =
  /(?:^|\n)\s*(?:import|export)\b[^;]*?(?:from\s*)?['"][^'"]*purchaseStoreClient\.fixture(?:\.ts)?['"]/;

async function listSourceFiles(dir: string): Promise<string[]> {
  const files: string[] = [];
  for (const entry of await readdir(dir, { withFileTypes: true })) {
    if (SKIPPED_DIRS.has(entry.name)) continue;
    const path = join(dir, entry.name);
    if (entry.isDirectory()) files.push(...(await listSourceFiles(path)));
    else if (entry.isFile() && SOURCE_FILE.test(entry.name)) files.push(path);
  }
  return files;
}

describe('the fixture purchase store', () => {
  it('is imported statically by no app source file', async () => {
    const offending: string[] = [];
    for (const file of await listSourceFiles(REPO_DIR)) {
      const path = relative(REPO_DIR, file);
      if (path === FIXTURE_FILE) continue;
      if (STATIC_IMPORT.test(await readFile(file, 'utf8'))) offending.push(path);
    }
    expect(offending).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('is reached by the store selector only through a lazy require', async () => {
    const selector = await readFile(SELECTOR_FILE, 'utf8');
    expect(selector).toContain("require('./purchaseStoreClient.fixture')");
    expect(STATIC_IMPORT.test(selector)).toBe(false);
  });

  it.each([
    ["import { buyStoreProduct } from './purchaseStoreClient.fixture';", true],
    ["import * as store from '../clients/purchaseStoreClient.fixture';", true],
    ["export * from './purchaseStoreClient.fixture';", true],
    ["import './purchaseStoreClient.fixture';", true],
    ["const store = require('./purchaseStoreClient.fixture');", false],
    ["import { buyStoreProduct } from './purchaseStoreClient';", false],
  ])('classifies %s as a static import: %s', (source, expected) => {
    expect(STATIC_IMPORT.test(source)).toBe(expected);
  });
});
```

```tsx
});

    useApi(PRODUCTION_API);

    const { result } = await renderHook(() => usePurchases(), { wrapper: QueryWrapper });
    let outcome: string | undefined;
    await act(async () => {

    expect(nativeSdk.purchasedProductIds).toEqual([ANNUAL_PRODUCT]);
    expect(requests.some(({ path }) => path.includes('test/webhook'))).toBe(false);
  });
});
```

```ts
// The store behind usePurchases, chosen at call time: the fixture store when the build's API base
// URL is an http loopback URL (only the e2e build can carry one; app.config.ts refuses it
// elsewhere), else the platform's real store. The fixture is required lazily inside that branch
// and never imported statically (scripts/__tests__/noFixtureInProduction.test.ts).
// hasCheckoutRedirect says a finished purchase returns through /purchase-complete (Web Billing
// checkout) instead of being confirmed in place.
import { Platform } from 'react-native';

import { readExtraString } from '../config/readExtraString';

import { isLoopbackUrl } from './isLoopbackUrl';
import * as platformStore from './purchaseStoreClient';
import type { PurchaseStoreClient } from './types/PurchaseStoreClient';

export type SelectedStore = { client: PurchaseStoreClient; hasCheckoutRedirect: boolean };

export function selectPurchaseStoreClient(): SelectedStore {
  if (isLoopbackUrl(readExtraString('apiBaseUrl'))) {
    const fixtureStore = require('./purchaseStoreClient.fixture') as PurchaseStoreClient;
    return { client: fixtureStore, hasCheckoutRedirect: false };
  }
  return { client: platformStore, hasCheckoutRedirect: Platform.OS === 'web' };
}
```

```ts
// e2e/specs/proPurchase.spec.ts
// Buying Pro on the web through the fixture store, which the e2e build uses because its API base
// URL is a loopback URL: the purchase posts a synthetic RevenueCat event to the test-mode webhook,

  product_id: string;

async function readEntitlements(email: string): Promise<EntitlementRow[]> {

}
```

Replace the whole file with:

````markdown
# In-app purchase products

One Pro tier, sold two ways: a yearly auto-renewing subscription and a one-time lifetime purchase. There is no monthly product. Pro removes sponsored cards and raises "Ask about this card" from 5 to 20 answers a day. Every question bank is free; nothing else is sold. The ids below must match exactly in App Store Connect, Play Console, RevenueCat, and `constants/proProducts.ts` (both match `PRODUCT_ID_PATTERN` in `constants/appConfig.ts`).

| Product id                 | Plan in the app | Store type                                                                                            | US price | Reference name | Display name (localized)   | Description (localized)                                                   |
| -------------------------- | --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | -------------- | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `syntactical.pro.annual`   | A year          | Apple: auto-renewable subscription, 1 year, group "Pro". Play: subscription with one yearly base plan | $19.99   | Pro annual     | Syntactical Pro (1 year)   | No sponsored cards and 20 asks a day. Renews every year until you cancel. |
| `syntactical.pro.lifetime` | Forever         | Apple: non-consumable. Play: one-time in-app product                                                  | $39.99   | Pro lifetime   | Syntactical Pro (lifetime) | No sponsored cards and 20 asks a day, for good. One payment.              |

The owner sets the other regions' prices from each store's own equivalence. The app never shows a hard-coded price: the Pro sheet's buttons read "A year for {price}" and "Forever for {price}" from the store's localized strings, and "A year" and "Forever" when no price has loaded.

## Per-store setup

- **App Store Connect:** My Apps, Syntactical, Monetization, Subscriptions. Create a subscription group with the reference name `Pro` and the localized group name "Syntactical Pro". In it, create the auto-renewable subscription `syntactical.pro.annual`: reference name `Pro annual`, duration 1 year, price $19.99, the display name and description above, and one review screenshot of the Pro sheet. Then Monetization, In-App Purchases: create the Non-Consumable `syntactical.pro.lifetime`: reference name `Pro lifetime`, price $39.99, the display name and description above, and the same screenshot. Product ids cannot be reused after deletion, so check them before saving.
- **Play Console:** Monetize, Products, Subscriptions: create the subscription `syntactical.pro.annual` with one base plan, id `yearly`, auto-renewing, billing period 1 year, price 19.99 USD, and activate it. Monetize, Products, In-app products: create `syntactical.pro.lifetime`, price 39.99 USD, and activate it.
- **RevenueCat:** add the iOS and Android apps with their store credentials and import both products from each store. Create one offering, `default`, and make it the **current** offering, with two packages: `$rc_annual` holding `syntactical.pro.annual` (on Android the `yearly` base plan) and `$rc_lifetime` holding `syntactical.pro.lifetime`. The app lists prices and buys through the current offering's packages and finds a package by its store product identifier (`clients/purchaseStoreClient.ts`), with a Play subscription's base-plan suffix stripped first (RevenueCat reports the annual on Android as `syntactical.pro.annual:yearly`; `clients/normalizeProductId.ts`, the same rule the server applies to webhook product ids), so a product missing from the current offering shows no price and its purchase is unavailable. For the web, add a Web Billing app, create the same two products with identifiers equal to the ids above (the annual as a 1-year subscription, the lifetime as a one-time purchase), and put them in the same two packages. No RevenueCat entitlement is needed: the server decides Pro from the product ids in webhook events.
- **RevenueCat webhook:** point it at `https://api.syntactical.dev/v1/webhooks/revenuecat`, with the `Authorization` header set to the value of `REVENUECAT_WEBHOOK_AUTH` (see `docs/launch-placeholders.md`). Pro shows only once the webhook has recorded the purchase: the app refetches `/v1/me` after a purchase and shows Pro when `pro.isActive` is true. A cancelled annual keeps Pro until its expiry; only the expiry or a refund ends it.

## Review notes

Use this text in each product's App Review Information field:

```
Syntactical Pro removes the sponsored cards and raises "Ask about this card" from 5 to 20 answers a day. Every question bank is free without it. To reach the purchase: open the app, tap Settings in the header, sign in with an emailed one-time code if asked, then tap Go Pro. The sheet titled "Syntactical Pro" offers "A year for <price>", an auto-renewing yearly subscription, and "Forever for <price>", a one-time purchase, and says that the year renews until cancelled. After purchase, Settings shows "Pro until <date>" or "Pro, lifetime". For the yearly plan, Settings, Manage subscription opens the store's subscription page. Settings, Restore purchases restores Pro on a new install. The same sheet opens from "See Pro" when a free account reaches its 5 asks for the day.
```

Screenshot for review: the Pro sheet, "Syntactical Pro" with both buttons showing the sandbox prices.

## Check before submitting

- Both products are "Ready to Submit" (Apple) or "Active" (Play), and the subscription group has its localized name.
- The first subscription and in-app purchase must be submitted with an app version: attach both on the version's In-App Purchases and Subscriptions section.
- A sandbox purchase of each product on a preview or production build makes `/v1/me` report `pro.isActive: true` with the matching `product`, and Settings shows the plan (`docs/device-checklist.md`).
````

### Open questions (area 4)

1. **`POST /v1/test/webhook` contract.** Assumed: the body is a RevenueCat webhook body (`{ event }`), no `Authorization` header is needed, it runs the real `recordPurchaseEvent` path (so `store: 'APP_STORE'` may change an entitlement and `expiration_at_ms` sets `expires_at`), it sits behind the normal CORS and CSRF checks the web client already passes, and it answers 200 when recorded.
2. **State area 3 leaves the purchase suites in.** Assumed area 3 deleted `app/__tests__/difficultyPaywall*.test.tsx` and stopped importing `PaywallSheet`; `settingsRestore.test.tsx` rendered the difficulty route's locks, so Task 4.7 rewrites it rather than relying on area 3. Task 4.3 stops with a `DISPUTE` if `PaywallSheet` still has an importer.
3. **Results-screen footer.** Dropped from the spec: the results screen's sponsored card (Task 6.6) is the house Pro card whenever no ad fills it, so no separate footer is built.
4. **Ask copy.** The spec says "5 a day on the free tier. Pro has 20." with a Go Pro action; the brief says "That is the free tier's 5 for today. Pro has 20." with "See Pro". The plan keeps the brief's copy. The panel picks the copy from the limit the server names (5 is the free tier), not from a separate Pro status read, so it never disagrees with the server. The strings `AskPanel` uses (Task 4.10), in one place:
   - After an answer: "{remaining} of {limit} left today" (for example "4 of 5 left today", "19 of 20 left today").
   - Daily limit, server names 5 (the free tier): "That is the free tier's 5 for today. Pro has 20." with a "See Pro" button that opens the Pro sheet with `source: 'ask_limit'`.
   - Daily limit, server names any other number (Pro): "That is today's {limit}." (for example "That is today's 20."), with no See Pro.
   - Daily limit with no number (kept from today's panel): "You've used today's questions. They reset at midnight UTC."
   - Burst limit and no answer (both kept from today's panel): "Too many questions at once. Try again in a minute." and "No answer right now. Try again in a moment."
   - Device checklist (Task 4.16) quotes the free-limit line and "of 20 left today".
5. **`useEntitlements` removal timing.** The brief puts the replacement and every importer in the first task. Each importer's change is a behaviour change owned by another task (confirm in 4.5, ask gating in 4.10, the admin probe in 4.11), so the file is deleted in 4.12, once `grep` finds no importer. Between 4.1 and 4.12 the old hook is dead weight, not a second source of truth: with areas 2 and 3 landed, `/v1/me` has no `entitlements`, so nothing relies on it.
6. **Date format for "Pro until {date}".** Not specified. Assumed `Intl.DateTimeFormat(undefined, { dateStyle: 'long' })`, the device's locale and time zone; tests use a noon-UTC expiry so the day is stable across CI time zones.
7. **"No Web Billing key" on the web.** `ProSheet`'s props are fixed by the brief, so the sheet reads `revenueCatWebBillingKey` from `extra` itself (through `readExtraString`) to decide on the "Pro is available in the iOS and Android apps for now." line. In the e2e build the fixture store's prices make the buttons show, though there is no Web Billing key.
8. **A Pro sheet over the query drawer on native.** `AskPanel`'s See Pro mounts a `Modal` (through `DialogShell`) while the query drawer's `Modal` is open. React Native supports a modal presented over a modal on iOS and Android, but it is not covered by an existing test in the repo; Task 4.16 adds a device-check row for it.
9. **e2e Ask needs a model.** The e2e API runs without `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, so `POST /v1/ask` answers 503. Task 4.15 passes a fixed `modelProvider` through `startServer`'s existing test-only seam (refused outside `NODE_ENV=test`) in `e2e/support/runApi.mts`.

## Area 5: Cloudflare Pages and static output (`feat/cloudflare-static`)

Risk: standard. Depends on: areas 1 and 2 only; independent of areas 3 and 4. Branch: `feat/cloudflare-static`.

The workflow merges with the Cloudflare step gated on the secrets being present and the GitHub Pages steps still in place, so GitHub Pages keeps deploying until Task 5.11 (the cutover commit), which runs only after the owner has created the Pages project, the token, the account id, and the custom domain.

Facts from the code that shape every task below:

- `state/ContentProvider.tsx` (lines 80-102) renders `null` until its `useEffect` has read the cached manifest and banks from AsyncStorage. Every route renders inside it (`app/_layout.tsx`, lines 38-54), so at build time, and on the first client render, the static HTML body for every route is empty. Hydration cannot mismatch below `ContentProvider` today, and the static pages carry only the document shell from `app/+html.tsx`. Crawlable text (spec "Crawlable pages") is area 7, whose Task 7.1 changes that gate; this area does not.
- `AuthProvider` (`state/AuthProvider.tsx`, lines 111 and 159-179) and `StatsProvider` (`state/StatsProvider.tsx`, lines 125-160) each expose an `isHydrated` flag that is false until their AsyncStorage read finishes. Effects do not run in a server render, so both flags are false in it.
- Expo Router's static export names pages after the route file: `app/settings.tsx` becomes `dist/settings.html`, `app/[language]/index.tsx` becomes `dist/<language>/index.html`, `app/[language]/[difficulty]/play.tsx` becomes `dist/<language>/<difficulty>/play.html`, and `app/+not-found.tsx` becomes `dist/+not-found.html`. Task 5.6 Step 4 confirms this on the first real build before anything depends on it (see Open questions 1).
- The current build script is `... && cp -R content dist/content && node scripts/copySpaFallback.mjs dist && node scripts/writeRouteEntries.mjs dist && node scripts/assertNoPaidBanks.mjs dist` (`package.json` line 9). Area 1 may already have removed `assertNoPaidBanks`; the edit in Task 5.6 replaces only the two middle commands and leaves whatever follows them.

Order inside the area: 5.1 to 5.4 are safe under today's single-page output and can land in any order; 5.5 adds the host-files script without wiring it; 5.6 turns static output on and wires 5.5 in; 5.7 makes the e2e host match; 5.8 adds the gated deploy step; 5.9 is the end-of-area verification; 5.10 is docs; 5.11 is the cutover, run after the owner's steps, possibly days later, on its own branch `chore/cloudflare-cutover`.

```ts
// False during the server render of the static export and the first client render, true once mounted, so a
// component can render the same loading state the static HTML holds and fill in after hydration.
import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';

export function useIsHydrated(): boolean {
  const [isHydrated, setIsHydrated] = useState(false);
  useEffect(() => {
    setIsHydrated(true);
  }, []);
  return isHydrated;
}
```

```ts
// The concrete params of the dynamic routes for the static web export, from the bundled manifest: every track, and
// every track and difficulty pair it lists a bank for. The export runs this in Node at build time.
import { BUNDLED_MANIFEST } from './bundledManifest.generated';

export type LanguageParams = { language: string };

}
```

```tsx
// The document shell for every page of the static web export, rendered only in Node at build time: language, charset,
// viewport, the obsidian theme colour (also the body background, so there is no white flash before the styles load),
// the title, and the EthicalAds client script only when extra.ethicalAdsPublisher is configured.
import type { ReactNode } from 'react';

import { ScrollViewStyleReset } from 'expo-router/html';

import { readExtraString } from '../config/readExtraString';

// The obsidian token in tailwind.config.js; htmlShell.web.test.tsx fails if they drift apart.
const THEME_COLOR = '#05060a';
const BODY_BACKGROUND = `body { background-color: ${THEME_COLOR}; }`;
const ETHICAL_ADS_SCRIPT = 'https://media.ethicalads.io/media/client/ethicalads.min.js';

export default function Root({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  const ethicalAdsPublisher = readExtraString('ethicalAdsPublisher');
  return (
    <html lang="en">
      <head>
        <meta charSet="utf-8" />
        <meta httpEquiv="X-UA-Compatible" content="IE=edge" />
        <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1, shrink-to-fit=no" />
        <meta name="theme-color" content={THEME_COLOR} />
        <title>Syntactical</title>
        <ScrollViewStyleReset />
        <style dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: BODY_BACKGROUND }} />
        {ethicalAdsPublisher === null ? null : <script async src={ETHICAL_ADS_SCRIPT} />}
      </head>
      <body>{children}</body>
    </html>
  );
}
```

`scripts/writeHostFiles.mjs`:

```js
// Writes the files Cloudflare Pages reads beside the static web export: _headers and 404.html. The bank files under
// content/ are cached for a year: the app fetches them with cache: 'no-cache' (clients/fetchContentText.ts) and
// checks every download against the manifest hash, and Pages purges its edge cache on each deploy. The manifest and
// the sponsor file revalidate on every request. 404.html is the exported not-found page, which Pages serves with
// status 404 for any path the export does not hold.
import { promises, realpathSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';

const { access, copyFile, writeFile } = promises;

const NOT_FOUND_PAGE = '+not-found.html';

// Pages applies every rule that matches a path and joins repeated header values with a comma, so the rules must not
// overlap: a :placeholder matches one path segment, so /content/:track/:bank never matches /content/manifest.json.
export const HOST_HEADERS = [
  '/content/manifest.json',
  '  Cache-Control: no-cache',
  '',
  '/content/sponsor.json',
  '  Cache-Control: no-cache',
  '',
  '/content/:track/:bank',
  '  Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable',
  '',
].join('\n');

export async function writeHostFiles(outputDir) {
  const notFoundPage = join(outputDir, NOT_FOUND_PAGE);
  try {
    await access(notFoundPage);
  } catch {
    throw new Error(`${NOT_FOUND_PAGE} is missing from the web export; app.config.ts must set web.output to 'static'`);
  }
  await copyFile(notFoundPage, join(outputDir, '404.html'));
  await writeFile(join(outputDir, '_headers'), HOST_HEADERS);
}

// Compare as file URLs: a plain string compare breaks on a path with a space, and a symlink needs its real path.
if (process.argv[1] && import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(realpathSync(process.argv[1])).href) {
  writeHostFiles(process.argv[2] ?? 'dist').catch((err) => {
    console.error(err.message);
    process.exitCode = 1;
  });
}
```

`e2e/support/startWebHost.ts` (whole file):

```ts
// Serves the web export the way Cloudflare Pages does: a path is answered by the exported file at that path, then by
// <path>.html, then by <path>/index.html, and anything else by 404.html with status 404 (an empty 404 when the export
// has none). The public content is served under /content/ from its own directory. Paid banks are never in it. Pages
// also redirects /python to /python/ for a directory page; this host serves the page without the redirect.
import { createReadStream, existsSync, statSync } from 'node:fs';
import { createServer } from 'node:http';
import type { Server } from 'node:http';
import { extname, join, normalize, sep } from 'node:path';

import { BASE_PATH, LOOPBACK } from './e2eEnv';

const CONTENT_PATH = `${BASE_PATH}/content/`;
const NOT_FOUND = 404;
const NOT_FOUND_PAGE = '404.html';
const OK = 200;
const MIME_TYPES: Record<string, string> = {
  '.css': 'text/css',
  '.html': 'text/html; charset=utf-8',
  '.ico': 'image/x-icon',
  '.js': 'text/javascript',
  '.json': 'application/json',
  '.png': 'image/png',
  '.svg': 'image/svg+xml',
  '.ttf': 'font/ttf',
  '.woff2': 'font/woff2',
};

function findFile(root: string, relativePath: string): string | null {
  const file = normalize(join(root, relativePath));
  const isInside = file === root || file.startsWith(`${root}${sep}`);
  return isInside && existsSync(file) && statSync(file).isFile() ? file : null;
}

// The exported page for a path: the file itself, then <path>.html, then <path>/index.html.
function findPage(root: string, relativePath: string): string | null {
  const trimmed = relativePath.replace(/\/+$/, '');
  const asHtml = trimmed === '' ? null : findFile(root, `${trimmed}.html`);
  return findFile(root, relativePath) ?? asHtml ?? findFile(root, join(trimmed, 'index.html'));
}

function startWebHost(options: { contentDir: string; port: number; webDir: string }): Promise<Server> {
  const { contentDir, port, webDir } = options;
  const server = createServer((request, response) => {
    const { pathname } = new URL(request.url ?? '/', `http://${LOOPBACK}`);
    const path = decodeURIComponent(pathname);
    let file: string | null = null;
    if (path.startsWith(CONTENT_PATH)) {
      file = findFile(contentDir, path.slice(CONTENT_PATH.length));
    } else if (path.startsWith(`${BASE_PATH}/`)) {
      file = findPage(webDir, path.slice(BASE_PATH.length + 1));
    }
    const status = file === null ? NOT_FOUND : OK;
    const served = file ?? findFile(webDir, NOT_FOUND_PAGE);
    if (served === null) {
      response.writeHead(NOT_FOUND).end();
      return;
    }
    response.writeHead(status, { 'Content-Type': MIME_TYPES[extname(served)] ?? 'application/octet-stream' });
    createReadStream(served).pipe(response);
  });
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    server.once('error', reject);
    server.listen(port, LOOPBACK, () => resolve(server));
  });
}

export { startWebHost };
```

### Task 5.8: Cloudflare Pages deploy step, gated on its secrets

Exception to test-first: workflow config with no behaviour Jest can reach. Each step has a verification command.

**Files:**

- Modify: `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` (name, line 1; permissions, lines 8-11; the `build` job's steps after line 35)

**Interfaces:**

- Consumes: the Actions secrets `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` and `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` (absent until the owner adds them).
- Produces: on push to `main` and on manual dispatch, `wrangler pages deploy dist --project-name=syntactical --branch=main` runs only when both secrets are set; the GitHub Pages upload and deploy steps keep running unchanged.

The secret is checked in its own step whose output gates the deploy, instead of a job-level `env` read by `if: env.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN != ''`: a job-level `env` would hand the token to `npm ci` and `npm run build`, which run third-party code. This is the same shape as "Check the Railway token is set" in `.github/workflows/server-deploy.yml` (lines 52-56). Secrets cannot be read in `if:` directly.

```yaml
# Until the owner creates the Cloudflare Pages project and adds both secrets this step is skipped, and GitHub
# Pages (below) stays the live host. The cutover commit removes the GitHub Pages steps.
- name: Check the Cloudflare secrets are set
  id: cloudflare
  env:
    CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
    CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
  run: |
    if [ -n "$CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN" ] && [ -n "$CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID" ]; then
      echo 'configured=true' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    else
      echo 'configured=false' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      echo 'The Cloudflare secrets are not set; skipping the Cloudflare Pages deploy.'
    fi

- name: Deploy to Cloudflare Pages
  if: steps.cloudflare.outputs.configured == 'true'
  id: cloudflare-deploy
  uses: cloudflare/wrangler-action@<sha> # v4.x.y
  with:
    apiToken: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
    accountId: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
    command: pages deploy dist --project-name=syntactical --branch=main
    gitHubToken: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

- name: Print the Cloudflare deployment URL
  if: steps.cloudflare.outputs.configured == 'true'
  env:
    DEPLOYMENT_URL: ${{ steps.cloudflare-deploy.outputs.deployment-url }}
  run: echo "Cloudflare Pages deployment at $DEPLOYMENT_URL"
```

`.github/workflows/deploy.yml` (whole file; `<sha>` and `v4.x.y` as resolved in Task 5.8):

```yaml
name: Deploy to Cloudflare Pages

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  deployments: write

concurrency:
  group: cloudflare-pages
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4.4.0

      - name: Set up Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020 # v4.4.0
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Build the Expo web export and content
        run: npm run build

      - name: Check the Cloudflare secrets are set
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          [ -n "$CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN" ] && [ -n "$CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID" ] || { echo 'The CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN or CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID Actions secret is not set; nothing was deployed.' >&2; exit 1; }

      - name: Deploy to Cloudflare Pages
        id: deployment
        uses: cloudflare/wrangler-action@<sha> # v4.x.y
        with:
          apiToken: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          accountId: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
          command: pages deploy dist --project-name=syntactical --branch=main
          gitHubToken: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: Print the deployment URL
        env:
          DEPLOYMENT_URL: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.deployment-url }}
        run: echo "Cloudflare Pages deployment at $DEPLOYMENT_URL"
```

Verify: `grep -nE 'pages: write|id-token|github-pages|upload-pages-artifact|deploy-pages|group: pages$' .github/workflows/deploy.yml`

Verify: `grep -nE 'group: cloudflare-pages|deployments: write|wrangler-action@[0-9a-f]{40}' .github/workflows/deploy.yml`

### Open questions (area 5)

1. **Static export file names.** I could not run the export (no `node_modules` here). Assumption: Expo Router writes `settings.html`, `<language>/index.html`, `<language>/<difficulty>/play.html`, and `+not-found.html`. Task 5.6 Step 4 checks this before anything depends on it, and says what to change if the names differ. It may also write pages for the unexpanded `[language]` segments. Task 5.9 records them, and they do no harm.
2. **`_headers` pattern.** The brief gives `/content/*/*.json`. I wrote `/content/:track/:bank` instead. My understanding is that Pages allows one splat per rule and joins the values when two rules match the same path. A `/content/*` rule would therefore turn the manifest's header into `public, max-age=31536000, immutable, no-cache`. A placeholder matches exactly one segment, so the rules cannot overlap. Task 5.9 Step 2 checks the headers Pages actually serves.
3. **Year-long cache on bank paths that carry no hash.** `content/python/easy.json` keeps the same URL when its content changes. The cache is safe only because of three things: the app fetches with `cache: 'no-cache'` (`clients/fetchContentText.ts` line 31), RN's fetch polyfill adds a cache-busting query for `no-cache`, and every download is checked against the manifest hash. Any other client would get stale bytes. If the owner wants a margin, `max-age=300` would be safer.
4. **Trailing-slash redirect.** I believe Pages redirects `/python` to `/python/` for a directory page. The e2e host serves the page with no redirect. Task 5.9 checks that the router renders both forms.
5. **Static pages have empty bodies.** `ContentProvider` renders `null` until AsyncStorage has been read, so every page is just the shell. I assumed that is acceptable until area 7, whose Task 7.1 changes it.
6. **`.nojekyll` removed while GitHub Pages still serves the site.** This assumes the Pages source is "GitHub Actions", which runs no Jekyll. Task 5.8 Step 4 checks that an `/_expo/` file still loads.
7. **`extra` during the build-time render.** This assumes `Constants.expoConfig.extra` is available when `+html.tsx` renders. If it is not, `readExtraString` returns null and the shell simply leaves the ad script out.
8. **Secret gate.** The deploy runs only if a check step reports both secrets, instead of using `if: env.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN != ''` at job level. That keeps the token away from `npm ci` and the build.
9. **`<sha>` for wrangler-action.** It is resolved when Task 5.8 Step 1 runs.

Area 6 code and test stand-ins type the value as `ProStatusState`.
- `components/purchase/ProSheet.tsx` (area 4, Task 4.3): `export function ProSheet(props: { isBuying: boolean; message: string | null; onBuy: (productId: string) => void; onClose: () => void; prices: Readonly<Record<string, string>>; source: ProSheetSource })` with `export type ProSheetSource = 'ask_limit' | 'house_card' | 'results' | 'settings'`. `'house_card'` is already in area 4's union, so area 6 adds nothing to it. The sheet records `paywall_viewed { source }` once per opening.
- `components/purchase/ProOffer.tsx` (area 4, Task 4.7): `export function ProOffer({ onClose, source }: { onClose: () => void; source: ProSheetSource })`, the sheet wired to `usePurchases({ shouldLoadPrices: true })`. It renders nothing for a guest (and calls `onClose`); on `unlocked` it closes; on `redirect` it pushes `{ pathname: '/purchase-complete', params: { product } }` and closes; on `unavailable` it shows `'The purchase did not go through. Try again.'`; on `pending` it shows `'Your purchase is still processing. Check back shortly.'` and re-checks twice through `confirm`, 2000 ms apart, while mounted; on `cancelled` it shows nothing; it cannot be closed while a purchase runs. This is the house card's buy flow; area 6 does not reimplement it.
- `state/usePurchases.ts` (area 4, Task 4.5, shape unchanged): `usePurchases({ shouldLoadPrices }): PurchasesState` with `PurchasesState = { buy: (productId: string) => Promise<BuyOutcome>; confirm: (productId: string, options?: ConfirmOptions) => Promise<boolean>; prices: Readonly<Record<string, string>>; restore: () => Promise<boolean> }` and `BuyOutcome = 'cancelled' | 'pending' | 'redirect' | 'unavailable' | 'unlocked'` (today's union, `state/usePurchases.ts:19`). `prices` is empty for a guest. Area 6 only stubs it in tests (for `ProOffer`), and every stub returns all four members typed as `PurchasesState`.
- `app/+html.tsx` (area 5, Task 5.4): `export default function Root({ children }: { children: ReactNode })`. Its `<head>` renders `{ethicalAdsPublisher === null ? null : <script async src={ETHICAL_ADS_SCRIPT} />}` from `const ethicalAdsPublisher = readExtraString('ethicalAdsPublisher');`. Task 6.11 swaps that for `<EthicalAdsScript />`, quoting each line before and after.

Design decisions made once for the whole area:

- **Where the Pro gate lives.** `state/SponsorProvider.tsx` is created in Task 6.3 (not in the AdMob half) and mounted inside `AuthProvider` in Task 6.4. It reads `useProStatus()` and `useAuth().isHydrated` once for the whole app and publishes `eligibility: 'eligible' | 'hidden'`; outside the provider `useSponsor()` returns `hidden`. Reason: `useProStatus` calls `useQuery`, which throws outside a `QueryClientProvider`, and more than twenty existing suites render `ResultsScreen` (through `QuizRound`) or `LanguageStep` with no providers; a fail-closed context keeps them green and keeps a card from flashing before auth hydrates (Review Focus 6). Task 6.14 adds the consent state to the same provider.
- **Where the Pro sheet is hosted.** A small `components/sponsor/SponsorProSheetHost.tsx` rendered by the card itself. For a signed-in user it renders area 4's `ProOffer` with `source="house_card"`, the same buy flow as Settings and Ask; for a guest, whom `ProOffer` does not serve, it renders a bare `ProSheet` with `source="house_card"` whose Buy sends them to sign in. The house card is the only sheet opener in this area, and a local host keeps `ResultsScreen` and `LanguageStep` free of purchase state.
- **One content slot for every fallback.** `components/sponsor/SponsorContentSlot.tsx` (Task 6.4) renders house or direct content, reports `ad_shown` once, and opens the sheet or the sponsor link. The native card, the web card's no-fill path, and the AdMob error path all render it.
- **Platform split.** `SponsoredCard.tsx` (native) and `SponsoredCard.web.tsx` (web), and `clients/adsConsentClient.ts` with `clients/adsConsentClient.web.ts`, follow the existing `clients/purchaseStoreClient.ts` / `purchaseStoreClient.web.ts` pair. Jest: the native project (`jest.config.js:216-223`) lists `ios.*` and `native.*` extensions before plain `ts`/`tsx` and never `web.*`, so native suites get `SponsoredCard.tsx`; the web project uses the `jest-expo/web` preset (`jest.config.js:224-229`), which resolves `.web.tsx` first and runs only `**/__tests__/**/*.web.test.ts?(x)`. No `jest.config.js` change is needed.

```tsx
// The sponsored card's frame, in the SelectionCard idiom: a "Sponsored" label at least 15 points high as
// the first child (AdMob's attribution rule), an optional icon on the left, and the content beside it.
// The right padding keeps the top-right corner clear for the AdChoices icon the AdMob SDK draws there.
// SponsorContentCard fills the frame from a SponsorContent with a headline, one line of body, and one
// link-role button; the AdMob card wraps its own Text and Image views, styled with SPONSOR_CLASSES, in
// the SDK's asset views instead. No media view and no second body line, on any feed.
import type { ReactNode } from 'react';
import { Image, Pressable, Text, View } from 'react-native';

import { SPONSOR_LABEL_MIN_HEIGHT } from '../../constants/sponsor';
import type { SponsorContent } from '../../services/sponsor/types/SponsorContent';

const ACTION_BOX = 'mt-3 self-start rounded border border-line px-4 py-2';
const ACTION_LABEL = 'font-mono text-xs uppercase tracking-widest text-signal';

export const SPONSOR_CLASSES = {
  actionBox: ACTION_BOX,
  actionLabel: ACTION_LABEL,
  // The AdMob call to action is a single Text inside its asset view, so box and label share one element.
  actionText: `${ACTION_BOX} ${ACTION_LABEL}`,
  body: 'mt-1 text-sm text-muted',
  headline: 'font-mono text-lg text-ink',
  icon: 'mr-4 h-10 w-10 rounded',
} as const;

type SponsoredCardFrameProps = { children: ReactNode; headline: string; icon?: ReactNode };

export function SponsoredCardFrame({ children, headline, icon }: SponsoredCardFrameProps) {
  return (
    <View
      testID="sponsored-card"
      role="group"
      aria-label={`Sponsored: ${headline}`}
      className="w-full rounded-lg border border-line bg-surface py-4 pl-5 pr-10"
    >
      <Text
        className="font-mono text-xs uppercase tracking-widest text-muted"
        style={{ minHeight: SPONSOR_LABEL_MIN_HEIGHT }}
      >
        Sponsored
      </Text>
      <View className="mt-2 flex-row items-start">
        {icon ?? null}
        <View className="flex-1">{children}</View>
      </View>
    </View>
  );
}

type SponsorContentCardProps = { content: SponsorContent; onPress: () => void };

export function SponsorContentCard({ content, onPress }: SponsorContentCardProps) {
  const { body, callToAction, headline, iconUri } = content;
  const icon =
    iconUri === undefined ? undefined : (
      <Image testID="sponsored-card-icon" aria-hidden source={{ uri: iconUri }} className={SPONSOR_CLASSES.icon} />
    );
  return (
    <SponsoredCardFrame headline={headline} icon={icon}>
      <Text className={SPONSOR_CLASSES.headline}>{headline}</Text>
      <Text numberOfLines={1} className={SPONSOR_CLASSES.body}>
        {body}
      </Text>
      <Pressable
        role="link"
        aria-label={`Sponsored: ${headline}. ${callToAction}`}
        onPress={onPress}
        className={SPONSOR_CLASSES.actionBox}
      >
        <Text className={SPONSOR_CLASSES.actionLabel}>{callToAction}</Text>
      </Pressable>
    </SponsoredCardFrame>
  );
}
```
