`components/seo/TrackSummary.tsx`:

```tsx
// Crawlable text for one track page in the static web export: the track label and tagline, its
// topics, and each bank's question count. The route renders it only before hydration, so the HTML a
// crawler reads carries it and the interactive difficulty step stands alone after mount. It reads
// the bundled manifest and the build-time counts, never storage or the network.
import { DIFFICULTIES } from '@syntactical/content-schema';
import { Text, View } from 'react-native';

import { BANK_QUESTION_COUNTS } from '../../services/content/bankTitles.generated';
import { BUNDLED_MANIFEST } from '../../services/content/bundledManifest.generated';
import { findLanguageEntry } from '../../services/content/findLanguageEntry';

type TrackSummaryProps = { language: string };

function describeCount(count: number): string {
  return `${count} ${count === 1 ? 'question' : 'questions'}`;
}

function listBankSizes(language: string, bankIds: readonly string[]) {
  return DIFFICULTIES.filter(({ id }) => bankIds.includes(id)).flatMap(({ id, label }) => {
    const count = BANK_QUESTION_COUNTS[`${language}/${id}`];
    return count === undefined ? [] : [{ count, id, label }];
  });
}

export function TrackSummary({ language }: TrackSummaryProps) {
  const entry = findLanguageEntry(BUNDLED_MANIFEST.languages, language);
  if (!entry) return null;
  const banks = listBankSizes(language, Object.keys(entry.banks));
  return (
    <View className="mt-10 gap-3">
      <Text role="heading" aria-level={2} className="font-mono text-xs uppercase tracking-widest text-muted">
        About {entry.label}
      </Text>
      <Text className="text-sm text-ink">{entry.tagline}</Text>
      {entry.topics.length === 0 ? null : (
        <View role="list" aria-label="Topics" className="gap-1">
          {entry.topics.map(({ id, label }) => (
            <Text key={id} role="listitem" className="text-sm text-muted">
              {label}
            </Text>
          ))}
        </View>
      )}
      <View role="list" aria-label="Banks" className="gap-1">
        {banks.map(({ count, id, label }) => (
          <Text key={id} role="listitem" className="font-mono text-sm text-muted">
            {`${label}: ${describeCount(count)}`}
          </Text>
        ))}
      </View>
    </View>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// Crawlable text for one bank page in the static web export: "What this bank covers" and the bank's
// distinct query titles in bank order. Titles are written not to give answers away; no prompt,
// choice, answer, or explanation is rendered. The route renders it only before hydration. It reads
// the build-time index, so Medium and Hard titles are there without bundling those banks.
import { Text, View } from 'react-native';

import { BANK_TITLES } from '../../services/content/bankTitles.generated';

type BankTitlesProps = { difficulty: string; language: string };

// Own keys only, so a route segment such as "constructor" never reads the prototype.
function readTitles(key: string): readonly string[] {
  return Object.hasOwn(BANK_TITLES, key) ? BANK_TITLES[key] : [];
}

export function BankTitles({ difficulty, language }: BankTitlesProps) {
  const titles = readTitles(`${language}/${difficulty}`);
  if (titles.length === 0) return null;
  return (
    <View className="mt-10 gap-3">
      <Text role="heading" aria-level={2} className="font-mono text-xs uppercase tracking-widest text-muted">
        What this bank covers
      </Text>
      <View role="list" aria-label="Bank titles" className="gap-1">
        {titles.map((title) => (
          <Text key={title} role="listitem" className="text-sm text-muted">
            {title}
          </Text>
        ))}
      </View>
    </View>
  );
}
```

`scripts/writeHostFiles.mjs`: merge `readdir`, `readFile`, and `writeFile` into the file's existing `node:fs` (or `node:fs/promises`) import and `join` into its `node:path` import. Then add, above the `writeHostFiles` export:

```js
const SITE_ORIGIN = 'https://syntactical.dev';
// Pages with nothing for a search engine: the admin console and the purchase return page.
const UNLISTED_PAGES = ['admin', 'purchase-complete'];
const ROUTE_FILE = /\.(tsx|ts|jsx|js)$/;
const NON_ROUTE_NAMES = new Set(['_layout', '+not-found', '+html', '__tests__']);

function isDynamicSegment(name) {
  return name.startsWith('[');
}

// Static page paths from the app/ tree, slash-separated, '' for the home page. Dynamic segments
// come from the manifest instead.
async function listStaticPagePaths(dir, prefix = '') {
  const paths = [];
  for (const entry of await readdir(dir, { withFileTypes: true })) {
    const base = entry.name.replace(ROUTE_FILE, '');
    if (NON_ROUTE_NAMES.has(base) || isDynamicSegment(base)) continue;
    if (entry.isDirectory()) {
      paths.push(...(await listStaticPagePaths(join(dir, entry.name), `${prefix}${entry.name}/`)));
    } else if (ROUTE_FILE.test(entry.name)) {
      paths.push(base === 'index' ? prefix.replace(/\/$/, '') : `${prefix}${base}`);
    }
  }
  return paths;
}

// One page per track and one per bank; the length and play steps take query parameters and are not listed.
function listTrackPagePaths(manifest) {
  return manifest.languages.flatMap((language) => [
    language.id,
    ...Object.keys(language.banks)
      .sort()
      .map((difficulty) => `${language.id}/${difficulty}`),
  ]);
}

function toLoc(path) {
  return path === '' ? `${SITE_ORIGIN}/` : `${SITE_ORIGIN}/${path}`;
}

export async function buildSitemap({ appDir = 'app', manifestPath = 'content/manifest.json' } = {}) {
  const manifest = JSON.parse(await readFile(manifestPath, 'utf8'));
  const staticPaths = (await listStaticPagePaths(appDir)).filter((path) => !UNLISTED_PAGES.includes(path)).sort();
  const urls = [...staticPaths, ...listTrackPagePaths(manifest)].map(
    (path) => `  <url><loc>${toLoc(path)}</loc></url>`,
  );
  return `<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<urlset xmlns="http://www.sitemaps.org/schemas/sitemap/0.9">
${urls.join('\n')}
</urlset>
`;
}

export function buildRobots() {
  const disallowed = UNLISTED_PAGES.map((page) => `Disallow: /${page}`);
  return ['User-agent: *', ...disallowed, `Sitemap: ${SITE_ORIGIN}/sitemap.xml`, ''].join('\n');
}

export async function writeSitemapFiles(outputDir, options = {}) {
  await writeFile(join(outputDir, 'sitemap.xml'), await buildSitemap(options));
  await writeFile(join(outputDir, 'robots.txt'), buildRobots());
}
```

```md
## Shared facts

- Twelve tracks: Python, Postgres, JavaScript, TypeScript, TypeScript Types, Node.js, Go, Ruby, Rails, SQL, Backend Security, and Frontend Security.

- Syntactical Pro is the only purchase, sold as Pro Annual (`syntactical.pro.annual`, a yearly auto-renewing subscription, $19.99 US) or Pro Lifetime (`syntactical.pro.lifetime`, one-time, $39.99 US). No monthly plan. Pro removes the sponsored cards and raises the daily Ask limit from 5 to 20. Cancelling Pro Annual keeps Pro until the end of the paid year.
- Free users see sponsored cards in the app's own card style, labelled "Sponsored": one on the results screen (from the second completed round, then every third round) and one in the track list. Never on a question, mid-round, in the query drawer, or in review rounds. On iOS and Android they are non-personalised Google AdMob native ads; on the web, an EthicalAds text ad, a direct sponsor, or the house Pro card. No ATT prompt, no tracking.
- Signing in is optional (an email code, or a password if you set one). Guests keep progress on the device; signed-in users sync progress across devices and can restore Pro.
```

The description block (lines 32-48, the fenced text under `### Description`) becomes:

```
Syntactical is a quiz for the parts of a language that behave differently than you expect. Every question bank is free.

Pick a track, then a difficulty. Twelve tracks: Python, Postgres, JavaScript, TypeScript, TypeScript Types, Node.js, Go, Ruby, Rails, SQL, Backend Security, and Frontend Security. Each round is a shuffled pass through a bank of multiple-choice, true/false, and A/B questions about runtime semantics, query planning, coercion, scope, injection, and the sharp edges in between.

Get one wrong and tap Explain. The Query panel shows the syntax, the reasoning, and the tags behind the question, so you learn why the answer is what it is.

What you get
- 12 tracks, each at Easy, Medium, and Hard: 36 question banks, every one free, no account needed.
- A streak, XP, and a daily goal of 10, 20, or 50 XP.
- Review rounds that bring back the questions you missed, on a schedule that spaces them out. They are built on your device, so they work offline.
- Easy banks are on your device from the first launch. Medium and Hard download once and then work offline.
- Signed in, ask about a card after you answer it: 5 a day free, 20 a day with Pro.
- Optional sign-in with an email code, or a password if you set one. Sign in to keep your progress across devices and to restore Pro. Delete your account at any time from Settings.

Syntactical Pro
- Removes the sponsored cards and raises the daily Ask limit from 5 to 20.
- Pro Annual is a subscription that renews every year until you cancel it. Pro Lifetime is a one-time purchase. There is no monthly plan.
- Manage or cancel Pro Annual in your App Store or Google Play account settings. Cancelling keeps Pro until the end of the paid year.

Sponsored cards
Free users see a sponsored card on the results screen every few rounds and one in the track list, in the app's own style and labelled Sponsored. Never on a question, never during a round, never in review rounds. The ads are non-personalised: the app does not track you and shows no tracking prompt.

Your answers and progress stay on your device until you sign in. Usage analytics are anonymous until you sign in, and are never tied to your email.

Privacy policy: https://syntactical.dev/privacy
Terms of use: https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/itunes/dev/stdeula/
```

```
Syntactical is a programming quiz app with 12 tracks (for example Python, Postgres, and Backend Security), each at Easy, Medium, and Hard. Every question bank is free and needs no account.

Syntactical Pro is the only in-app purchase, in two products: syntactical.pro.annual (auto-renewing subscription, one year, in the subscription group "Pro") and syntactical.pro.lifetime (non-consumable). Pro removes the sponsored cards and raises the daily limit of "Ask about this card" from 5 to 20. There is no monthly product.

How to reach Pro:
1. Open the app. The track list shows a card labelled Sponsored between the track groups. When no ad is available it is the house card, "Syntactical Pro", with a See Pro button.
2. Tap See Pro. Or open Settings (reachable from the header on every screen) and tap Go Pro.
3. If you are not signed in, the app sends you to Sign in first. Enter your email, receive a one-time code by email, and enter it. Any email address you control works, and an account is created the first time you sign in.
4. The Syntactical Pro sheet shows two buttons with the store prices, "A year for <price>" and "Forever for <price>", and Not now. Buy either one with your sandbox account.
5. The sponsored cards disappear. Settings shows "Pro until <date>" for the annual product or "Pro, lifetime". Settings, Manage subscription opens the store's subscription page. Settings, Restore purchases restores Pro on a new install.

Sponsored cards: a free user sees one card on the results screen after a round (first after the second completed round, then every third round) and one in the track list. They never appear on a question, during a round, in the query drawer, or in review rounds. On iOS and Android the card is a Google AdMob native ad drawn in the app's own card style, with the "Sponsored" label at the top and the AdChoices icon in the top-right corner. When no ad loads, the card is the house Pro card. Development builds show Google test ads labelled "Test Ad"; the build under review requests real ads.

Ads are non-personalised only. The app does not use the advertising identifier for tracking and does not show the App Tracking Transparency prompt. In the EEA and the UK, Google's consent form (User Messaging Platform) appears on first launch, before any ad request; Settings, Privacy settings reopens it.

Account deletion: Settings, then Account, then Delete account. The app asks you to type DELETE to confirm. Deleting removes the account, synced answers, and progress. Records that remain at vendors are limited to analytics events tied to the account's random user id (never the email), the RevenueCat customer record, the email provider's send log, Google AdMob's own ad request records, and the stores' own transactions.

Data collection: email (sign-in), whether the account has Pro and until when, anonymous product analytics through PostHog (no location), and advertising data through Google AdMob (non-personalised, not linked to the user, not used for tracking). The privacy policy is at https://syntactical.dev/privacy.

Purchases are processed by Apple and Google through RevenueCat. The app never handles card details.
```

## Area 9: model failover and model updates (`feat/model-failover`)

Risk: standard. Depends on: area 3 merged (area 3 edits `server/src/routes/ask.ts` and `startServer.ts`; this area edits the provider wiring beside them). Server only. Merged on green after the `pr-reviewer` pass.

**What this area does.** `POST /v1/ask` and `GET /v1/study-note` make one model call each through the `ModelProvider` interface (`server/src/clients/modelProvider.ts`), today Claude Haiku 5.5 only, with the id hard-coded in `server/src/constants/model.ts`. After this area:

- A second provider, OpenAI through the Responses API, answers when the primary fails for a transient reason (timeout, connection, 429, 5xx) or a configuration reason (400, 401, 403, 404).
- A refusal or a truncated answer is an answer, not an outage: it resolves `null` and is never sent to the other vendor. Routing a declined learner message to a second vendor would route around the first vendor's refusal.
- A per-process circuit breaker skips a failing primary: three transient failures in a row open it for 60 seconds; one configuration failure opens it for 15 minutes and logs an error naming the provider, the model id, and the status, so a retired model or a rejected parameter is visible at once and costs one slow request, not every request.
- Model ids come from the environment with today's id as the default, so a model change is a Railway variable change, not a code change.
- A model-availability check runs after boot and every 24 hours through each vendor's Models API; an unavailable configured model logs an error and opens that provider's breaker for 15 minutes. It never blocks boot or readiness.
- A smoke script runs the real Ask and study-note prompts through each configured provider, for use before changing a model id, with a manual workflow that runs it in CI when the keys are present.

**Time budget.** The app waits 30 seconds on these routes and the code comment in `constants/model.ts` targets about 25. Each attempt now gets 11 seconds. With one provider the SDK keeps one retry (two attempts, 22 seconds worst case, as today's 12-second budget with one retry gave 24); with two providers the SDK retries are turned off and the failover is the retry (11 plus 11).

**Global constraints for this area.**

- Provider ids: `'anthropic' | 'openai'`. `MODEL_PRIMARY` defaults to `anthropic`.
- `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` defaults to `claude-haiku-5-5` and must match `^claude-[a-z0-9-]+$`. `OPENAI_MODEL` is required when `OPENAI_API_KEY` is set and has no default; the owner chooses a small, fast model. `OPENAI_REASONING_EFFORT` is optional (`low | medium | high`) and the `reasoning` field is omitted when it is unset, so a non-reasoning model is never sent a parameter it rejects.
- Breaker: `FAILURES_TO_OPEN = 3`, `TRANSIENT_COOLDOWN_MS = 60_000`, `CONFIG_COOLDOWN_MS = 900_000`, `ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT_MS = 11_000`, `AVAILABILITY_CHECK_INTERVAL_MS = 86_400_000`, `AVAILABILITY_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS = 5_000`.
- Logging: provider, model id, outcome (`answered | declined | transient | config`), latency in milliseconds, and whether the answer came from the secondary. Never the prompt, the learner's message, the answer text, or an SDK error object (the existing routes already avoid logging the error object for this reason).
- No change to the routes' responses: both still answer 503 `ASK_UNAVAILABLE` or `STUDY_NOTE_UNAVAILABLE` when no provider answers, and Ask still releases the reserved usage.

Commands for this area: unit tests `cd server && npx vitest run <path>`; integration tests `cd server && npx vitest run --config vitest.integration.config.ts <path>` (needs `TEST_DATABASE_URL` or local Docker); GREEN gate `cd server && npm test && npm run test:integration && npm run typecheck`, then `npm run lint` at the root.

`server/src/clients/ModelProviderError.ts`:

```ts
// A failed model request, classified for the failover. `config` means the request cannot succeed
// until the configuration changes (a retired model, a rejected parameter, a bad key); `transient`
// means it may succeed on retry. Built from the provider, model, and status only: the SDK error
// is dropped because its request carries the learner's message.
type ProviderId = 'anthropic' | 'openai';
type ModelFailureKind = 'config' | 'transient';

const CONFIG_STATUSES = new Set([400, 401, 403, 404]);

class ModelProviderError extends Error {
  readonly kind: ModelFailureKind;
  readonly model: string;
  readonly provider: ProviderId;
  readonly status: number | null;

  constructor(provider: ProviderId, model: string, status: number | null) {
    const kind: ModelFailureKind = status !== null && CONFIG_STATUSES.has(status) ? 'config' : 'transient';
    super(`${provider} ${model} failed (${kind}${status === null ? '' : `, ${status}`})`);
    this.name = 'ModelProviderError';
    this.kind = kind;
    this.model = model;
    this.provider = provider;
    this.status = status;
  }
}

export { ModelProviderError };
export type { ModelFailureKind, ProviderId };
```

In `modelProvider.ts`: the deps gain `model: string` and `maxRetries: number`; `ModelProvider` gains `readonly id: ProviderId; readonly model: string`; wrap `client.create(...)` in `try`/`catch` and rethrow `new ModelProviderError('anthropic', model, error instanceof Anthropic.APIError ? (error.status ?? null) : null)`. Replace `MODEL.ID` with the `model` argument. In `buildAnthropicOptions.ts`, take `maxRetries` from the caller and use `MODEL.ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT_MS`; update its test for the new argument.
```ts
// The OpenAI fallback behind POST /v1/ask and GET /v1/study-note, behind the same interface as the
// Claude provider. One Responses API request per answer. Resolves the answer text, or null on a
// refusal, an incomplete response, or an empty answer, so a partial answer is never shown. Rejects
// with a ModelProviderError; the SDK error is dropped because its request carries the learner's
// message. The key comes from the caller; this module never reads the environment.
import OpenAI from 'openai';

import { MODEL } from '../constants/model.js';

import { ModelProviderError } from './ModelProviderError.js';
import type { ModelProvider } from './modelProvider.js';

type ResponsesClient = Pick<OpenAI['responses'], 'create'>;

interface OpenAIProviderDeps {
  apiKey: string;
  maxRetries: number;
  model: string;
  reasoningEffort?: 'low' | 'medium' | 'high';
  // Test seam: replaces the SDK's responses resource.
  responses?: ResponsesClient;
}

function readAnswer(response: OpenAI.Responses.Response): string | null {
  if (response.status !== 'completed') return null;
  const parts: string[] = [];
  for (const item of response.output) {
    if (item.type !== 'message') continue;
    for (const content of item.content) {
      if (content.type === 'refusal') return null;
      if (content.type === 'output_text') parts.push(content.text);
    }
  }
  const text = parts.join('').trim();
  return text === '' ? null : text;
}

function createOpenAIModelProvider({ apiKey, maxRetries, model, reasoningEffort, responses }: OpenAIProviderDeps) {
  const client = responses ?? new OpenAI({ apiKey, maxRetries, timeout: MODEL.ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT_MS }).responses;
  const provider: ModelProvider = {
    id: 'openai',
    model,
    async answer({ system, user }) {
      let response: OpenAI.Responses.Response;
      try {
        response = await client.create({
          input: user,
          instructions: system,
          max_output_tokens: MODEL.MAX_TOKENS,
          model,
          ...(reasoningEffort ? { reasoning: { effort: reasoningEffort } } : {}),
        });
      } catch (error) {
        throw new ModelProviderError('openai', model, error instanceof OpenAI.APIError ? (error.status ?? null) : null);
      }
      return readAnswer(response);
    },
  };
  return provider;
}

export { createOpenAIModelProvider };
export type { ResponsesClient };
```

### Task 9.4: failover provider with a circuit breaker

**Files:**

- Create: `server/src/clients/failoverModelProvider.ts`
- Test: `server/src/__tests__/clients/failoverModelProvider.test.ts` (new)

**Interfaces:**

- Produces: `createFailoverModelProvider({ providers: ModelProvider[], logger: Logger, now?: () => number }): ModelProvider & { openBreaker(id: ProviderId, kind: ModelFailureKind): void }`. `providers[0]` is the primary. `id` and `model` of the returned provider are the primary's.
- Behaviour: try each provider in order, skipping one whose breaker is open (unless every breaker is open, in which case try the primary anyway so an outage of both still gets one attempt). A resolved value, `null` included, ends the call: a decline is never retried elsewhere. A rejection records a failure for that provider and moves to the next; when the last one rejects, rethrow the last `ModelProviderError`. A success resets the provider's failure count and closes its breaker. Three consecutive transient failures open the breaker for `TRANSIENT_COOLDOWN_MS`; one config failure opens it for `CONFIG_COOLDOWN_MS` and logs `error` once per opening. A non-`ModelProviderError` rejection counts as transient.
- Logs one `info` line per call: `{ provider, model, outcome, latencyMs, isFailover }`, message `model call`. Never the prompt or the answer.

```ts
// server/src/__tests__/clients/failoverModelProvider.test.ts
// The failover in front of the model providers: the primary answers when it can; a failure moves the
// call to the next provider; a decline is final; a failing primary is skipped for a cooldown; a
// configuration failure (a retired model, a rejected parameter) opens a long cooldown and logs an
// error. The log never carries the prompt or the answer.
import { describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';

import { createFailoverModelProvider } from '../../clients/failoverModelProvider.js';
import { ModelProviderError } from '../../clients/ModelProviderError.js';
import type { ModelProvider } from '../../clients/modelProvider.js';
import type { ProviderId } from '../../clients/ModelProviderError.js';
import { MODEL } from '../../constants/model.js';

import { createRecordingLogger } from '../support/recordingLogger.js';

const PROMPT = { system: 'You are the tutor.', user: '<learner_message>"secret question"</learner_message>' };

function provider(
  id: ProviderId,
  outcomes: Array<string | null | 'transient' | 'config'>,
): ModelProvider & { calls: number } {
  const queue = [...outcomes];
  const fake = {
    calls: 0,
    id,
    model: `${id}-model`,
    answer: vi.fn(() => {
      fake.calls += 1;
      const next = queue.length > 1 ? queue.shift() : queue[0];
      if (next === 'transient') return Promise.reject(new ModelProviderError(id, `${id}-model`, 503));
      if (next === 'config') return Promise.reject(new ModelProviderError(id, `${id}-model`, 404));
      return Promise.resolve(next ?? null);
    }),
  };
  return fake;
}

describe('createFailoverModelProvider', () => {
  it('answers from the primary and never calls the secondary', async () => {
    const primary = provider('anthropic', ['From Claude.']);
    const secondary = provider('openai', ['From OpenAI.']);
    const { logger } = createRecordingLogger();

    await expect(createFailoverModelProvider({ logger, providers: [primary, secondary] }).answer(PROMPT)).resolves.toBe(
      'From Claude.',
    );

  });

    const primary = provider('anthropic', ['transient']);
    const secondary = provider('openai', ['From OpenAI.']);

    await expect(createFailoverModelProvider({ logger, providers: [primary, secondary] }).answer(PROMPT)).resolves.toBe(
```

`server/src/clients/failoverModelProvider.ts`:

```ts
// The model providers in order, behind one ModelProvider. The first provider whose breaker is
// closed answers; a failure moves the call to the next; a decline (null) is final, because a
// refusal is an answer and is never routed to another vendor. A provider that fails three times in
// a row is skipped for a minute; one configuration failure (a retired model, a rejected parameter,
// a bad key) skips it for 15 minutes and logs an error once. When every breaker is open the
// primary is tried anyway. State is per process, as the rate limiter's is.
import type { Logger } from 'pino';

import { MODEL } from '../constants/model.js';

import { ModelProviderError } from './ModelProviderError.js';
import type { ModelFailureKind, ProviderId } from './ModelProviderError.js';
import type { ModelPrompt, ModelProvider } from './modelProvider.js';

const { CONFIG_COOLDOWN_MS, FAILURES_TO_OPEN, TRANSIENT_COOLDOWN_MS } = MODEL.BREAKER;

interface BreakerState {
  failures: number;
  openUntil: number;
}

interface FailoverDeps {
  logger: Logger;
  now?: () => number;
  providers: ModelProvider[];
}

function toFailure(provider: ModelProvider, error: unknown): ModelProviderError {
  return error instanceof ModelProviderError ? error : new ModelProviderError(provider.id, provider.model, null);
}

function createFailoverModelProvider({ logger, now = Date.now, providers }: FailoverDeps) {
  const [primary] = providers;
  if (primary === undefined) throw new Error('createFailoverModelProvider needs at least one provider');
  const breakers = new Map<ProviderId, BreakerState>(providers.map(({ id }) => [id, { failures: 0, openUntil: 0 }]));

  function isOpen(id: ProviderId): boolean {
    return (breakers.get(id)?.openUntil ?? 0) > now();
  }

  function openBreaker(id: ProviderId, kind: ModelFailureKind): void {
    const state = breakers.get(id);
    if (state === undefined) return;
    state.openUntil = now() + (kind === 'config' ? CONFIG_COOLDOWN_MS : TRANSIENT_COOLDOWN_MS);
    state.failures = 0;
  }

  function recordFailure(failure: ModelProviderError): void {
    const state = breakers.get(failure.provider);
    if (state === undefined) return;
    if (failure.kind === 'config') {
      const wasOpen = isOpen(failure.provider);
      openBreaker(failure.provider, 'config');
      if (!wasOpen) {
        const { model, provider, status } = failure;
        logger.error({ model, provider, status }, 'model configuration failure; provider skipped for 15 minutes');
      }
      return;
    }
    state.failures += 1;
    if (state.failures >= FAILURES_TO_OPEN) openBreaker(failure.provider, 'transient');
  }

  function recordSuccess(id: ProviderId): void {
    const state = breakers.get(id);
    if (state !== undefined) Object.assign(state, { failures: 0, openUntil: 0 });
  }

  async function answer(prompt: ModelPrompt): Promise<string | null> {
    const ready = providers.filter(({ id }) => !isOpen(id));
    const order = ready.length > 0 ? ready : [primary];
    let lastFailure: ModelProviderError | undefined;
    for (const candidate of order) {
      const started = now();
      const base = { isFailover: candidate.id !== primary.id, model: candidate.model, provider: candidate.id };
      try {
        const result = await candidate.answer(prompt);
        recordSuccess(candidate.id);
        logger.info(
          { ...base, latencyMs: now() - started, outcome: result === null ? 'declined' : 'answered' },
          'model call',
        );
        return result;
      } catch (error) {
        lastFailure = toFailure(candidate, error);
        recordFailure(lastFailure);
        logger.info({ ...base, latencyMs: now() - started, outcome: lastFailure.kind }, 'model call');
      }
    }
    throw lastFailure;
  }

  return { answer, id: primary.id, model: primary.model, openBreaker };
}

export { createFailoverModelProvider };
```

```ts
    const { agent, questionId, readUsage } = await signedInAskSetup({ modelProvider });

    const response = await agent.post('/v1/ask').send({ choiceIndex: 0, message: 'Why?', questionId });

    expect(response.status).toBe(503);
    expect(response.body.error.code).toBe('ASK_UNAVAILABLE');
    expect(await readUsage()).toBe(0);
  });
});
```

`signedInAskSetup`, `silentLogger`, and `readUsage` stand for whatever the suite already uses to sign a user in, pick a question, silence the logger, and read `ask_usage`; the RED author names the real helpers (or adds a small local helper in this file if the suite inlines that setup). Add the matching two cases to the study-note suite: a fallback answer stores and returns the note; both down answers 503 `STUDY_NOTE_UNAVAILABLE` and stores nothing.

### Task 9.7: model availability check at boot and daily

**Files:**

- Create: `server/src/clients/checkModelAvailability.ts`
- Modify: `server/src/startServer.ts` (start the check after the server listens; clear the interval on close)
- Test: `server/src/__tests__/clients/checkModelAvailability.test.ts` (new)

**Interfaces:**

- Produces: `checkModelAvailability({ checks: AvailabilityCheck[], failover: FailoverModelProvider, logger }): Promise<void>` where `AvailabilityCheck = { id: ProviderId; model: string; retrieve: (model: string, options: { timeout: number }) => Promise<unknown> }`. For each check, call `retrieve(model, { timeout: MODEL.AVAILABILITY.CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS })`. A rejection whose status is 404 (or 400, 401, 403) logs `error` `{ provider, model, status }` with the message `configured model is unavailable` and calls `failover.openBreaker(id, 'config')`. A transient rejection logs `warn` and opens nothing. A success logs nothing. The function never rejects.
- `startModelAvailabilityChecks(deps): { stop(): void }` runs it once and then every `MODEL.AVAILABILITY.INTERVAL_MS` with an `unref`'d timer.
- `startServer` builds the checks from the same environment as Task 9.5: Anthropic uses `new Anthropic(buildAnthropicOptions(...)).models.retrieve`, OpenAI uses `new OpenAI({ apiKey }).models.retrieve`. Both SDKs expose `models.retrieve(id)` (the Anthropic Models API is documented in the Claude API reference, `client.models.retrieve(id)`; OpenAI's is `client.models.retrieve(model)`).

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**

```ts
// server/src/__tests__/clients/checkModelAvailability.test.ts
// The check that a configured model still exists: an unavailable model is logged as an error and
// its provider is skipped before a learner's request finds out; a vendor outage is only a warning;
// the check never throws and never blocks boot.
import { describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';

import { checkModelAvailability, startModelAvailabilityChecks } from '../../clients/checkModelAvailability.js';
import { MODEL } from '../../constants/model.js';

import { createRecordingLogger } from '../support/recordingLogger.js';

function failover() {
  return { answer: vi.fn(), id: 'anthropic' as const, model: 'claude-haiku-5-5', openBreaker: vi.fn() };
}

function statusError(status: number) {
  return Object.assign(new Error('x'), { status });
}

describe('checkModelAvailability', () => {
  it('logs nothing and opens nothing when every model exists', async () => {
    const target = failover();
    const { entries, logger } = createRecordingLogger();
    const retrieve = vi.fn().mockResolvedValue({ id: 'claude-haiku-5-5' });

    await checkModelAvailability({
      checks: [{ id: 'anthropic', model: 'claude-haiku-5-5', retrieve }],
      failover: target,
      logger,
    });

    expect(retrieve).toHaveBeenCalledWith('claude-haiku-5-5', { timeout: MODEL.AVAILABILITY.CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS });
    expect(target.openBreaker).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(entries.filter((entry) => entry.level === 'error' || entry.level === 'warn')).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  it('logs an error and opens the config breaker for a model that is gone', async () => {
    const target = failover();
    const { entries, logger } = createRecordingLogger();
    const retrieve = vi.fn().mockRejectedValue(statusError(404));

    await checkModelAvailability({
      checks: [{ id: 'anthropic', model: 'claude-retired', retrieve }],
      failover: target,
      logger,
    });

    expect(target.openBreaker).toHaveBeenCalledWith('anthropic', 'config');
    expect(entries.find((entry) => entry.level === 'error')).toMatchObject({
      model: 'claude-retired',
      msg: 'configured model is unavailable',
      provider: 'anthropic',
      status: 404,
    });
  });

  it('only warns on a vendor outage and never rejects', async () => {
    const target = failover();
    const { entries, logger } = createRecordingLogger();
    const retrieve = vi.fn().mockRejectedValue(new Error('socket hang up'));

    await expect(
      checkModelAvailability({ checks: [{ id: 'openai', model: 'small-model', retrieve }], failover: target, logger }),
    ).resolves.toBeUndefined();
    expect(target.openBreaker).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(entries.some((entry) => entry.level === 'warn')).toBe(true);
  });
});

describe('startModelAvailabilityChecks', () => {
  it('checks once now and again each interval, and stops', async () => {
    vi.useFakeTimers();
    const retrieve = vi.fn().mockResolvedValue({});
    const { logger } = createRecordingLogger();
    const running = startModelAvailabilityChecks({
      checks: [{ id: 'anthropic', model: 'claude-haiku-5-5', retrieve }],
      failover: failover(),
      logger,
    });

    await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(0);
    expect(retrieve).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(MODEL.AVAILABILITY.INTERVAL_MS);
    expect(retrieve).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);

    running.stop();
    await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(MODEL.AVAILABILITY.INTERVAL_MS);
    expect(retrieve).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
    vi.useRealTimers();
  });
});
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Run it and confirm the expected failure**

Run: `cd server && npx vitest run src/__tests__/clients/checkModelAvailability.test.ts`
Expected: FAIL at import with `Error: Cannot find module '../../clients/checkModelAvailability.js'`. Commit alone, message `test(server): pin the model availability check`.

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

`server/src/clients/checkModelAvailability.ts` reads `status` from the rejection when it is a number (both SDKs' `APIError` carry `status`), classifies 400, 401, 403, and 404 as config and everything else as transient, and logs `{ model, provider, status }` only. `startModelAvailabilityChecks` calls `void checkModelAvailability(deps)`, then `setInterval(..., MODEL.AVAILABILITY.INTERVAL_MS).unref()`, and returns `{ stop: () => clearInterval(timer) }`.

In `startServer.ts`, after the server starts listening and only when `buildModelProvider` returned a provider (not when a test injected one), call `startModelAvailabilityChecks` with one check per configured provider, and call `stop()` inside the returned server's `close`. `buildModelProvider` exports the configured `{ id, model }` list next to the provider so `startServer` builds the checks without re-reading the environment rules.

Run: `cd server && npm test && npm run test:integration && npm run typecheck`
Expected: pass, exit 0; `startServer.integration.test.ts` does not hang on an open interval (the timer is `unref`'d and cleared on close).

### Task 9.8: model smoke script and manual workflow

No behaviour to unit-test: the script calls the real APIs. Its pure part (which prompts it sends and what it reports) reuses the tested prompt builders.

**Files:**

- Create: `server/scripts/modelSmoke.ts`
- Modify: `server/package.json` (`"model:smoke": "tsx scripts/modelSmoke.ts"`; `tsx` is already a root dev dependency)
- Create: `.github/workflows/model-smoke.yml`

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the script**

`server/scripts/modelSmoke.ts` loads the environment with `loadEnv(process.env)` (it needs only the model variables, so it sets `ALLOW_STUBBED_INTEGRATIONS=true` and placeholder `DATABASE_URL` for the parse when they are missing, and never connects to a database), reads three fixed questions from `content/python/easy.json`, `content/postgres/medium.json`, and `content/javascript/hard.json` through `readServerQuestions`, builds one Ask prompt per question with `buildAskPrompt` and one study-note prompt from a fixed synthetic summary with `buildStudyNotePrompt`, and sends all four to each configured provider separately (not through the failover), printing one line per call: provider, model, outcome, latency, and the first 80 characters of the answer. It exits 1 when any call rejects or declines, so a model change that breaks the prompts fails loudly. It accepts `--provider anthropic|openai` to run one.

Pin the actions to the same SHAs as `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. The job skips a provider whose key secret is empty.

```md
## Changing or losing a model

Ask and the study note call `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` (default `claude-haiku-5-5`) first, or `OPENAI_MODEL` first when
`MODEL_PRIMARY=openai`. When both keys are set, a failure on the first provider moves the call to the second.

To switch a model (an upgrade, or a retirement notice from Anthropic or OpenAI):

1. Run `npm run model:smoke -w server` locally with the new id in `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` or `OPENAI_MODEL`, or run the
   "Model smoke" workflow with the id as its input. Every line must say `answered`.
2. Set the variable on the staging Railway service, ask one question in a preview build, and check the
   `model call` log lines show the new id with outcome `answered`.
3. Set it on production.

If a model is retired or a parameter is rejected before you switch, the server logs `model configuration failure`
or `configured model is unavailable` with the provider, model, and status, skips that provider for 15 minutes, and
answers from the other one. With only one key set, Ask and the study note answer 503 until the variable is fixed.
```

### Open questions (area 9)

1. **The OpenAI model.** No default is set; the owner picks one when adding `OPENAI_API_KEY`. The smoke script is the check that it handles the prompts.
2. **Prompt portability.** The Ask and study-note prompts were written for Claude. The fallback sends them unchanged; if the smoke script shows the OpenAI answers drifting in tone or length, a per-provider system-prompt suffix is the smallest fix, and it would be its own task.
3. **The pipeline.** The content pipeline already runs on two vendors (`claude -p` or the API, plus Codex and `PIPELINE_SECOND_MODEL`) and has a run-level provider failure cap (#177). It is a batch tool run by the owner, so it is left out of this area.
4. **One replica.** The breaker is per process, like the rate limiter. With more than one Railway replica each keeps its own breaker, which is acceptable: each replica pays at most one slow request per cooldown.
5. **OpenAI SDK field names.** The plan names the Responses API fields from the SDK's documented shape (`instructions`, `input`, `max_output_tokens`, `reasoning.effort`, `status`, `output[].content[].type`). Task 9.3 makes the installed package's types the authority, with one `DISPUTE` if any differ.

## Cross-area decisions made while writing this plan

These settle the places where one area's draft assumed something about another. The spec's "Resolved questions" records the product-level ones.

1. **Admin access shape.** Today's `{ grantSource, isGranted, productId }` stays on the server (Task 3.6) and in the app (Task 4.11); `GET` reports any active store purchase of either Pro product as `'purchase'`.
2. **The 429 limit.** Inside the standard error envelope as `error.limit` (Tasks 3.8 and 4.9).
3. **Play base-plan suffixes.** Stripped by the same rule on both sides (Tasks 3.1 and 4.4).
4. **An annual grant without an expiry.** Recorded, ignored for status and expiry, logged; an annual `CANCELLATION` without an expiry cannot set a NULL expiry either (Task 3.4).
5. **"On first use".** Opening a track's difficulty step downloads that track's Medium and Hard banks, which is what `useQuestionBank` already does for each option it renders; the background refresh never downloads a bank the device does not have (Tasks 2.5 and 2.6). Roughly 400 KB per visited track instead of 4 MB on first launch.
6. **Areas 1 and 2 on one branch.** The schema change breaks other workspaces until area 2 lands (header, "The areas").
7. **The content build's misconceptions.** With every bank in `content/`, the build ships exactly the approved taxonomy entries a card links, and stops carrying over entries for banks it could not read. This follows from the move, not a separate change (Task 1.3).
8. **Static pages need content.** Area 5 leaves `ContentProvider` alone; area 7 opens with Task 7.1, which renders the bundled content before storage is read. A track that exists only in a newer cached manifest shows "not found" for the moment before the cache is read; accepted as rare.
9. **Sample AdMob ids.** Allowed in development and preview builds so the SDK starts; refused in a production build (Task 6.13).
10. **Review rounds and the sponsor cadence.** They count toward the round counter but never show a card (Task 6.5).
11. **Model failover scope.** Server only. The content pipeline already runs on two vendors with a run-level failure cap and is owner-run (Task 9.9 note, area 9 open questions).

Each area lists its own at its end, with the assumption it made. The ones most likely to need a `DISPUTE` or a device check:

- The exact page file names `expo export` writes under static output, including the not-found page (area 5; Task 5.6 checks them).
